sec01-card-sec01-F035.question_text: Is the Rhode Island driver's handbook considered an official legal statute document itself?
sec01-card-sec01-F035.teaching_text: Exam questions test whether you know the manual explains laws in plain language rather than replacing enacted state statutes.

sec01-card-sec01-F036.question_text: Where should you look to verify recent changes in Rhode Island driving laws, procedures, or fees?
sec01-card-sec01-F036.teaching_text: Printed handbooks can lag behind new legislation, so checking the motor vehicle agency or state legislature online gives current rules.

sec01-card-sec01-F037.question_text: What kind of behind-the-wheel experience are new permit holders encouraged to build?
sec01-card-sec01-F037.teaching_text: Logging plenty of coached miles across different weather, traffic, and road types turns textbook knowledge into calm muscle memory.

sec01-card-sec01-F038.question_text: What seat belt habit defines a responsible driver before shifting out of park?
sec01-card-sec01-F038.teaching_text: Unbelted riders can be thrown into other occupants during a collision, so responsible drivers make everyone click in first.

sec01-card-sec01-F039.question_text: Besides typing out texts, what other electronic message habit must you avoid while driving?
sec01-card-sec01-F039.teaching_text: Drivers often rationalize just reading an incoming text, yet reading steals your visual focus from traffic just like typing.

sec01-card-sec01-F040.question_text: How should drivers treat pedestrians and fellow motorists using public streets?
sec01-card-sec01-F040.teaching_text: Patience and courtesy at crosswalks and merges defuse road rage and protect vulnerable walkers who have zero metal armor.

sec01-card-sec01-F041.question_text: Whose safety is a driver held accountable for on every trip?
sec01-card-sec01-F041.teaching_text: Every choice you make with speed, space, and attention affects everyone inside your cabin and everyone sharing the street.

sec01-card-sec01-F042.question_text: While studying the manual prepares you for the knowledge test, what builds lasting safe driving habits?
sec01-card-sec01-F042.teaching_text: Passing a written quiz proves you know the rules, whereas consistent daily discipline behind the wheel keeps you crash-free.

sec02-card-sec02-F001.question_text: Which age group follows Rhode Island's three-stage graduated licensing path from instructional permit to provisional and full operator license?
sec02-card-sec02-F001.teaching_text: Phasing in driving privileges step by step gives teen beginners supervised practice before tackling solo nighttime or group trips.

sec02-card-sec02-F002.question_text: What two requirements must an applicant aged sixteen to eighteen finish before receiving a limited learner permit?
sec02-card-sec02-F002.teaching_text: Skipping accredited classroom hours blocks teen applicants at the counter even if they feel ready to pass the computer test.

sec02-card-sec02-F003.question_text: How do permit requirements change once an applicant is older than eighteen?
sec02-card-sec02-F003.teaching_text: Adult learners still prove road-rule mastery on the computerized knowledge test without sitting through the teen classroom course.

sec02-card-sec02-F004.question_text: What is the earliest age at which Rhode Island will issue a limited learner permit?
sec02-card-sec02-F004.teaching_text: Even if you finish classroom driver education early, you cannot hold a limited learner permit before your sixteenth birthday.

sec02-card-sec02-F005.question_text: How old must a student be on the first day of class to start driver education before turning sixteen?
sec02-card-sec02-F005.teaching_text: Starting the course two months before your sixteenth birthday lets you wrap up classroom hours right on schedule for permit day.

sec02-card-sec02-F006.question_text: Why must you bring original identity and age documents rather than photocopies to your first driver-education class?
sec02-card-sec02-F006.teaching_text: Showing up on day one with paper copies or phone photos of your birth certificate can get you turned away.

sec02-card-sec02-F007.question_text: What topics in the handbook should you prioritize when preparing for the knowledge test?
sec02-card-sec02-F007.teaching_text: Focusing your study time on traffic statutes, signs, and safe right-of-way rules matches what the computerized test actually grades.

sec02-card-sec02-F008.question_text: What does a limited instructional permit grant to a learner under eighteen who passes the knowledge exam?
sec02-card-sec02-F008.teaching_text: Passing the computer test unlocks supervised practice behind the wheel rather than unrestricted solo driving privileges.

sec02-card-sec02-F009.question_text: What form of identity documentation is required when applying for a limited learner permit?
sec02-card-sec02-F009.teaching_text: Counter staff verify authentic security features on original records and automatically reject photocopied identity papers.

sec02-card-sec02-F010.question_text: What education proof must a permit applicant under eighteen submit at the licensing counter?
sec02-card-sec02-F010.teaching_text: Your completion proof shows the agency you finished every required classroom hour before sitting for your learner permit.

sec02-card-sec02-F011.question_text: How many documents proving Rhode Island residency are required on a permit application?
sec02-card-sec02-F011.teaching_text: Bringing only a single piece of mail forces a wasted trip home, so pack two qualifying residency proofs.

sec02-card-sec02-F012.question_text: What payment requirement accompanies every learner permit application?
sec02-card-sec02-F012.teaching_text: Your permit paperwork cannot be processed and issued until the required state fee is paid at application time.

sec02-card-sec02-F013.question_text: Which check type is refused when paying permit fees, even though cash, credit cards, money orders, and accepted checks work?
sec02-card-sec02-F013.teaching_text: Cash, cards, money orders, and standard personal checks clear fine, whereas a check signed over from someone else gets rejected.

sec02-card-sec02-F014.question_text: Which four qualifying adults generally accompany a minor who is applying for a permit?
sec02-card-sec02-F014.teaching_text: Minors need a legally recognized adult present to verify consent and accept responsibility on the permit application.

sec02-card-sec02-F015.question_text: What extra authority papers must a legal guardian or licensed foster parent bring to a minor's permit appointment?
sec02-card-sec02-F015.teaching_text: Agency staff must verify legal custody authority through official court guardianship orders or state child-services placement records.

sec02-card-sec02-F016.question_text: What can a parent without a valid Rhode Island driver license do on a minor's permit application, and what can they not do?
sec02-card-sec02-F016.teaching_text: Parental authority lets an unlicensed parent sign the form, yet coaching from the front passenger seat requires a qualified license.

sec02-card-sec02-F017.question_text: Where must a parent ride during practice drives if that parent does not qualify as a supervising driver?
sec02-card-sec02-F017.teaching_text: The right front seat is strictly reserved for the qualified supervising driver who can legally step in during emergencies.

sec02-card-sec02-F018.question_text: What minimum age and licensing history must a driver have to supervise a learner under the detailed handbook rule?
sec02-card-sec02-F018.teaching_text: Test questions pair both numbers together, ensuring your front-seat coach has mature judgment and half a decade of driving experience.

sec02-card-sec02-F019.question_text: How can a permit applicant satisfy Rhode Island's vision check requirement?
sec02-card-sec02-F019.teaching_text: You can either read the eye chart at the counter or submit a signed vision card from an optometrist or ophthalmologist.

sec02-card-sec02-F020.question_text: What must applicants do during vision screening if they rely on glasses or contacts for distance sight?
sec02-card-sec02-F020.teaching_text: Testing with your distance glasses or contacts proves your eyes meet safe road acuity and records the proper lens restriction.

sec02-card-sec02-F021.question_text: What corrected visual-acuity score does the Rhode Island handbook require for licensing?
sec02-card-sec02-F021.teaching_text: Sharp distance vision lets you read highway signs, spot brake lights, and judge intersection gaps early enough to react.

sec02-card-sec02-F022.question_text: What adult endorsement is mandatory on a minor's permit or license application?
sec02-card-sec02-F022.teaching_text: State law bars minors from self-signing licensing paperwork without verified consent from an eligible responsible adult.

sec02-card-sec02-F023.question_text: Who may sign a minor's application if no qualifying parent, guardian, or licensed foster parent is available?
sec02-card-sec02-F023.teaching_text: Another responsible adult can step in so a teen is not blocked from licensing, provided they formally accept legal liability.

sec02-card-sec02-F024.question_text: What must the qualifying supervisor do while a learner is practicing behind the wheel?
sec02-card-sec02-F024.teaching_text: A supervisor scrolling a phone or napping cannot spot developing hazards or grab control if a learner freezes.

sec02-card-sec02-F025.question_text: Who carries legal responsibility if a learner commits a driving violation during supervised practice?
sec02-card-sec02-F025.teaching_text: Because the licensed coach oversees every maneuver from the front seat, traffic law places responsibility for learner violations on that supervisor.

sec02-card-sec02-F026.question_text: Under what single exception may a learner drive without wearing a safety belt?
sec02-card-sec02-F026.teaching_text: Unless a doctor's written medical exemption has been supplied to the motor vehicle agency, every learner must buckle up.

sec02-card-sec02-F027.question_text: What restraint rule applies to every passenger riding in a car driven by a learner?
sec02-card-sec02-F027.teaching_text: No matter which row they sit in, every adult and child riding with a permit holder must use lawful restraints.

sec02-card-sec02-F028.question_text: Why should a learner practice on different road types and in varied weather or lighting conditions?
sec02-card-sec02-F028.teaching_text: Driving only sunny neighborhood loops hides steering, spacing, or speed mistakes that surface on highways, hills, and wet pavement.

sec02-card-sec02-F029.question_text: How long must a learner hold an instructional permit before taking the driving-skills road test?
sec02-card-sec02-F029.teaching_text: Six full months of supervised seasons and traffic ensures teens build real judgment rather than cramming practice into one weekend.

sec02-card-sec02-F030.question_text: How long does a limited learner permit remain valid, and how many renewals are allowed under the validity paragraph?
sec02-card-sec02-F030.teaching_text: Knowing both the eighteenth-birthday cutoff and the two-renewal ceiling keeps teen learners from losing permit continuity.

sec02-card-sec02-F031.question_text: When does an expired limited learner permit become ineligible for renewal?
sec02-card-sec02-F031.teaching_text: Letting an expired permit sit past the two-year mark wipes out renewal eligibility and forces you to restart.

sec02-card-sec02-F032.question_text: What option opens up if you turn eighteen before holding your limited learner permit for a full year?
sec02-card-sec02-F032.teaching_text: Reaching adulthood lets you transition from the teen limited permit track onto an adult full learner permit.

sec02-card-sec02-F033.question_text: How many months with a limited learner permit are required to qualify for a provisional license?
sec02-card-sec02-F033.teaching_text: You cannot jump from limited permit to provisional license until you clear the mandatory six-month supervised holding window.

sec02-card-sec02-F034.question_text: What violation record is required during the six months right before applying for a provisional license?
sec02-card-sec02-F034.teaching_text: Even a single seat-belt or moving ticket resets your clean six-month streak and delays your provisional upgrade.

sec02-card-sec02-F035.question_text: Which practical evaluation must a provisional-license applicant pass at the motor vehicle agency?
sec02-card-sec02-F035.teaching_text: Logged hours and clean months open the door, while passing the behind-the-wheel test proves you control the car safely.

sec02-card-sec02-F036.question_text: How many total and nighttime supervised practice hours must a parent or guardian certify for provisional licensing?
sec02-card-sec02-F036.teaching_text: Nighttime glare and depth-perception traps challenge beginners, so ten of your fifty certified hours must happen after dark.

sec02-card-sec02-F037.question_text: What must an applicant do if they do not pass the driving-skills test?
sec02-card-sec02-F037.teaching_text: A failed road test grants zero provisional privileges, meaning you continue supervised practice and book a new test date.

sec02-card-sec02-F038.question_text: How does road-test eligibility differ between first-time license applicants and holders of a valid out-of-state license?
sec02-card-sec02-F038.teaching_text: New drivers must demonstrate behind-the-wheel skills, whereas newcomers holding a valid license from another state already proved road competence.

sec02-card-sec02-F039.question_text: Why does the handbook advise driving a vehicle whose controls you already know well?
sec02-card-sec02-F039.teaching_text: Fumbling around an unfamiliar dashboard takes your eyes off traffic right when sudden rain, fog, or hazards demand focus.

sec02-card-sec02-F040.question_text: Which two vehicle controls must you know how to work before heading out in rainy weather?
sec02-card-sec02-F040.teaching_text: Sudden downpours cut visibility fast, and Rhode Island drivers need clear glass plus lit headlights so surrounding cars spot them.

sec02-card-sec02-F041.question_text: How well should you know the spot of your vehicle's hazard-light switch?
sec02-card-sec02-F041.teaching_text: During a roadside breakdown or sudden highway slowdown, you need four-way flashers blinking immediately without asking a passenger where to press.

sec02-card-sec02-F042.question_text: After passing the road test, by what deadline must you pick up your limited provisional license?
sec02-card-sec02-F042.teaching_text: Passing the skills test is not your license credential itself, so visit the agency before your underlying permit expires.

sec02-card-sec02-F043.question_text: When can a teen under eighteen collect a provisional license without the accompanying adult present in person?
sec02-card-sec02-F043.teaching_text: Getting the parent or guardian signature notarized ahead of time saves that adult from attending the license pickup counter.

sec02-card-sec02-F044.question_text: Who can stand in at provisional licensing when no qualifying parent, guardian, foster parent, or adult spouse is available?
sec02-card-sec02-F044.teaching_text: Law allows another responsible adult to sign and assume legal obligation so teens without listed family signers can progress.

sec02-card-sec02-F045.question_text: How many days must you wait after failing a driving-skills test before taking your next road test?
sec02-card-sec02-F045.teaching_text: That mandatory thirty-day cooling-off window pushes learners to fix weak maneuvers through real practice rather than guessing tomorrow.

sec02-card-sec02-F046.question_text: What can happen if a second permit expiration hits before you secure another road-test appointment?
sec02-card-sec02-F046.teaching_text: Running out the clock on a second permit expiration can send you back to square one for another written test.

sec02-card-sec02-F047.question_text: When may a provisional license holder drive if a qualifying supervising driver is sitting right beside them?
sec02-card-sec02-F047.teaching_text: Nighttime curfews restrict solo teen trips, whereas having a qualified front-seat coach unlocks legal driving around the clock.

sec02-card-sec02-F048.question_text: During what daily hours may a provisional license holder generally drive without supervision?
sec02-card-sec02-F048.teaching_text: Late-night crash rates spike between one and five in the morning, so Rhode Island closes solo provisional driving during those hours.

sec02-card-sec02-F049.question_text: May a provisional driver drive solo during late-night curfew hours for employment?
sec02-card-sec02-F049.teaching_text: Teens working early bakery shifts or late restaurant closings may commute directly between home and work without supervision.
sec02-card-sec02-F049.must_match_memory_hook: Yes, going to or from work

visual_sync.text_span: Yes, going to or from work

sec02-card-sec02-F050.question_text: What curfew exception applies to a provisional driver serving in a volunteer fire, rescue, or emergency-medical unit?
sec02-card-sec02-F050.teaching_text: Emergency calls and drills happen at any hour, so active youth volunteers may drive solo to and from organization duties.

sec02-card-sec02-F051.question_text: Under what conditions may a provisional driver travel solo between four and five in the morning for school sports?
sec02-card-sec02-F051.teaching_text: Early morning hockey or swim practices qualify between four and five only when the school provides zero bus transportation.

sec02-card-sec02-F052.question_text: Who must wear safety belts or child restraints inside a vehicle driven by a provisional license holder?
sec02-card-sec02-F052.teaching_text: Whether a parent is coaching beside you or you are driving alone, every single person inside the cabin must buckle.

sec02-card-sec02-F053.question_text: At what birthday does the learner provisional license expire?
sec02-card-sec02-F053.teaching_text: Mark your eighteenth birthday on the calendar so you upgrade to a full operator license instead of driving expired.

sec02-card-sec02-F054.question_text: How many passengers under twenty-one may ride with a provisional driver during the first twelve months, and who is exempt?
sec02-card-sec02-F054.teaching_text: Packing a car with peer friends multiplies teen crash risk, so law caps young non-household riders at one.

sec02-card-sec02-F055.question_text: What is the minimum age required to obtain a Rhode Island full operator license?
sec02-card-sec02-F055.teaching_text: Even if you earned your permit on your sixteenth birthday, full operator eligibility starts at seventeen and a half.

sec02-card-sec02-F056.question_text: How many months must you hold a limited provisional license before upgrading to a full operator license?
sec02-card-sec02-F056.teaching_text: Completing a full year on provisional restrictions proves you can handle solo daytime and evening driving responsibly.

sec02-card-sec02-F057.question_text: What restrictions disappear with a full operator license, and what rules still apply?
sec02-card-sec02-F057.teaching_text: Curfews and supervision rules lift at full licensing, while speed limits, seat-belt laws, and sober-driving statutes apply forever.
sec02-card-sec02-F057.must_match_memory_hook: Graduated limits end, traffic laws stay

visual_sync.text_span: Graduated limits end, traffic laws stay

sec02-card-sec02-F058.question_text: What conviction record must a provisional holder maintain during the six months preceding a full operator upgrade?
sec02-card-sec02-F058.teaching_text: Just like moving from permit to provisional, earning full operator privileges requires six straight months free of moving or belt convictions.

sec02-card-sec02-F059.question_text: If your license is suspended, what may you still use the physical card for, and what is strictly forbidden?
sec02-card-sec02-F059.teaching_text: Keeping the plastic card in your wallet for identification never means your legal right to drive is still active.

sec02-card-sec02-F060.question_text: Can you legally drive in another state while your Rhode Island license is suspended?
sec02-card-sec02-F060.teaching_text: Crossing a state border never restores suspended driving privileges, so driving anywhere during suspension is illegal.

sec02-card-sec02-F061.question_text: What three situations listed in the handbook can trigger a Rhode Island license suspension?
sec02-card-sec02-F061.teaching_text: Ignoring a traffic fine or picking up a suspension notice from another state can pause your license just like serious offenses.

sec02-card-sec02-F062.question_text: Why can recorded motor vehicle violations cause your auto insurance premiums to climb?
sec02-card-sec02-F062.teaching_text: Traffic convictions sit on public driving records that insurance companies review when pricing your crash risk.

sec02-card-sec02-F063.question_text: When must a learner have the physical instructional permit with them?
sec02-card-sec02-F063.teaching_text: Leaving your permit on the kitchen counter means you cannot prove valid preliminary driving authority during a traffic stop.

sec02-card-sec02-F064.question_text: Who is the only person allowed in the front passenger seat beside a limited learner permit holder?
sec02-card-sec02-F064.teaching_text: Friends or siblings must sit in the back so the qualified coach has unobstructed access to the front controls.

sec02-card-sec02-F065.question_text: What document must a provisional driver keep in their possession every time they drive?
sec02-card-sec02-F065.teaching_text: Just like any operator credential, your provisional license must physically ride with you whenever you take the wheel.

sec02-card-sec02-F066.question_text: How do graduated-license passenger caps apply once a driver holds a full operator license?
sec02-card-sec02-F066.teaching_text: Reaching full operator status removes the teen peer-passenger cap, though every rider still needs an available seat belt.

sec02-card-sec02-F067.question_text: What must you do before applying for a Rhode Island license if your license is suspended in another state?
sec02-card-sec02-F067.teaching_text: States share driver records electronically, so Rhode Island blocks new applications until prior-state holds are cleared.

sec02-card-sec02-F068.question_text: How long can an out-of-state license be expired and still transfer to Rhode Island without taking knowledge or skills tests?
sec02-card-sec02-F068.teaching_text: New residents transferring an active license or one expired within five years skip retesting once paperwork checks out.

sec02-card-sec02-F069.question_text: When is a returning former Rhode Island license holder exempt from retaking the knowledge and driving-skills tests?
sec02-card-sec02-F069.teaching_text: Former Rhode Island drivers whose credentials lapsed no more than five years ago enjoy the same test waiver.

sec02-card-sec02-F070.question_text: What happens to existing restrictions and endorsements when transferring an out-of-state license to Rhode Island?
sec02-card-sec02-F070.teaching_text: Corrective-lens restrictions or special endorsements carry straight across onto your new Rhode Island credential.

sec02-card-sec02-F071.question_text: What four items are required when transferring an out-of-state license to Rhode Island?
sec02-card-sec02-F071.teaching_text: You cannot hold two state driver licenses at once, so bring your application, identity and residency proofs, and surrender the old card.

sec04-card-sec04-F001.question_text: What should you inspect around your vehicle before stepping inside?
sec04-card-sec04-F001.teaching_text: Small children, pets, or toys crouched near bumpers stay hidden below window height once you sit in the driver's seat.

sec04-card-sec04-F002.question_text: What two door and ignition steps come right before starting the engine?
sec04-card-sec04-F002.teaching_text: Locking cabin doors first secures everyone inside and helps keep doors latched shut during an unexpected impact.
sec04-card-sec04-F002.must_match_memory_hook: Lock doors, position key or fob

visual_sync.text_span: Lock doors, position key or fob

sec04-card-sec04-F003.question_text: Which three visibility and cabin adjustments should be finished before starting your trip?
sec04-card-sec04-F003.teaching_text: Dialing in your seating posture, mirror angles, and airflow while parked prevents awkward reaches once traffic starts moving.

sec04-card-sec04-F004.question_text: What seat-belt steps must happen before you pull out to drive?
sec04-card-sec04-F004.teaching_text: Fitting your own belt snugly and confirming every passenger clicks in keeps everyone anchored before wheels roll.

sec04-card-sec04-F005.question_text: Which four driver-position and dash items should you adjust before moving the vehicle?
sec04-card-sec04-F005.teaching_text: Proper head restraint height guards against whiplash while comfortable wheel, pedal, and audio setup keeps control effortless.

sec04-card-sec04-F006.question_text: What does Rhode Island's primary seat-belt law allow police to do if someone inside your vehicle is unbuckled?
sec04-card-sec04-F006.teaching_text: Primary enforcement means an officer needs zero other speeding or equipment violation to initiate a seat-belt traffic stop.

sec04-card-sec04-F007.question_text: Which seats are covered by the driver's duty to ensure adult passengers buckle up?
sec04-card-sec04-F007.teaching_text: Back-seat adults do not get a pass in Rhode Island, because unbelted rear riders slam forward during crashes.

sec04-card-sec04-F008.question_text: What restraint requirement applies directly to the vehicle operator while driving?
sec04-card-sec04-F008.teaching_text: Staying strapped into your seat keeps you behind the wheel and able to steer through secondary crash impacts.

sec04-card-sec04-F009.question_text: What safety-belt fine amount does the handbook list for each unrestrained occupant?
sec04-card-sec04-F009.teaching_text: Because the forty-dollar penalty applies per unrestrained person, multiple unbuckled riders multiply ticket costs fast.

sec04-card-sec04-F010.question_text: Under what three combined age, height, and weight thresholds must a child ride in an approved rear-seat child restraint?
sec04-card-sec04-F010.teaching_text: Memorize all three benchmarks together so small children stay protected in a rear car seat or booster.

sec04-card-sec04-F011.question_text: What restraint may a child under eight use in the rear seat once reaching fifty-seven inches tall or eighty pounds?
sec04-card-sec04-F011.teaching_text: Hitting either the fifty-seven-inch height mark or eighty-pound weight mark lets a child under eight use a rear seat belt.

sec04-card-sec04-F012.question_text: What restraint rule applies to passengers aged eight up to their eighteenth birthday?
sec04-card-sec04-F012.teaching_text: Older kids and teens from eight to eighteen must wear the safety belt or shoulder harness regardless of seating row.

sec04-card-sec04-F013.question_text: What restraint requirement applies specifically to drivers younger than eighteen?
sec04-card-sec04-F013.teaching_text: Not only does a belt protect you in a wreck, a seat-belt conviction also stalls graduated-license upgrades.

sec04-card-sec04-F014.question_text: Under what two vehicle situations is a child younger than eight exempt from riding in the rear seat?
sec04-card-sec04-F014.teaching_text: Two-seat pickups have zero back row, and families with every rear spot already filled by children need a legal front option.

sec04-card-sec04-F015.question_text: Which child should ride up front when a rear-seat exception applies and a passenger airbag is present?
sec04-card-sec04-F015.teaching_text: Larger, older children sit taller and farther back from forceful front airbag deployment than toddlers or infants.

sec04-card-sec04-F016.question_text: What legal step is mandatory if you are cited for transporting a child without the required child restraint?
sec04-card-sec04-F016.teaching_text: Unlike a mail-in parking ticket, skipping required child safety restraints triggers a compulsory court appearance before a judge.

sec04-card-sec04-F017.question_text: According to the child-restraint table, which children must stay in a rear-facing car seat?
sec04-card-sec04-F017.teaching_text: Rear-facing shells cradle fragile infant necks and spines during sudden frontal crash forces.

sec04-card-sec04-F018.question_text: How long does the handbook urge keeping children rear-facing, and at what age does forward-facing convertible seating start?
sec04-card-sec04-F018.teaching_text: Riding rear-facing as long as seat limits allow maximizes neck protection before switching forward at age two or older.

sec04-card-sec04-F019.question_text: Where across your body should the lap belt and shoulder belt rest for safe protection?
sec04-card-sec04-F019.teaching_text: Strong pelvic bones and the sternum absorb crash forces safely, whereas a high belly belt risks internal injury.

sec04-card-sec04-F020.question_text: What posture check at the vehicle cushion tests whether a child is ready to graduate out of a booster seat?
sec04-card-sec04-F020.teaching_text: If a child's legs are too short to bend naturally at the seat edge, they slouch and slide the belt onto their stomach.

sec04-card-sec04-F021.question_text: Where must the shoulder and lap straps sit on a child to pass the adult seat-belt fit check?
sec04-card-sec04-F021.teaching_text: Straps cutting across the neck or riding over soft stomach tissue mean the child still needs booster elevation.

sec04-card-sec04-F022.question_text: How long must a child hold proper belt-fitting posture to pass the seat-belt fit check?
sec04-card-sec04-F022.teaching_text: Sitting tall for ten seconds in the driveway means nothing if the child squirms or tucks the strap mid-drive.

sec04-card-sec04-F023.question_text: What must you use if a child misses even one step of the adult seat-belt fit check?
sec04-card-sec04-F023.teaching_text: Missing any single fit criterion shows the adult belt geometry still cannot protect that child's body safely alone.

sec04-card-sec04-F024.question_text: What type of vehicle belt system is required whenever securing a child on a booster seat?
sec04-card-sec04-F024.teaching_text: A lap-only strap cannot restrain a child's upper torso on a booster, so always pair boosters with full lap-shoulder belts.

sec04-card-sec04-F025.question_text: Which seating row does the handbook name as safer for protecting children from airbag force?
sec04-card-sec04-F025.teaching_text: Front airbags inflate at explosive speed scaled for adult bodies, making the back row the safest zone for kids.

sec04-card-sec04-F026.question_text: What three sequential driver actions are required to bring a moving vehicle to a stop?
sec04-card-sec04-F026.teaching_text: Brakes never work instantaneously because human eyes and brains must spot the threat and command your foot first.

sec04-card-sec04-F027.question_text: What does perception distance measure during an emergency stop?
sec04-card-sec04-F027.teaching_text: Your car keeps rolling at full speed during the split second your brain realizes brake lights ahead mean danger.

sec04-card-sec04-F028.question_text: What does reaction distance measure once you recognize a roadway hazard?
sec04-card-sec04-F028.teaching_text: Lifting your right foot off the accelerator and pivoting onto the brake pedal eats up extra yards before pads touch rotors.

sec04-card-sec04-F029.question_text: Where does braking distance begin and end?
sec04-card-sec04-F029.teaching_text: Once your foot presses the pedal, tire grip, vehicle weight, speed, and road surface determine how far you slide or roll.

sec04-card-sec04-F030.question_text: Which three distances add together to form total stopping distance?
sec04-card-sec04-F030.teaching_text: Forgetting perception and reaction distances tricks drivers into tailgating inside space that disappears before brakes even engage.

sec04-card-sec04-F031.question_text: Roughly how long does the average alert driver take to press the brake after seeing danger?
sec04-card-sec04-F031.teaching_text: Even an alert three-quarter-second reaction covers over sixty feet at highway speed before slowing begins.

sec04-card-sec04-F032.question_text: How does higher travel speed affect the ground your vehicle covers before brakes are even applied?
sec04-card-sec04-F032.teaching_text: Because reaction time stays roughly fixed, going faster stretches out the pre-braking distance your car travels untouched.

sec04-card-sec04-F033.question_text: How do wet or icy roads change tire grip and stopping distance, and what must you do?
sec04-card-sec04-F033.teaching_text: Water and ice slash friction between rubber and asphalt, making lower speed the only way to keep stopping room manageable.

sec04-card-sec04-F034.question_text: Why are pavements often slickest right as rainfall begins?
sec04-card-sec04-F034.teaching_text: Initial raindrops float accumulated motor oil, tire dust, and road grime into a greasy film before heavy rain washes it off.

sec04-card-sec04-F035.question_text: What sensory illusion does the handbook call velocitizing?
sec04-card-sec04-F035.teaching_text: Cruising fast for miles numbs your sense of motion so forty miles per hour suddenly feels like a crawl.

sec04-card-sec04-F036.question_text: Why must you take extra care to slow down when leaving a highway onto an exit ramp?
sec04-card-sec04-F036.teaching_text: Highway speed adaptation tricks drivers into entering tight curved ramps way too hot unless they check the speedometer.

sec04-card-sec04-F037.question_text: What happens to your front tires and steering when a vehicle hydroplanes?
sec04-card-sec04-F037.teaching_text: When water wedges underneath tread faster than grooves channel it away, front wheels skim like water skis without steering grip.

sec04-card-sec04-F038.question_text: What three practical steps lower your risk of hydroplaning in rainy weather?
sec04-card-sec04-F038.teaching_text: Slower speed, manufacturer-recommended tire inflation, and steering clear of standing water help tire treads stay planted on asphalt.
sec04-card-sec04-F038.must_match_memory_hook: Slow down, proper pressure, skip puddles

visual_sync.text_span: Slow down, proper pressure, skip puddles

sec04-card-sec04-F039.question_text: How should you warn traffic behind you and adjust speed when approaching a left turn?
sec04-card-sec04-F039.teaching_text: Early turn signals and smooth deceleration give following cars time to adjust instead of slamming brakes behind you.

sec04-card-sec04-F040.question_text: What rear-traffic danger should you verify is clear right before turning left?
sec04-card-sec04-F040.teaching_text: On two-lane roads or driveways, an impatient follower already overtaking on your left will T-bone your turning car.

sec04-card-sec04-F041.question_text: What should you do if you are stuck in a right-hand lane when you realize you wanted to turn left?
sec04-card-sec04-F041.teaching_text: Lunging left across active lanes causes side-impact wrecks, whereas looping at the next block costs less than a minute.
sec04-card-sec04-F041.must_match_memory_hook: Never cut across, use next intersection

visual_sync.text_span: Never cut across, use next intersection

sec04-card-sec04-F042.question_text: How must your front wheels be aimed while paused waiting for a safe left-turn gap?
sec04-card-sec04-F042.teaching_text: Pre-turning your wheels left means a rear-end bump shoves your car straight into oncoming head-on traffic.

sec04-card-sec04-F043.question_text: Which vehicle streams must you yield to when preparing a left turn?
sec04-card-sec04-F043.teaching_text: Turning left crosses opposing paths, so oncoming straight cars and vehicles approaching from the right go ahead of you.

sec04-card-sec04-F044.question_text: What obligation do left-turning drivers owe to pedestrians?
sec04-card-sec04-F044.teaching_text: Drivers scanning hard for oncoming car gaps often overlook walkers already crossing the side street they are turning into.

sec04-card-sec04-F045.question_text: What signal check should follow every completed turn?
sec04-card-sec04-F045.teaching_text: Gentle turns sometimes fail to auto-cancel the blinker, confusing other drivers into pulling out right in front of you.

sec04-card-sec04-F046.question_text: From what roadway position and with what warning should you start a right turn?
sec04-card-sec04-F046.teaching_text: Positioning snugly near the right curb with your right blinker prevents cyclists or cars from squeezing inside your turn.

sec04-card-sec04-F047.question_text: Why must you avoid swinging left before making a right turn?
sec04-card-sec04-F047.teaching_text: Veering left fools following drivers into thinking you are turning left and tempts them to pass on your right.

sec04-card-sec04-F048.question_text: Who gets the right-of-way before you complete a right turn?
sec04-card-sec04-F048.teaching_text: Wait until cross traffic clears and every pedestrian in the street safely finishes crossing your path.

sec04-card-sec04-F049.question_text: When should you plan your turning arc and shed speed for a corner?
sec04-card-sec04-F049.teaching_text: Braking in a straight line before turning keeps tire grip balanced instead of skidding mid-corner.

sec04-card-sec04-F050.question_text: How should you manage the brake and accelerator from early turn entry to exit?
sec04-card-sec04-F050.teaching_text: Staying poised to brake early handles hidden crosswalk surprises before gentle throttle straightens the car smoothly.

sec04-card-sec04-F051.question_text: What is the purpose of a turnabout maneuver?
sec04-card-sec04-F051.teaching_text: Turnabouts flip your heading one hundred eighty degrees so you can head back along the same road.

sec04-card-sec04-F052.question_text: What regulatory checks come first before attempting any turnabout?
sec04-card-sec04-F052.teaching_text: Many busy streets and town centers ban U-turns or mid-block reversals by sign or local ordinance.

sec04-card-sec04-F053.question_text: How much clear sight distance and intersection clearance does the handbook's turnabout checklist require?
sec04-card-sec04-F053.teaching_text: Exam questions love pairing five hundred feet of two-way visibility with two hundred feet away from any intersection.
sec04-card-sec04-F053.must_match_memory_hook: Five hundred sight, two hundred corner

visual_sync.text_span: Five hundred sight, two hundred corner

sec04-card-sec04-F054.question_text: Which roadway conditions make a spot unsafe for a turnabout?
sec04-card-sec04-F054.teaching_text: Blind crests, curves, heavy traffic, cramped pavement, or nearby pedestrians leave zero safe margin to swing across lanes.

sec04-card-sec04-F055.question_text: Under what two conditions is a U-turn lawful?
sec04-card-sec04-F055.teaching_text: Even without a no-U-turn sign, forcing oncoming or following cars to brake makes your U-turn unlawful.

sec04-card-sec04-F056.question_text: Where do you position and what do you check right before starting a U-turn?
sec04-card-sec04-F056.teaching_text: Pulling to the right curb first maximizes turning width and lets you scan both directions from a full stop.

sec04-card-sec04-F057.question_text: Which lights warn drivers as you start a U-turn, and what do you do afterward?
sec04-card-sec04-F057.teaching_text: Flashing your left signal or four-way hazards alerts traffic to your wide arc, and canceling afterward restores normal cues.

sec04-card-sec04-F058.question_text: Why does the handbook favor backing into a driveway or side street on the right for a turnabout?
sec04-card-sec04-F058.teaching_text: Driving nose-first back onto the main street gives you clear windshield sightlines instead of backing blind across lanes.

sec04-card-sec04-F059.question_text: What three steps prepare you to back into a driveway on the right?
sec04-card-sec04-F059.teaching_text: Stopping just past the apron while signaling and scanning ensures pedestrians and following cars clear your reverse path.

sec04-card-sec04-F060.question_text: Once backed completely past the curb line into a right-side driveway, how do you re-enter the road?
sec04-card-sec04-F060.teaching_text: Clearing the curb line fully, stopping, scanning both ways, and signaling lets you pull out cleanly in the new direction.

sec04-card-sec04-F061.question_text: Why is pulling nose-first into a left-side driveway riskier as a turnabout?
sec04-card-sec04-F061.teaching_text: Reversing tail-first out into moving lanes exposes your rear blind zones to fast cross traffic.

sec04-card-sec04-F062.question_text: During a left-driveway turnabout, where do you stop and what do you scan before shifting to reverse?
sec04-card-sec04-F062.teaching_text: Getting your rear bumper fully clear of the street first lets you pause safely and check sidewalks and lanes.

sec04-card-sec04-F063.question_text: Which way do you steer while backing out of a left-side driveway, and when do you straighten the wheel?
sec04-card-sec04-F063.teaching_text: Turning the wheel right swings your rear toward the far lane, and straightening mid-arc lines you up neatly.

sec04-card-sec04-F064.question_text: Which turnabout works when a street is too narrow for a U-turn and has no open driveways?
sec04-card-sec04-F064.teaching_text: Where legal, alternating forward-left, reverse-right, and forward-left turns your car around inside tight curbs.

sec04-card-sec04-F065.question_text: How do you set up at the curb before starting the first leg of a three-point turn?
sec04-card-sec04-F065.teaching_text: Starting stopped against the right edge with proper signals gives you every inch of street width for leg one.

sec04-card-sec04-F066.question_text: How do you execute the first movement of a three-point turn?
sec04-card-sec04-F066.teaching_text: Scanning both directions, cranking the wheel sharply left, and stopping short of the far curb protects tires and suspension.

sec04-card-sec04-F067.question_text: How far back and with what steering angle do you reverse on the second movement of a three-point turn?
sec04-card-sec04-F067.teaching_text: Re-checking traffic and backing with full right lock until your nose clears the street's middle sets up a clean exit.

sec04-card-sec04-F068.question_text: What steps finish the third and final movement of a three-point turn?
sec04-card-sec04-F068.teaching_text: One final traffic scan before steering left into your new lane and canceling your blinker completes the reversal cleanly.

sec04-card-sec04-F069.question_text: Who has priority over your vehicle throughout every stage of a turnabout?
sec04-card-sec04-F069.teaching_text: Because your vehicle blocks lanes sideways mid-maneuver, through traffic and pedestrians always come first.

sec04-card-sec04-F070.question_text: How long should a complete stop last, and what head-scan pattern does the handbook advise?
sec04-card-sec04-F070.teaching_text: Coming to a full stop breaks rolling-stop habits and gives your eyes time to catch fast cross traffic.

sec04-card-sec04-F071.question_text: Where must you bring your vehicle to a halt at a stop sign that has a crosswalk or stop line?
sec04-card-sec04-F071.teaching_text: Stopping short of the near-side crosswalk or painted bar keeps pedestrian walking lanes unobstructed.

sec04-card-sec04-F072.question_text: Where do you stop at a stop sign when neither a crosswalk nor a painted stop line is present?
sec04-card-sec04-F072.teaching_text: Halt before your bumper enters cross traffic at the closest spot where you can see down the intersecting street.

sec04-card-sec04-F073.question_text: When may you roll past a stop sign without making the standard stop?
sec04-card-sec04-F073.teaching_text: Live traffic direction from a uniformed police officer or an active proceed signal overrides a static sign.

sec04-card-sec04-F074.question_text: Who goes first when cars arrive at a four-way stop at different moments?
sec04-card-sec04-F074.teaching_text: First to complete a stop is first to proceed, keeping all-way intersections orderly and predictable.

sec04-card-sec04-F075.question_text: Which driver gets the right-of-way when two vehicles stop at a four-way intersection at the exact same moment?
sec04-card-sec04-F075.teaching_text: Letting the driver on your right proceed first resolves simultaneous stops cleanly without hesitation waves.

sec04-card-sec04-F076.question_text: Which lane and signal habit should you use before pulling into a parking space?
sec04-card-sec04-F076.teaching_text: Approaching from the closest lane with your blinker flashing warns trailing drivers why you are slowing near the curb.

sec04-card-sec04-F077.question_text: What four steps secure your vehicle once you have parked inside a space?
sec04-card-sec04-F077.teaching_text: Shutting the motor, locking ignition, taking your key, and setting the parking brake stops rollaways and theft.

sec04-card-sec04-F078.question_text: What visual checks are required right before pulling out of a curb parking space?
sec04-card-sec04-F078.teaching_text: Side mirrors alone miss oncoming cars or cyclists tucked right beside your rear quarter panel.

sec04-card-sec04-F079.question_text: How should you signal and choose your lane when pulling away from a parked curb spot?
sec04-card-sec04-F079.teaching_text: Signaling before rolling and merging straight into the adjacent lane avoids cutting wide across multi-lane traffic.

sec04-card-sec04-F080.question_text: Name the six roadway structures and travel surfaces where stopping or parking is strictly banned.
sec04-card-sec04-F080.teaching_text: Leaving a vehicle on active highway lanes, sidewalks, intersections, bridges, tunnels, or rails traps traffic and emergency paths.
sec04-card-sec04-F080.must_match_memory_hook: Lanes, sidewalks, corners, bridges, tunnels, tracks

visual_sync.text_span: Lanes, sidewalks, corners, bridges, tunnels, tracks

sec04-card-sec04-F081.question_text: How does Rhode Island treat double parking or parking alongside roadwork where traffic gets blocked?
sec04-card-sec04-F081.teaching_text: Stopping abreast of parked cars or squeezing narrow construction zones chokes lane flow and blinds passing drivers.

sec04-card-sec04-F082.question_text: Which three access points and signed zones must never be blocked by a parked vehicle?
sec04-card-sec04-F082.teaching_text: Blocking driveways traps residents, blocking accessible ramps strands wheelchair users, and posted bans keep sightlines open.

sec04-card-sec04-F083.question_text: At least how many feet away from a fire hydrant must you park in Rhode Island?
sec04-card-sec04-F083.teaching_text: Note Rhode Island's specific eight-foot hydrant rule so fire crews have instant hose access without smashing windows.

sec04-card-sec04-F084.question_text: How close to an intersection crosswalk is parking prohibited?
sec04-card-sec04-F084.teaching_text: Keeping twenty feet clear beside crosswalks lets approaching drivers spot pedestrians before they step off the curb.

sec04-card-sec04-F085.question_text: Parking is prohibited within how many feet of a stop sign, traffic signal, or flashing beacon?
sec04-card-sec04-F085.teaching_text: Tall vehicles parked inside thirty feet hide stop signs and signals from approaching drivers until it is too late.

sec04-card-sec04-F086.question_text: What are the same-side and signed opposite-side parking clearances at a fire-station driveway?
sec04-card-sec04-F086.teaching_text: Wide ladder trucks need twenty feet on the station side and seventy-five signed feet across the street to swing out.

sec04-card-sec04-F087.question_text: How far must you park from the nearest railroad rail, and what brief exception exists?
sec04-card-sec04-F087.teaching_text: Staying fifty feet back keeps warning gates and train sightlines clear, allowing only quick active passenger or package stops.

sec04-card-sec04-F088.question_text: How close to the right curb or edge must your right wheels rest when parking on a two-lane road?
sec04-card-sec04-F088.teaching_text: Tucking your right tires within one foot of the curb keeps your left doors out of active traffic.

sec04-card-sec04-F089.question_text: How may you park on a one-way street where curb parking is allowed?
sec04-card-sec04-F089.teaching_text: One-way streets permit left-curb or right-curb parking within twelve inches, always pointed with traffic flow.
sec04-card-sec04-F089.must_match_memory_hook: Either side, twelve inches, with flow

visual_sync.text_span: Either side, twelve inches, with flow

sec04-card-sec04-F090.question_text: What job must your parking brake perform whenever you stop on a hill?
sec04-card-sec04-F090.teaching_text: A working parking brake locks the wheels securely so gravity cannot roll your car into bumpers behind you.

sec04-card-sec04-F091.question_text: What sequence gets you moving safely uphill from a parked curb spot?
sec04-card-sec04-F091.teaching_text: Checking your left blind spot, engaging drive gear, signaling, and releasing the parking brake prevents rolling backward as you merge.

sec04-card-sec04-F092.question_text: What four checks must happen before steering into an adjacent lane?
sec04-card-sec04-F092.teaching_text: Confirming space, signaling early, checking mirrors, and glancing over your shoulder catches hidden cars before you move.

sec04-card-sec04-F093.question_text: Where are the two separate stops required when pulling out of a driveway across a sidewalk?
sec04-card-sec04-F093.teaching_text: Exam questions test both stops, protecting joggers on the sidewalk first and roadway vehicles at the curb second.

sec04-card-sec04-F094.question_text: What three questions must all be answered yes before overtaking another vehicle?
sec04-card-sec04-F094.teaching_text: Even where passing lines are broken, risking oncoming traffic just to gain one car length before a red light makes zero sense.

sec04-card-sec04-F095.question_text: What pavement marking rule appears on the handbook's turnabout checklist?
sec04-card-sec04-F095.teaching_text: Solid yellow paint marks restricted sightlines or no-passing zones where swinging across lanes invites a crash.

sec06-card-sec06-F001.question_text: What signal is required before you pull out from a parking space in Rhode Island?
sec06-card-sec06-F001.teaching_text: Pulling away from a curb unannounced surprises approaching traffic expecting parked cars to stay put.

sec06-card-sec06-F002.question_text: At least how many feet ahead of a turn must you activate your turn signal?
sec06-card-sec06-F002.teaching_text: Flipping a blinker right as your wheels turn leaves trailing traffic zero time to brake smoothly.

sec06-card-sec06-F003.question_text: How do you position your left arm when giving a hand signal for a left turn?
sec06-card-sec06-F003.teaching_text: Waving or bending your arm confuses nearby drivers when electric turn lamps fail in daylight.

sec06-card-sec06-F004.question_text: How do you position your left arm when giving a hand signal for a right turn?
sec06-card-sec06-F004.teaching_text: Mixing up upward and downward arm angles makes following traffic misread a right turn as braking.

sec06-card-sec06-F005.question_text: How do you hold your left arm to hand-signal slowing down or stopping?
sec06-card-sec06-F005.teaching_text: Pointing your left arm straight down warns drivers behind you even if brake bulbs burn out.

sec06-card-sec06-F006.question_text: Why must you give directional signals well ahead of a planned maneuver?
sec06-card-sec06-F006.teaching_text: Early communication lets trailing vehicles adjust speed and spacing calmly before your path changes.

sec06-card-sec06-F007.question_text: What do solid lane lines generally forbid, and when does Rhode Island allow exceptions?
sec06-card-sec06-F007.teaching_text: Solid stripes protect high-conflict zones while still allowing lawful turns or steering around stalled hazards.

sec06-card-sec06-F008.question_text: What movements do broken white lines allow between lanes moving in one direction?
sec06-card-sec06-F008.teaching_text: Dashed white markings separate same-way lanes where shifting over is allowed once mirrors and blind spots clear.

sec06-card-sec06-F009.question_text: What does a single broken yellow centerline allow between opposing traffic streams?
sec06-card-sec06-F009.teaching_text: Dashed yellow paint permits overtaking only when oncoming sight distance is wide open and clear.

sec06-card-sec06-F010.question_text: When a solid line pairs with a broken line, what rule applies to drivers beside the solid line?
sec06-card-sec06-F010.teaching_text: Having the solid stripe on your side signals restricted sight distance where pulling out risks a head-on crash.

sec06-card-sec06-F011.question_text: What may a driver do when traveling beside the broken side of a paired solid-and-broken centerline?
sec06-card-sec06-F011.teaching_text: Even when your side has dashed paint, you still have to verify clear opposing space before overtaking.

sec06-card-sec06-F012.question_text: How do yellow pavement lines and white pavement lines differ in traffic direction?
sec06-card-sec06-F012.teaching_text: Spotting line color instantly tells you whether the adjacent lane carries oncoming cars or same-way traffic.

sec06-card-sec06-F013.question_text: What does a solid yellow line prohibit, and what crossing exceptions are recognized?
sec06-card-sec06-F013.teaching_text: Crossing solid yellow to overtake is illegal, though lawful left turns and blocked lanes justify careful crossing.

sec06-card-sec06-F014.question_text: How is a shared center turn lane marked on Rhode Island pavement?
sec06-card-sec06-F014.teaching_text: Paired solid outside and dashed inside yellow lines with turn arrows distinguish center turn pockets from travel lanes.

sec06-card-sec06-F015.question_text: What is a shared center turn lane reserved for instead of ordinary through travel?
sec06-card-sec06-F015.teaching_text: Cruising straight down a shared center pocket puts you nose-to-nose with opposing drivers setting up turns.

sec06-card-sec06-F016.question_text: What does a shared-lane bicycle marking warn motorists to expect?
sec06-card-sec06-F016.teaching_text: Narrow lanes leave zero safe room to squeeze past side by side, so riders lawfully use full lane width.

sec06-card-sec06-F017.question_text: What purpose is a high-occupancy vehicle lane designed to serve?
sec06-card-sec06-F017.teaching_text: Solo drivers who slip into restricted carpool lanes risk citations while slowing multi-passenger traffic.

sec06-card-sec06-F018.question_text: Which turning movements does a shared center left-turn lane serve?
sec06-card-sec06-F018.teaching_text: Drivers from both directions share the middle pocket when turning into or out of left-side driveways and streets.

sec06-card-sec06-F019.question_text: What does an overhead green arrow above a reversible lane tell drivers?
sec06-card-sec06-F019.teaching_text: Reversible lanes switch flow by rush hour, so overhead green arrows confirm your direction owns the lane.

sec06-card-sec06-F020.question_text: What is required to park legally in a disabled-parking space marked for permit holders?
sec06-card-sec06-F020.teaching_text: Parking in accessible stalls without proper authorization blocks vital ramp access and triggers steep fines.

sec06-card-sec06-F021.question_text: In which direction does traffic circulate around a roundabout's central island?
sec06-card-sec06-F021.teaching_text: Turning right upon entry keeps every vehicle circulating counterclockwise around the center island.

sec06-card-sec06-F022.question_text: What traffic controls guide roundabouts instead of ordinary stop signs or traffic lights?
sec06-card-sec06-F022.teaching_text: Continuous circular flow relies on entry yield signs and lane paint rather than red-yellow-green signal cycles.

sec06-card-sec06-F023.question_text: Because standard handbook roundabout steps cover single-lane circles, what should you do before another layout?
sec06-card-sec06-F023.teaching_text: Reading advance lane-choice signs early prevents last-second weaving inside multi-lane circular intersections.

sec06-card-sec06-F024.question_text: How should you manage speed and priority as you approach a roundabout?
sec06-card-sec06-F024.teaching_text: Dropping down to advisory entry speed gives you time to spot crosswalk pedestrians and priority users.

sec06-card-sec06-F025.question_text: Who has priority before you enter a roundabout?
sec06-card-sec06-F025.teaching_text: Forcing your nose ahead of cars already in the circle causes side-impact crashes at the entry apron.

sec06-card-sec06-F026.question_text: Once circulating inside a roundabout, when is stopping permitted?
sec06-card-sec06-F026.teaching_text: Halting mid-circle to wave someone in triggers instant rear-end chain collisions behind you.

sec06-card-sec06-F027.question_text: What two steps must you take when exiting a roundabout to the right?
sec06-card-sec06-F027.teaching_text: Signaling tells waiting drivers your path while yielding protects people crossing the exit leg.

sec06-card-sec06-F028.question_text: What two ways may a bicyclist navigate a roundabout depending on experience?
sec06-card-sec06-F028.teaching_text: Less confident cyclists can dismount for pedestrian crossings while experienced riders merge into traffic flow.

sec06-card-sec06-F029.question_text: Where in the lane should a cyclist ride through a roundabout, and why?
sec06-card-sec06-F029.teaching_text: Hugging the outer curb tempts motorists to overtake beside a bike inside a tight curved lane.

sec06-card-sec06-F030.question_text: What duty do cyclists riding through a roundabout owe pedestrians in crosswalks?
sec06-card-sec06-F030.teaching_text: Bicycles operating on the roadway carry the same obligation as cars to let crosswalk users pass.

sec06-card-sec06-F031.question_text: How should a pedestrian scan and stage a crossing at a roundabout approach?
sec06-card-sec06-F031.teaching_text: Splitter islands divide crossing into two one-way checks so walkers handle one traffic stream at a time.

sec06-card-sec06-F032.question_text: Where must pedestrians cross at a roundabout instead of cutting across the center?
sec06-card-sec06-F032.teaching_text: Walking through circulating lanes or across the central island puts pedestrians directly into blind curving traffic.

sec06-card-sec06-F033.question_text: Who must yield at a rotary or circle when no sign or traffic-control device is posted?
sec06-card-sec06-F033.teaching_text: Missing signs never flip priority, so approaching cars still wait for vehicles already circulating.

sec06-card-sec06-F034.question_text: How should you approach an intersection lacking any traffic signals or signs?
sec06-card-sec06-F034.teaching_text: Assuming open priority at an unsigned residential corner invites broadside collisions with cross traffic.

sec06-card-sec06-F035.question_text: How must you respond on a green signal if another driver runs a red light?
sec06-card-sec06-F035.teaching_text: Having a green lamp never shields you physically from a red-light runner entering the box.

sec06-card-sec06-F036.question_text: What exact foot movement defines covering the brake?
sec06-card-sec06-F036.teaching_text: Poising your right foot over the pedal trims reaction delay without riding the brakes or flashing stop lamps.

sec06-card-sec06-F037.question_text: What does the legal concept of right-of-way determine on the road?
sec06-card-sec06-F037.teaching_text: Clear priority rules keep intersecting drivers and pedestrians from claiming the same pavement simultaneously.

sec06-card-sec06-F038.question_text: Where must you stop at a steady red light when no other signal authorizes movement?
sec06-card-sec06-F038.teaching_text: Rolling onto the crosswalk blocks foot traffic and noses your bumper into cross-street turning paths.

sec06-card-sec06-F039.question_text: Under what three conditions is a right turn on a steady red light lawful?
sec06-card-sec06-F039.teaching_text: Rolling a red turn or overlooking a posted prohibition sign triggers tickets and crosswalk strikes.

sec06-card-sec06-F040.question_text: Are you required to turn right on a steady red light if drivers behind you want to go?
sec06-card-sec06-F040.teaching_text: Right on red is permissive rather than mandatory, so impatient honking never forces you to turn.

sec06-card-sec06-F041.question_text: What does a steady yellow traffic light mean, and when may you continue through?
sec06-card-sec06-F041.teaching_text: Speeding up to beat yellow puts you inside the intersection just as cross traffic gets green.

sec06-card-sec06-F042.question_text: How should you proceed when facing a steady green traffic signal?
sec06-card-sec06-F042.teaching_text: Even on steady green, leftover turning vehicles or slow walkers may still occupy the intersection.

sec06-card-sec06-F043.question_text: What three actions are required when approaching a flashing yellow traffic light?
sec06-card-sec06-F043.teaching_text: Flashing yellow flags a hazard spot where dropping speed and hovering over the brake prevents surprises.

sec06-card-sec06-F044.question_text: How must you handle a flashing red traffic signal?
sec06-card-sec06-F044.teaching_text: Treating flashing red like a yield instead of a full stop causes high-speed T-bone crashes.

sec06-card-sec06-F045.question_text: What does a lighted green arrow allow when shown alongside a steady red light?
sec06-card-sec06-F045.teaching_text: A green arrow grants protected movement for its specific lane even while through lanes stay stopped on red.

sec06-card-sec06-F046.question_text: What does a lighted red arrow prohibit at an intersection?
sec06-card-sec06-F046.teaching_text: Unlike a circular red, a red arrow blocks turns in its pointed direction until a permissive signal appears.

sec06-card-sec06-F047.question_text: How early should you move into the proper lane for an upcoming turn?
sec06-card-sec06-F047.teaching_text: Diving across lanes at the last moment cuts off adjacent cars and leaves zero room to signal.

sec06-card-sec06-F048.question_text: When may you turn on a flashing yellow arrow signal?
sec06-card-sec06-F048.teaching_text: Flashing yellow arrows mean permissive turns where oncoming traffic still holds green and crosswalks stay active.

sec06-card-sec06-F049.question_text: How does a stale green signal differ from a fresh green signal?
sec06-card-sec06-F049.teaching_text: Recognizing a signal staying green awhile prepares you to stop smoothly when yellow appears.

sec06-card-sec06-F050.question_text: What is the purpose of a HAWK crossing signal?
sec06-card-sec06-F050.teaching_text: High-intensity pedestrian beacons stop street traffic on demand where walkers face wide or busy roadways.

sec09-card-sec09-F001.question_text: What does defensive driving anticipate, and whom does it protect?
sec09-card-sec09-F001.teaching_text: Spotting mistakes before they escalate shields your cabin as well as surrounding drivers, riders, and walkers.

sec09-card-sec09-F002.question_text: Which two vehicle controls does a defensive driver adjust as traffic, weather, and roads change?
sec09-card-sec09-F002.teaching_text: Holding rigid speed or lane placement when rain starts or traffic crowds erases your safety cushion.

sec09-card-sec09-F003.question_text: What four ordered actions make up the IPDE driving sequence?
sec09-card-sec09-F003.teaching_text: Working through all four steps in order turns panic reactions into smooth, deliberate hazard avoidance.

sec09-card-sec09-F004.question_text: What does the identify step mean inside the IPDE process?
sec09-card-sec09-F004.teaching_text: You cannot dodge a threat you never spotted, so active scanning comes before every other step.

sec09-card-sec09-F005.question_text: What does predicting mean in the IPDE defensive driving sequence?
sec09-card-sec09-F005.teaching_text: Asking where a backing car or darting pedestrian could intersect your path prevents last-second surprises.

sec09-card-sec09-F006.question_text: What choices are made during the decide step of IPDE?
sec09-card-sec09-F006.teaching_text: Choosing whether to brake, steer, or tap the horn ahead of time prevents hesitation under pressure.

sec09-card-sec09-F007.question_text: What happens during the execute step of the IPDE sequence?
sec09-card-sec09-F007.teaching_text: Physical braking, steering, or signaling turns your mental plan into safe separation on the pavement.

sec09-card-sec09-F008.question_text: How many areas of space around your vehicle does the zone system monitor?
sec09-card-sec09-F008.teaching_text: Tracking front, rear, and corner spaces keeps you aware of every escape lane and blind-spot intruder.

sec09-card-sec09-F009.question_text: What defines an open zone around your vehicle?
sec09-card-sec09-F009.teaching_text: An open zone gives you both clean sightlines and empty pavement to move into without conflict.

sec09-card-sec09-F010.question_text: What makes a zone around your vehicle count as a closed zone?
sec09-card-sec09-F010.teaching_text: A truck, curve, or parked car closes a zone by cutting off either visibility or drivable space.

sec09-card-sec09-F011.question_text: What is the purpose of following a regular visual-search sequence while driving?
sec09-card-sec09-F011.teaching_text: Traffic shifts every second, so cycling your eyes across priority zones catches hazards early.

sec09-card-sec09-F012.question_text: How many seconds ahead should you scan intersections, driveways, and parked cars in your target area?
sec09-card-sec09-F012.teaching_text: Looking twelve to fifteen seconds downrange reveals emerging cross-traffic well before hard braking is needed.

sec09-card-sec09-F013.question_text: Along with rear mirror checks, what closer forward time zone belongs in your visual-search pattern?
sec09-card-sec09-F013.teaching_text: Pairing rear mirror glances with your immediate four-to-six-second path catches sudden brake lights and tailgaters.

sec09-card-sec09-F014.question_text: How should your eyes cover areas ahead, beside, and behind your vehicle instead of staring?
sec09-card-sec09-F014.teaching_text: Target fixation freezes awareness, allowing blind-spot mergers or braking traffic to catch you off guard.

sec09-card-sec09-F015.question_text: Which interior checks belong inside a driver's regular visual-search routine?
sec09-card-sec09-F015.teaching_text: Quick instrument flicks catch creeping highway speed or warning lamps without pulling focus off traffic.

sec09-card-sec09-F016.question_text: How does the Smith driving approach use space around your vehicle?
sec09-card-sec09-F016.teaching_text: Surrounding your car with open pavement buys reaction time when nearby drivers swerve or slam brakes.

sec09-card-sec09-F017.question_text: What does leaving yourself an escape option mean in traffic?
sec09-card-sec09-F017.teaching_text: Boxing yourself tightly between cars on every side leaves nowhere to steer if traffic ahead locks up.

sec09-card-sec09-F018.question_text: Where should you aim your eyes while driving instead of staring down at your hood or fender?
sec09-card-sec09-F018.teaching_text: Looking down near your front bumper causes wandering steering and late reactions to stopped traffic ahead.

sec09-card-sec09-F019.question_text: How far ahead does Rhode Island recommend looking in towns versus on highways?
sec09-card-sec09-F019.teaching_text: Faster highway speeds cover ground rapidly, requiring a half-mile view to match a one-block town scan.

sec09-card-sec09-F020.question_text: Between which three areas should your eyes keep moving to maintain full awareness?
sec09-card-sec09-F020.teaching_text: Rotating focus across front lanes, side margins, and mirrors prevents tunnel vision on long drives.

sec09-card-sec09-F021.question_text: What should you do instead of assuming another road user sees your vehicle?
sec09-card-sec09-F021.teaching_text: A polite horn tap or quick beam flash alerts distracted drivers or walkers before paths cross.

sec09-card-sec09-F022.question_text: What limitation applies even when you hold a three-second following gap?
sec09-card-sec09-F022.teaching_text: Slick roads, heavy loads, or multi-car pileups can demand far more stopping room than three dry seconds.

sec09-card-sec09-F023.question_text: When do you begin counting seconds to measure your following distance?
sec09-card-sec09-F023.teaching_text: Picking a fixed shadow or signpost as the lead car's rear bumper clears it gives an honest time check.

sec09-card-sec09-F024.question_text: What should you do if your front bumper passes your landmark before three seconds finish?
sec09-card-sec09-F024.teaching_text: Reaching the mark early proves you are tailgating, so backing off and recounting restores safe margin.

sec09-card-sec09-F025.question_text: How much extra following time must you add for each adverse road or weather condition?
sec09-card-sec09-F025.teaching_text: Stacking rain, darkness, and glare multiplies stopping distance, so each extra hazard earns another full second.

sec09-card-sec09-F026.question_text: What does the point-of-no-return concept measure as you approach an intersection?
sec09-card-sec09-F026.teaching_text: Speed and pavement grip determine the exact spot past which you can no longer halt safely before a crosswalk.

sec09-card-sec09-F027.question_text: Where is lane position one located, and when is it your ordinary choice?
sec09-card-sec09-F027.teaching_text: Centering inside your stripes maximizes equal buffer space on both sides during normal hazard-free driving.

sec09-card-sec09-F028.question_text: Where does lane position two place your car, and when might you use it?
sec09-card-sec09-F028.teaching_text: Hugging three to six inches inside the left stripe creates clearance past parked cars or sets up left turns.

sec09-card-sec09-F029.question_text: Where does lane position three place your car, and when might you use it?
sec09-card-sec09-F029.teaching_text: Positioning several inches inside the right curb or stripe widens buffer space from left-side traffic or preps right turns.

sec10-card-sec10-F001.question_text: How do large commercial trucks compare with passenger cars in maneuverability and blind spots?
sec10-card-sec10-F001.teaching_text: Heavy rigs need far wider turning arcs and carry massive blind areas where small cars vanish.

sec10-card-sec10-F002.question_text: Where are the main blind areas located around a large truck?
sec10-card-sec10-F002.teaching_text: High cabs and long trailers block the trucker's view right off the nose, alongside doors, and astern.

sec10-card-sec10-F003.question_text: How far behind a truck pulling a trailer can its rear blind area stretch?
sec10-card-sec10-F003.teaching_text: Tucking close behind trailer doors hides your car completely while blocking your own view of traffic ahead.

sec10-card-sec10-F004.question_text: How should you handle driving near a large truck's right-side blind area?
sec10-card-sec10-F004.teaching_text: Lingering alongside a trailer's right flank invites a squeeze crash if the rig merges or swings wide.
sec10-card-sec10-F004.must_match_memory_hook: Clear right side, pass or drop

visual_sync.text_span: Clear right side, pass or drop

sec10-card-sec10-F005.question_text: Why must you keep a firm two-handed grip when overtaking near a large truck?
sec10-card-sec10-F005.teaching_text: High-speed air pressure shifts beside a big trailer can tug a relaxed driver toward the rig's wheels.

sec10-card-sec10-F006.question_text: At least how many feet behind a large truck does Rhode Island recommend staying so the driver sees you?
sec10-card-sec10-F006.teaching_text: Holding fifty feet or more puts your hood back inside the wide-angle sweep of cab side mirrors.

sec10-card-sec10-F007.question_text: What visual check confirms a truck driver can spot you while you follow behind?
sec10-card-sec10-F007.teaching_text: If trailer walls block your view of the cab's side mirrors, the trucker cannot see your car either.

sec10-card-sec10-F008.question_text: How should you share intersections and driveways with turning large vehicles?
sec10-card-sec10-F008.teaching_text: Long wheelbases swing wide and track inward, so watching marker lamps prevents squeezing inside a turning trailer.

sec10-card-sec10-F009.question_text: During which hours and sight-distance limit are headlights mandatory in Rhode Island?
sec10-card-sec10-F009.teaching_text: Turning headlights on whenever visibility drops under five hundred feet lets oncoming drivers see you in time.

sec10-card-sec10-F010.question_text: When does operating your windshield wipers make headlights mandatory?
sec10-card-sec10-F010.teaching_text: Daytime rain, sleet, or snow hides gray cars in spray unless headlights and taillights stay lit.

sec10-card-sec10-F011.question_text: Why should you use low beams rather than high beams in fog, rain, or snow?
sec10-card-sec10-F011.teaching_text: High beams bounce straight back off airborne water droplets and snowflakes, blinding you with whiteout glare.

sec10-card-sec10-F012.question_text: From at least how many feet behind must your rear license-plate light make the plate readable?
sec10-card-sec10-F012.teaching_text: A burned-out rear tag bulb is an easy nighttime equipment stop if numbers fade within sixty feet.

sec10-card-sec10-F013.question_text: At least how many feet away must you dim high beams for an approaching vehicle?
sec10-card-sec10-F013.teaching_text: Blasting brights closer than five hundred feet blinds oncoming drivers steering right beside your lane.

sec10-card-sec10-F014.question_text: Within what distance behind another vehicle must you switch to low-beam headlights?
sec10-card-sec10-F014.teaching_text: High beams inside two hundred feet bounce off interior and side mirrors straight into the lead driver's eyes.

sec10-card-sec10-F015.question_text: Where should you direct your gaze when oncoming headlights glare at night?
sec10-card-sec10-F015.teaching_text: Using the right fog line keeps your car centered while sparing your retinas from direct bright beams.

sec10-card-sec10-F016.question_text: What does glare recovery time measure after bright light hits your eyes?
sec10-card-sec10-F016.teaching_text: For several seconds after bright glare passes, your pupils stay constricted and miss dark roadside hazards.

sec10-card-sec10-F017.question_text: Why must you slow down and stay alert wherever pedestrians and parked cars line the street?
sec10-card-sec10-F017.teaching_text: Parked SUVs and vans hide people stepping off curbs until they emerge right beside your front fender.

sec10-card-sec10-F018.question_text: Must you still yield if a pedestrian crosses carelessly outside proper rules?
sec10-card-sec10-F018.teaching_text: Holding legal priority never excuses striking an unprotected person crossing on foot.

sec10-card-sec10-F019.question_text: Why do children near a street require extra driver caution?
sec10-card-sec10-F019.teaching_text: Young kids chase balls or friends impulsively without scanning traffic or judging closing speed.

sec10-card-sec10-F020.question_text: Why should you give older pedestrians extra patience and crossing time?
sec10-card-sec10-F020.teaching_text: Reduced mobility or slower reaction speed means older adults may still be mid-crosswalk when signals change.

sec10-card-sec10-F021.question_text: What does the Rhode Island handbook instruct drivers about stopping for hitchhikers?
sec10-card-sec10-F021.teaching_text: Halting unexpectedly along highway shoulders risks personal safety and high-speed rear-end collisions.

sec10-card-sec10-F022.question_text: When may a pedestrian step across against a yellow or red traffic light?
sec10-card-sec10-F022.teaching_text: Pedestrian heads govern foot crossings, so walkers wait unless an active Walk symbol authorizes stepping out.

sec10-card-sec10-F023.question_text: Where should pedestrians walk when a road has a sidewalk versus when no sidewalk exists?
sec10-card-sec10-F023.teaching_text: Walking on the left shoulder facing oncoming cars lets you see approaching headlights and step clear.

sec10-card-sec10-F024.question_text: Does a public road intersection form a legal crosswalk when no painted lines exist?
sec10-card-sec10-F024.teaching_text: Missing paint never cancels pedestrian crossing rights where two public streets meet.

sec10-card-sec10-F025.question_text: What clothing should pedestrians wear when walking at dusk or after dark?
sec10-card-sec10-F025.teaching_text: Light colors and retroreflective strips bounce low-beam light back to drivers hundreds of feet earlier.

sec10-card-sec10-F026.question_text: When should you reduce speed after spotting a visible hazard down the road?
sec10-card-sec10-F026.teaching_text: Easing speed right away keeps stopping effortless instead of forcing hard last-second braking at the hazard.

sec10-card-sec10-F027.question_text: What must you do when a pedestrian with a white cane or guide dog crosses or prepares to cross ahead?
sec10-card-sec10-F027.teaching_text: Rhode Island requires a complete stop before the intersection whenever a blind pedestrian enters or approaches a crossing.

sec10-card-sec10-F028.question_text: What maximum fine warns drivers against failing to yield for a blind pedestrian?
sec10-card-sec10-F028.teaching_text: Endangering a visually impaired walker triggers one of Rhode Island's heaviest traffic fines.

sec10-card-sec10-F029.question_text: Why can turning right on red catch a visually impaired pedestrian off guard?
sec10-card-sec10-F029.teaching_text: Hearing your car halt suggests stopped traffic, leaving a blind walker unaware you plan to roll right on red.

sec10-card-sec10-F030.question_text: Why do electric and hybrid drivers need extra awareness near pedestrians who rely on hearing?
sec10-card-sec10-F030.teaching_text: Near-silent electric motors give blind or distracted walkers almost zero engine sound at low neighborhood speeds.

sec10-card-sec10-F031.question_text: What must traffic from both directions do when a school bus flashes red lights, and for how long?
sec10-card-sec10-F031.teaching_text: Children cross unpredictably in front of and behind buses until red warning lamps switch completely off.

sec10-card-sec10-F032.question_text: Beyond public highways, where else does Rhode Island's school-bus stopping law apply?
sec10-card-sec10-F032.teaching_text: School campus loops, apartment drives, and parking lots enforce identical flashing-red school-bus stop rules.

sec10-card-sec10-F033.question_text: When is oncoming traffic exempt from stopping for a school bus's flashing red lights?
sec10-card-sec10-F033.teaching_text: Only drivers on the opposite roadway of a physically divided highway may proceed while watching cautiously.

sec10-card-sec10-F034.question_text: What physical separation defines a divided highway for school-bus stopping rules?
sec10-card-sec10-F034.teaching_text: Painted yellow lines or shared turn pockets never excuse oncoming cars from stopping for red bus lights.

sec10-card-sec10-F035.question_text: What fine range applies to a first conviction for illegally passing a stopped school bus?
sec10-card-sec10-F035.teaching_text: Even a first-time failure to stop for flashing school-bus reds carries a steep mandatory dollar penalty.

sec10-card-sec10-F036.question_text: How long can your license be suspended for a first school-bus stopping violation?
