sec10-card-sec10-F036.teaching_text: Passing a stopped bus can cost your driving privileges for thirty days on offense one, escalating sharply afterward.

sec10-card-sec10-F037.question_text: How do a bicyclist's roadway rights and duties compare with a motor-vehicle driver's?
sec10-card-sec10-F037.teaching_text: Treating cyclists as lawful vehicle operators prevents cutoffs at stop signs, turn lanes, and intersections.

sec10-card-sec10-F038.question_text: At most how many bicycles may ride abreast side by side in Rhode Island?
sec10-card-sec10-F038.teaching_text: Spreading three or more bikes across a lane blocks lawful overtaking and crowds opposing traffic.

sec10-card-sec10-F039.question_text: Which bicycle riders and passengers must wear a certified helmet on Rhode Island public ways?
sec10-card-sec10-F039.teaching_text: Every young cyclist or bike passenger aged fifteen or younger needs certified head protection on roads and paths.

sec10-card-sec10-F040.question_text: Which street-surface and curbside hazards can force a cyclist to shift lane position suddenly?
sec10-card-sec10-F040.teaching_text: Skinny bike tires trap or puncture easily on grates, glass, rails, or swinging car doors.

sec10-card-sec10-F041.question_text: Why must you leave generous side space instead of crowding a cyclist's path?
sec10-card-sec10-F041.teaching_text: Crowding a rider eliminates the lateral room needed to steer around storm grates or broken pavement.

sec10-card-sec10-F042.question_text: Which way should bicyclists ride relative to traffic, and how must drivers yield?
sec10-card-sec10-F042.teaching_text: Cycling with traffic matches vehicle patterns, and drivers owe bikes identical intersection priority.

sec10-card-sec10-F043.question_text: How should you adjust space around a cyclist who looks unsteady or inexperienced?
sec10-card-sec10-F043.teaching_text: Wobbling handlebars signal a beginner who could drift sideways unexpectedly when looking back or pedaling uphill.

sec10-card-sec10-F044.question_text: How do shared-lane pavement markings guide cyclist placement in narrow lanes?
sec10-card-sec10-F044.teaching_text: Painted chevrons guide riders outside the parked-door swing zone and mark safe placement inside tight lanes.

sec10-card-sec10-F045.question_text: What two behaviors do shared-lane markings promote for drivers and cyclists?
sec10-card-sec10-F045.teaching_text: Clear lane chevrons remind motorists to pass wide and steer cyclists away from riding wrong-way.

sec10-card-sec10-F046.question_text: Why shouldn't you blast your horn right beside or behind a bicyclist?
sec10-card-sec10-F046.teaching_text: A sudden close horn blast can shock a rider into jerking handlebars straight into your bumper.

sec10-card-sec10-F047.question_text: What must you avoid doing around marked bicycle lanes when approaching riders?
sec10-card-sec10-F047.teaching_text: Drifting onto phone screens or weaving across solid bike-lane paint puts cars directly onto exposed cyclists.

sec10-card-sec10-F048.question_text: How should you adjust following and passing room around cyclists during bad weather?
sec10-card-sec10-F048.teaching_text: Crosswinds, wet rims, and spray stretch bike braking and push riders sideways without warning.

sec10-card-sec10-F049.question_text: How many feet of passing clearance does the handbook describe when overtaking a cyclist, and what readiness is required?
sec10-card-sec10-F049.teaching_text: Leaving three to five feet and staying ready to halt prevents running over a rider who slips.

sec10-card-sec10-F050.question_text: What must you do when a lane is too narrow to pass a centered cyclist safely?
sec10-card-sec10-F050.teaching_text: Squeezing past inside a tight lane leaves zero margin, so wait behind until safe width opens.

sec10-card-sec10-F051.question_text: When is it safe to pull out to overtake a cyclist on a two-way street?
sec10-card-sec10-F051.teaching_text: Starting a pass against oncoming cars traps you into cutting back sharply into the cyclist.

sec10-card-sec10-F052.question_text: What must you avoid doing right after overtaking a bicyclist?
sec10-card-sec10-F052.teaching_text: Passing a rider only to slam your brakes for a turn or parking spot forces a rear-end bike crash.

sec10-card-sec10-F053.question_text: How must you treat an oncoming cyclist when preparing to turn left?
sec10-card-sec10-F053.teaching_text: Underestimating a cyclist's closing speed causes left-cross collisions right in the intersection.

sec10-card-sec10-F054.question_text: Where must you check for cyclists before turning right into a street or driveway?
sec10-card-sec10-F054.teaching_text: Turning right across a straight-moving rider's path causes classic right-hook crashes at corners and driveways.

sec10-card-sec10-F055.question_text: What check is required before unlatching and opening a parked car's street-side door?
sec10-card-sec10-F055.teaching_text: Swinging a heavy door into a bike lane leaves an approaching rider zero feet to stop or swerve.

sec10-card-sec10-F056.question_text: When may you cross a bicycle lane, and who holds right-of-way?
sec10-card-sec10-F056.teaching_text: Turns and driveway entries allow crossing bike lanes only after yielding to every cyclist and sidewalk user.

sec10-card-sec10-F057.question_text: How should you drive around children riding bicycles, especially near schools?
sec10-card-sec10-F057.teaching_text: Young riders weave unpredictably and misjudge traffic gaps around schoolyards and neighborhood corners.

sec10-card-sec10-F058.question_text: What type of crash does the term dooring describe?
sec10-card-sec10-F058.teaching_text: Dooring either knocks a rider onto the door edge or pitches them outward under moving traffic.

sec10-card-sec10-F059.question_text: How do you perform the Dutch Reach when opening the driver's door?
sec10-card-sec10-F059.teaching_text: Reaching across with your right hand naturally pivots your shoulders to scan side and rear glass.

sec10-card-sec10-F060.question_text: When is opening a vehicle door on the side of moving traffic lawful?
sec10-card-sec10-F060.teaching_text: Rhode Island law places full duty on the person opening the door to wait for a clear gap.

sec10-card-sec10-F061.question_text: How long may a vehicle door stay open toward moving traffic?
sec10-card-sec10-F061.teaching_text: Leaving a street-side door propped open creates a fixed collision hazard for passing bikes and cars.

sec10-card-sec10-F062.question_text: Which driving behaviors can provoke aggressive reactions from other motorists?
sec10-card-sec10-F062.teaching_text: Camping in passing lanes, blocking merges, or leaning on the horn needlessly escalates minor delays into rage.

sec10-card-sec10-F063.question_text: What assumption should you avoid when another driver makes a sudden or rude-looking move?
sec10-card-sec10-F063.teaching_text: Most abrupt lane cuts stem from distraction or unfamiliar streets rather than personal malice toward you.

sec10-card-sec10-F064.question_text: How can you lower your own risk of driving aggressively before and during a trip?
sec10-card-sec10-F064.teaching_text: Starting a drive exhausted or furious shrinks patience fast whenever traffic slows down.

sec10-card-sec10-F065.question_text: Which retaliatory actions must you avoid when dealing with an aggressive driver?
sec10-card-sec10-F065.teaching_text: Brake-checking or staring down a hostile motorist turns a brief traffic annoyance into a dangerous confrontation.

sec10-card-sec10-F066.question_text: Where should you drive if a hostile motorist persists in tailing or harassing you?
sec10-card-sec10-F066.teaching_text: Pulling into an isolated driveway or empty lot leaves you alone, whereas police stations deter pursuers.

sec10-card-sec10-F067.question_text: What two precautions keep you safer inside your car when stopped in traffic?
sec10-card-sec10-F067.teaching_text: Locked doors secure the cabin while stopping back from the bumper ahead lets you steer around trouble.

sec10-card-sec10-F068.question_text: How should you draw immediate help if someone tries to open or enter your vehicle?
sec10-card-sec10-F068.teaching_text: Loud continuous horn or alarm blasts put public eyes on the aggressor and call bystanders' attention.

sec10-card-sec10-F069.question_text: How should you handle a heated traffic confrontation regarding fights or weapons?
sec10-card-sec10-F069.teaching_text: Giving a hostile driver open room to drive off ends the threat without violence.

sec11-card-sec11-F001.question_text: Who bears personal responsibility for learning Rhode Island's motor vehicle laws?
sec11-card-sec11-F001.teaching_text: Claiming you did not know a Rhode Island traffic statute never excuses a violation during a stop.

sec11-card-sec11-F002.question_text: Is turning right on red mandatory, and what three conditions must be met before turning?
sec11-card-sec11-F002.teaching_text: Impatient honking behind you never forces a right-on-red turn, and rolling without a full stop earns a ticket.

sec11-card-sec11-F003.question_text: Which two manufacturer guidelines govern how a child restraint must be used?
sec11-card-sec11-F003.teaching_text: Graduating a child out of a harness too early compromises crash protection engineered around strict height-and-weight specs.

sec11-card-sec11-F004.question_text: Who inside a motor vehicle is required to wear a safety belt in Rhode Island?
sec11-card-sec11-F004.teaching_text: An unbuckled rider becomes a dangerous projectile inside the cabin, putting belted occupants at risk during impacts.

sec11-card-sec11-F005.question_text: What must you prepare to do whenever a school bus activates flashing red lights?
sec11-card-sec11-F005.teaching_text: Flashing red bus lamps mean children are actively stepping off the curb or crossing traffic lanes nearby.

sec11-card-sec11-F006.question_text: At least how many feet ahead of a turn or lane change must you start signaling?
sec11-card-sec11-F006.teaching_text: Clicking your blinker mid-turn surprises trailing drivers instead of giving them advance space to adjust speed.

sec11-card-sec11-F007.question_text: Why should you ease your speed down gradually before making a turn?
sec11-card-sec11-F007.teaching_text: Slamming the brakes at the last instant invites rear-end collisions from drivers trailing right behind your bumper.

sec11-card-sec11-F008.question_text: When two cars reach an unsigned, unsignaled intersection from different roads together, who yields?
sec11-card-sec11-F008.teaching_text: Checking right and yielding when you sit on the left resolves uncontrolled residential ties without hesitation.

sec11-card-sec11-F009.question_text: During which daily hours—and below what forward visibility distance—must your headlights stay on?
sec11-card-sec11-F009.teaching_text: Daytime fog or heavy overcast under five hundred feet hides unlit gray cars from oncoming drivers.

sec11-card-sec11-F010.question_text: What lighting rule applies during rain, falling snow, or other low-visibility weather?
sec11-card-sec11-F010.teaching_text: Daytime running lights often leave rear taillights dark, whereas full headlights illuminate both ends in spray.

sec11-card-sec11-F011.question_text: What exterior lights must be switched on whenever your windshield wipers are running?
sec11-card-sec11-F011.teaching_text: Linking your headlight switch directly to wiper use guarantees your car stays visible during passing showers.

sec11-card-sec11-F012.question_text: What winter buildup must you clear off your vehicle wherever it blocks your sightlines?
sec11-card-sec11-F012.teaching_text: Peeking through a tiny scraped porthole hides cross-traffic and pedestrians stepping off snowy corners.

sec11-card-sec11-F013.question_text: Why must you brush accumulated snow off your vehicle's roof before driving?
sec11-card-sec11-F013.teaching_text: Sheets of frozen roof snow peel off at highway speed and smash straight into trailing windshields.

sec11-card-sec11-F014.question_text: What financial protection must every motor vehicle driven on Rhode Island public roads carry?
sec11-card-sec11-F014.teaching_text: Active liability coverage ensures crash victims are not stuck paying out-of-pocket for damage another driver caused.

sec11-card-sec11-F015.question_text: What insurance commitment must an owner affirm when obtaining or renewing Rhode Island registration?
sec11-card-sec11-F015.teaching_text: Canceling your policy right after getting plates violates your signed affirmation to keep continuous coverage active.

sec11-card-sec11-F016.question_text: Which two documents should stay together inside your vehicle whenever it is on the road?
sec11-card-sec11-F016.teaching_text: Storing active insurance verification alongside your registration card makes traffic stops and crash exchanges effortless.

sec11-card-sec11-F017.question_text: What dollar fine is listed for failing to comply with Rhode Island's proof-of-insurance requirement?
sec11-card-sec11-F017.teaching_text: Forgetting or dropping required insurance proof exposes you to a steep five-hundred-dollar statutory penalty.

sec11-card-sec11-F018.question_text: What insurance duty must an applicant acknowledge when getting or renewing a Rhode Island driver license?
sec11-card-sec11-F018.teaching_text: Even when borrowing someone else's car, the driver behind the wheel must verify insurance proof is aboard.

sec11-card-sec11-F019.question_text: Where is tossing trash or litter illegal under Rhode Island law?
sec11-card-sec11-F019.teaching_text: Roadside debris punctures tires, clogs storm drains, and breaks state law on both public and private land.

sec11-card-sec11-F020.question_text: What dollar fine range does the Rhode Island manual list for littering violations?
sec11-card-sec11-F020.teaching_text: Tossing a cup or wrapper out a car window can cost anywhere from eighty-five up to a thousand dollars.

sec11-card-sec11-F021.question_text: How should you adjust speed and noise when approaching a ridden or drawn horse on a public road?
sec11-card-sec11-F021.teaching_text: Honking or revving an engine can spook a horse into bolting sideways directly into traffic lanes.

sec11-card-sec11-F022.question_text: May you wear earphones or a headset while driving a motor vehicle on a public highway?
sec11-card-sec11-F022.teaching_text: Covering your ears blocks approaching ambulance sirens, train horns, and screeching tires until too late.

sec11-card-sec11-F023.question_text: Which three items must you show a police officer upon request during a traffic stop?
sec11-card-sec11-F023.teaching_text: Having your license, registration, and active insurance card organized keeps roadside enforcement stops brief and calm.

sec11-card-sec11-F024.question_text: What signature check may an officer require in person to verify your identity during a stop?
sec11-card-sec11-F024.teaching_text: Comparing a live signature against the signature printed on your license helps officers spot borrowed or altered cards.

sec11-card-sec11-F025.question_text: What must you do when a police officer orders you to step out of the car?
sec11-card-sec11-F025.teaching_text: While you normally stay belted inside, a lawful order from an officer to step out requires prompt compliance.

sec11-card-sec11-F026.question_text: What cabin lighting step applies during a nighttime traffic stop, and how long does it stay on?
sec11-card-sec11-F026.teaching_text: Illuminating the cabin from arrival until release lets the officer see hands clearly in the dark.

sec11-card-sec11-F027.question_text: Because traffic laws can change over time, what ongoing responsibility stays on every driver?
sec11-card-sec11-F027.teaching_text: Staying current on updated Rhode Island statutes keeps you accountable for the safety of everyone riding aboard.

sec11-card-sec11-F028.question_text: Why can actual ticket amounts differ from the common-violation fine table printed in the manual?
sec11-card-sec11-F028.teaching_text: State lawmakers periodically revise penalty schedules, so statutory updates override static numbers printed in study guides.

sec13-card-sec13-F001.question_text: What are the very first two things you should do right after any collision?
sec13-card-sec13-F001.teaching_text: Stopping right away keeps you compliant with state law while calm breathing helps you spot traffic and injury hazards.

sec13-card-sec13-F002.question_text: After stopping at a collision scene, what must you share with everyone who has a stake in the crash?
sec13-card-sec13-F002.teaching_text: Every involved driver, passenger, or property owner has a legal right to your true identity before anyone leaves.

sec13-card-sec13-F003.question_text: What risk do you run by leaving a collision scene without properly identifying yourself?
sec13-card-sec13-F003.teaching_text: Panicking and driving off turns even a minor scrape into a serious hit-and-run offense with heavy penalties.

sec13-card-sec13-F004.question_text: Which law-enforcement agencies does the Rhode Island manual direct drivers to notify immediately after a collision?
sec13-card-sec13-F004.teaching_text: Alerting the closest municipal department or State Police barracks gets traffic control and official documentation rolling fast.

sec13-card-sec13-F005.question_text: When must you request emergency rescue assistance at a crash scene?
sec13-card-sec13-F005.teaching_text: Getting trained paramedics rolling immediately protects crash victims whose internal or head injuries may worsen rapidly.

sec13-card-sec13-F006.question_text: After a minor crash where the car still drives safely, where should you position it while calling police?
sec13-card-sec13-F006.teaching_text: Clearing drivable vehicles out of active travel lanes prevents fast-approaching traffic from piling into the wreck.

sec13-card-sec13-F007.question_text: If you bump an empty parked car or other unattended property, what written notice must you leave?
sec13-card-sec13-F007.teaching_text: Fastening your name and address securely where the returning owner will spot it prevents an unattended hit-and-run charge.

sec13-card-sec13-F008.question_text: Beyond leaving a note on damaged unattended property, whom else must you notify promptly?
sec13-card-sec13-F008.teaching_text: Wind or rain can blow a windshield note away, so prompt police notification protects you with an official timestamp.

sec13-card-sec13-F009.question_text: Besides any bodily injury, what property-damage threshold requires a formal police report?
sec13-card-sec13-F009.teaching_text: Modern bumper sensors and paintwork easily top one thousand dollars, making police reports mandatory on most collisions.

sec13-card-sec13-F010.question_text: Does colliding with an unattended parked vehicle require a police report?
sec13-card-sec13-F010.teaching_text: Even low-speed parking-lot scrapes against an empty vehicle require filing a police report alongside leaving your note.

sec13-card-sec13-F011.question_text: What reporting duty applies if your vehicle strikes a domesticated animal?
sec13-card-sec13-F011.teaching_text: Dogs, cats, and livestock are someone's cared-for animals and property, so striking one legally requires notifying police.

sec13-card-sec13-F012.question_text: What roadway details should you write down to document where a collision happened?
sec13-card-sec13-F012.teaching_text: Exact cross-streets and lane positions anchor insurance diagrams and police reconstructions weeks after the scene clears.

sec13-card-sec13-F013.question_text: When cross-streets are far apart, which three fixed references help pinpoint a crash site?
sec13-card-sec13-F013.teaching_text: Noting a highway mile marker or nearest house number tells dispatchers and insurers the exact stretch of road.

sec13-card-sec13-F014.question_text: What time detail should you record right after a collision occurs?
sec13-card-sec13-F014.teaching_text: Exact timestamps match traffic-camera footage, sun angles, and weather records when fault disputes arise.

sec13-card-sec13-F015.question_text: Which three personal and credential details should you exchange with the other driver?
sec13-card-sec13-F015.teaching_text: Verifying the other operator's full name, home address, and driver-license number prevents dead-end phone numbers later.

sec13-card-sec13-F016.question_text: Which two insurance facts must you write down from the other driver?
sec13-card-sec13-F016.teaching_text: Both the insurance company's name and the exact policy number are needed to open a third-party damage claim.

sec13-card-sec13-F017.question_text: Which two vehicle-registration details should you log for the other car?
sec13-card-sec13-F017.teaching_text: Plate numbers repeat across state borders, so writing down the issuing state alongside the registration number avoids mix-ups.

sec13-card-sec13-F018.question_text: Who at a two-car collision has the right to receive identifying and vehicle details?
sec13-card-sec13-F018.teaching_text: Information exchange is a two-way street regardless of who thinks the other person caused the collision.

sec13-card-sec13-F019.question_text: Besides the other driver, which two groups should you gather names and addresses from?
sec13-card-sec13-F019.teaching_text: Independent witnesses and passengers inside the other vehicle provide crucial accounts if stories change afterward.

sec13-card-sec13-F020.question_text: What detail should you jot down about law enforcement responding to your collision?
sec13-card-sec13-F020.teaching_text: Knowing the investigating officer's name makes retrieving the official crash report from the department straightforward.

sec13-card-sec13-F021.question_text: What physical outcomes of the crash should you write down specifically before leaving?
sec13-card-sec13-F021.teaching_text: Specific notes on fresh dents, broken glass, and reported injuries stop unrelated pre-existing damage from being added later.

sec13-card-sec13-F022.question_text: Which two speed-related errors frequently contribute to roadway collisions?
sec13-card-sec13-F022.teaching_text: Even driving below the posted sign causes crashes when rain, snow, or traffic calls for much slower speeds.

sec13-card-sec13-F023.question_text: Alongside alcohol or drug impairment, what modern cabin habit ranks as a major crash contributor?
sec13-card-sec13-F023.teaching_text: Glancing down at a phone blinds a driver for hundreds of feet, rivaling chemical impairment as a crash trigger.

sec13-card-sec13-F024.question_text: Which three spacing, lane-keeping, or curb-departure mistakes commonly trigger crashes?
sec13-card-sec13-F024.teaching_text: Following too closely, crossing centerlines, or pulling away from a curb without checking mirrors leaves zero margin.

sec13-card-sec13-F025.question_text: What intersection or merge rule violation commonly causes collisions?
sec13-card-sec13-F025.teaching_text: Pushing through intersections, crosswalks, or highway merges when another road user holds right-of-way sparks angle crashes.

sec13-card-sec13-F026.question_text: Beyond driver error, what vehicle condition and four road-surface hazards contribute to collisions?
sec13-card-sec13-F026.teaching_text: Bald tires or worn brakes combined with work zones, loose gravel, sand, or potholes stretch stopping distances unexpectedly.

sec13-card-sec13-F027.question_text: What crime classification applies to failing to stop after a crash that injures or kills someone?
sec13-card-sec13-F027.teaching_text: Fleeing a crash where anyone is hurt or killed elevates a traffic incident into a serious felony prosecution.

sec13-card-sec13-F028.question_text: What legal step is required for stopping-duty violations involving vehicle, parked-car, or highway-fixture damage?
sec13-card-sec13-F028.teaching_text: You cannot simply mail in a fine after failing to stop for damaged vehicles, parked cars, or guardrails—court is mandatory.

sec14-card-sec14-F001.question_text: At a nighttime traffic stop, what interior lighting step must you take—and when may you turn it off?
sec14-card-sec14-F001.teaching_text: Brightening the cabin immediately lets the approaching officer see every occupant's hands clearly in the dark.

sec14-card-sec14-F002.question_text: Should you leave your headlights on or switch them off during a nighttime traffic stop?
sec14-card-sec14-F002.teaching_text: Keeping exterior lamps illuminated makes your stopped vehicle visible to traffic and lights the roadside shoulder.

sec14-card-sec14-F003.question_text: When police emergency lights or a siren signal you to pull over, where should you stop?
sec14-card-sec14-F003.teaching_text: Guiding smoothly to a safe spot on the right keeps the stop clear of fast-moving left-hand lanes.

sec14-card-sec14-F004.question_text: How should you signal, brake, and position your car as you pull over for an officer?
sec14-card-sec14-F004.teaching_text: Signaling right and easing speed down smoothly avoids sudden braking right in front of the trailing cruiser.

sec14-card-sec14-F005.question_text: Which two spots should you avoid blocking when choosing where to stop for police?
sec14-card-sec14-F005.teaching_text: Stopping clear of active lanes and private driveways keeps passing cars and residents moving without hazards.

sec14-card-sec14-F006.question_text: Once safely parked on the shoulder, what two vehicle steps prepare for the officer's walk-up?
sec14-card-sec14-F006.teaching_text: Turning off the motor shows you are staying put while an open window lets you speak clearly right away.

sec14-card-sec14-F007.question_text: When may you unbuckle your safety belt during a law-enforcement traffic stop?
sec14-card-sec14-F007.teaching_text: Unbuckling as the officer walks up looks like preparing to bolt or reach, and removes crash protection if rear-ended.

sec14-card-sec14-F008.question_text: Where should the driver rest both hands as the officer walks toward the vehicle?
sec14-card-sec14-F008.teaching_text: Resting both hands atop the steering wheel in plain sight immediately lowers roadside tension.

sec14-card-sec14-F009.question_text: What should you ask your passengers to do with their hands during a traffic stop?
sec14-card-sec14-F009.teaching_text: Officers watch every occupant inside the cabin, so visible passenger hands keep the entire stop calm.

sec14-card-sec14-F010.question_text: Should you stay inside your car during a traffic stop unless asked to step out?
sec14-card-sec14-F010.teaching_text: Staying seated protects you from passing traffic and avoids startling the approaching officer.

sec14-card-sec14-F011.question_text: Should you grab your paperwork while the officer walks up, or wait for instructions first?
sec14-card-sec14-F011.teaching_text: Rummaging in pockets or consoles as an officer approaches mimics reaching for a weapon; wait until asked.

sec14-card-sec14-F012.question_text: Which three sudden or hidden movements must a driver avoid during an enforcement stop?
sec14-card-sec14-F012.teaching_text: Dipping beneath seats or lunging toward the glove compartment raises immediate officer-safety alarm.

sec14-card-sec14-F013.question_text: How should passengers behave physically while the officer approaches or speaks with the driver?
sec14-card-sec14-F013.teaching_text: Sudden twists or reaches from back-seat or front-seat riders distract the officer and escalate tension needlessly.

sec14-card-sec14-F014.question_text: Which three documents must you carry on you or in the car whenever driving?
sec14-card-sec14-F014.teaching_text: Keeping your personal license plus vehicle registration and insurance proof aboard prevents avoidable citations.

sec14-card-sec14-F015.question_text: When is the right moment to present your license, registration, or insurance proof?
sec14-card-sec14-F015.teaching_text: Letting the officer greet you and state what they need keeps every hand movement expected and transparent.

sec14-card-sec14-F016.question_text: How should you prepare a license or registration card stored inside a wallet sleeve before handing it over?
sec14-card-sec14-F016.teaching_text: Handing over a loose card lets the officer inspect both sides cleanly without handling your personal wallet.

sec14-card-sec14-F017.question_text: Does Rhode Island allow showing electronic proof of insurance on a device during a traffic stop?
sec14-card-sec14-F017.teaching_text: Pulling up your insurer's digital ID card satisfies Rhode Island's proof-of-insurance requirement once requested.

sec14-card-sec14-F018.question_text: What should you do when the officer walks back to the cruiser with your documents?
sec14-card-sec14-F018.teaching_text: Walking back toward the patrol cruiser uninvited creates an immediate safety confrontation on the shoulder.

sec14-card-sec14-F019.question_text: When does the document-check phase of a traffic stop finish?
sec14-card-sec14-F019.teaching_text: Patience while dispatch runs plates and credentials ensures you never pull out prematurely without your cards.

sec14-card-sec14-F020.question_text: Does signing a traffic citation admit guilt to the violation listed on it?
sec14-card-sec14-F020.teaching_text: Your signature simply confirms you received the notice; you keep every right to contest the ticket in court.

sec14-card-sec14-F021.question_text: Does arguing or refusing to sign a citation change the outcome of the roadside traffic stop?
sec14-card-sec14-F021.teaching_text: Roadside shoulders are never courtrooms; disputes belong before a judge rather than debating on the curb.

sec14-card-sec14-F022.question_text: Why is selecting people for stops, searches, or seizures based solely on race, ethnicity, or national origin barred?
sec14-card-sec14-F022.teaching_text: Lawful enforcement actions must rest on observed conduct or evidence, never a person's race, ethnicity, or origin.

sec14-card-sec14-F023.question_text: Which three public institutions lose community trust when racial profiling occurs?
sec14-card-sec14-F023.teaching_text: Fair, equal treatment at roadside stops sustains public confidence across policing, courtrooms, and the wider justice system.
sec14-card-sec14-F023.must_match_memory_hook: Erodes trust in police, courts, justice

visual_sync.text_span: Erodes trust in police, courts, justice

sec14-card-sec14-F024.question_text: Which named Rhode Island Act provides statutory details on anti-profiling protections?
sec14-card-sec14-F024.teaching_text: State lawmakers enacted that statutory framework to spell out equal-treatment rules and citizen rights during stops.

sec15-card-sec15-F001.question_text: What ongoing vehicle-condition and equipment duties does Rhode Island law place on every driver?
sec15-card-sec15-F001.teaching_text: Driving with neglected safety gear invites mechanical failures on rainy highways and instant equipment citations.

sec15-card-sec15-F002.question_text: Which cabin surfaces do lap and shoulder belts help stop occupants from hitting in a crash?
sec15-card-sec15-F002.teaching_text: Even a thirty-mile-per-hour sudden stop hurls unbuckled riders forward into hard cabin surfaces violently.

sec15-card-sec15-F003.question_text: Beyond cabin impacts, how else do safety belts protect someone during a violent collision?
sec15-card-sec15-F003.teaching_text: Being thrown through glass onto pavement during a rollover multiplies fatal injury risk dramatically.

sec15-card-sec15-F004.question_text: Are airbags standalone restraints, or how are they designed to protect occupants?
sec15-card-sec15-F004.teaching_text: Without a buckled seat belt holding your torso aligned, an unrestrained rider slides straight into deploying force.

sec15-card-sec15-F005.question_text: Where should infants and children sit in any vehicle equipped with passenger-side airbags?
sec15-card-sec15-F005.teaching_text: Front passenger airbags inflate at explosive speed engineered for adult chests, endangering small frames up front.

sec15-card-sec15-F006.question_text: What seat adjustment may a driver need to stay safe from a deploying steering-wheel airbag?
sec15-card-sec15-F006.teaching_text: Sitting right against the steering hub puts your chest inside the airbag's high-force inflation zone.

sec15-card-sec15-F007.question_text: Below what minimum tread depth does the Rhode Island handbook prohibit driving on a tire?
sec15-card-sec15-F007.teaching_text: Bald tires under two thirty-seconds cannot channel standing rainwater away, causing sudden highway hydroplaning.

sec15-card-sec15-F008.question_text: Which two tire construction types must never be mixed on the same vehicle?
sec15-card-sec15-F008.teaching_text: Radial and bias sidewalls flex differently in corners, creating unpredictable handling and wet-road spinouts.

sec15-card-sec15-F009.question_text: Which guide should you check to find maintenance intervals for your tires and vehicle systems?
sec15-card-sec15-F009.teaching_text: Factory engineers print exact rotation miles, fluid specs, and service intervals right inside the glovebox book.

sec15-card-sec15-F010.question_text: Under what tire temperature condition should you measure air pressure for an accurate reading?
sec15-card-sec15-F010.teaching_text: Highway friction heats trapped air and raises PSI temporarily, masking an underinflated tire if checked warm.

sec15-card-sec15-F011.question_text: What dangerous procrastination mistake with brake repairs does the handbook warn against?
sec15-card-sec15-F011.teaching_text: By the time a brake pedal sinks to the floorboard, hydraulic stopping power can vanish mid-traffic.

sec15-card-sec15-F012.question_text: Which two brake feel symptoms call for checking maintenance steps in the owner's manual?
sec15-card-sec15-F012.teaching_text: Uneven caliper grip yanks your car toward adjacent lanes while air in lines makes pedals mushy.

sec15-card-sec15-F013.question_text: Why must your vehicle's parking brake stay in proper working order?
sec15-card-sec15-F013.teaching_text: A crisp mechanical parking brake holds parked cars securely on steep coastal or downtown hills.

sec15-card-sec15-F014.question_text: What mechanical slack should never appear when you turn the steering wheel?
sec15-card-sec15-F014.teaching_text: Worn tie rods or steering joints create dead-zone slop that delays emergency lane swerves.

sec15-card-sec15-F015.question_text: What fluid check may be needed if your car makes noise while steering?
sec15-card-sec15-F015.teaching_text: Groaning or whining pumps often signal low power-steering fluid before heavy steering assist cuts out.

sec15-card-sec15-F016.question_text: Which three primary exterior light groups should you inspect to confirm they work?
sec15-card-sec15-F016.teaching_text: Burned-out blinkers or dark taillights leave trailing drivers guessing in rain and night traffic.

sec15-card-sec15-F017.question_text: Which four additional exterior lamp types also require operational checks?
sec15-card-sec15-F017.teaching_text: Dead brake lamps hide sudden highway slowdowns while out reverse bulbs leave pedestrians unwarned in lots.

sec15-card-sec15-F018.question_text: Which interior illumination belongs in your routine vehicle lighting inspection?
sec15-card-sec15-F018.teaching_text: A dark speedometer cluster at night hides both creeping highway speeds and warning gauges.

sec15-card-sec15-F019.question_text: What three winter or road coatings should you wipe off exterior lamps during inspection?
sec15-card-sec15-F019.teaching_text: Dried New England salt crust can cut headlight reach and brake-light brightness in half.

sec15-card-sec15-F020.question_text: Why is a helper useful when inspecting all of your vehicle's exterior lights?
sec15-card-sec15-F020.teaching_text: Brake and reverse lamps only light up while someone holds the pedal down from the driver seat.

sec15-card-sec15-F021.question_text: How can snow, ice, or salty road grime affect advanced vehicle safety systems?
sec15-card-sec15-F021.teaching_text: Slush packed over bumper radar or windshield cameras blinds automatic braking and blind-spot alerts.

sec15-card-sec15-F022.question_text: What two habits should drivers practice regarding their vehicle's safety sensors?
sec15-card-sec15-F022.teaching_text: Knowing where cameras and radar pods sit lets you clear winter slush before hitting the interstate.

sec15-card-sec15-F023.question_text: Which four additional sight, sound, and exhaust components require regular maintenance?
sec15-card-sec15-F023.teaching_text: Streaking wiper blades or a leaky exhaust muffler creates blind downpours or cabin fume hazards.

sec15-card-sec15-F024.question_text: Which three brake-related issues can instrument-panel warnings flag?
sec15-card-sec15-F024.teaching_text: Ignoring a glowing brake warning risks worn pads grinding rotors or low hydraulic fluid failing.

sec15-card-sec15-F025.question_text: Which two electronic grip-and-braking systems may have separate dashboard indicator lights?
sec15-card-sec15-F025.teaching_text: A steady ABS or stability light means electronic skid assist is offline even if normal brakes work.

sec15-card-sec15-F026.question_text: What three-letter label may mark an airbag warning light, and what do those letters stand for?
sec15-card-sec15-F026.teaching_text: A lit SRS icon warns that airbags or belt pretensioners may fail to fire in a wreck.

sec15-card-sec15-F027.question_text: Which four critical lubrication, electrical, and heat warnings can appear on the dashboard?
sec15-card-sec15-F027.teaching_text: Driving past an oil-pressure or overheating alert can seize an engine or transmission within miles.

sec15-card-sec15-F028.question_text: List four engine, fuel, temperature, and tire indicators commonly found on the instrument panel?
sec15-card-sec15-F028.teaching_text: Spotting a tire-pressure or check-engine icon early turns a roadside breakdown into a routine check.

sec15-card-sec15-F029.question_text: Which four washer, door, bulb, and belt alerts may also appear on the dashboard?
sec15-card-sec15-F029.teaching_text: Running out of washer fluid during salty slush blinds your windshield in seconds behind trucks.
sec15-card-sec15-F029.must_match_memory_hook: Washer supply, ajar door, bulb, belt

visual_sync.text_span: Washer supply, ajar door, bulb, belt

sec15-card-sec15-F030.question_text: Which three signaling and headlamp status indicators can appear on the instrument panel?
sec15-card-sec15-F030.teaching_text: Glancing for the blue high-beam telltale stops you from accidentally blinding oncoming traffic at night.

sec16-card-sec16-F001.question_text: What opportunity does Rhode Island's organ-and-tissue donor program offer a driver-license applicant?
sec16-card-sec16-F001.teaching_text: Putting your choice on file during licensing removes uncertainty when seconds count for transplant teams.

sec16-card-sec16-F002.question_text: Can a person's race ever bar them from consideration as an organ or tissue donor?
sec16-card-sec16-F002.teaching_text: Every background needs life-saving matches, so nobody is ruled out from registering based on race.

sec16-card-sec16-F003.question_text: Does having a medical history automatically disqualify someone from potential donor consideration?
sec16-card-sec16-F003.teaching_text: Doctors evaluate organ and tissue suitability individually at the time rather than rejecting past conditions upfront.

sec16-card-sec16-F004.question_text: What extra authorization is required if someone younger than eighteen wants to register as a donor?
sec16-card-sec16-F004.teaching_text: Teens getting their first Rhode Island permit or license discuss and confirm consent with a parent.

sec16-card-sec16-F005.question_text: What financial fee or charge applies to a person or family for making an organ or tissue donation?
sec16-card-sec16-F005.teaching_text: Clearing up the cost myth reassures families that donation never adds medical bills to loved ones.

sec16-card-sec16-F006.question_text: What does the Rhode Island handbook state about how major religions view organ and tissue donation?
sec16-card-sec16-F006.teaching_text: Faith traditions widely embrace saving another person's life as an act of generosity and compassion.

sec16-card-sec16-F007.question_text: Does carrying a signed donor card reduce the quality of medical care if you get sick or injured?
sec16-card-sec16-F007.teaching_text: Emergency physicians treat every patient aggressively without letting donor cards influence life-saving treatment.

sec16-card-sec16-F008.question_text: Does having a donor designation printed on your driver license alter the medical care you receive?
sec16-card-sec16-F008.teaching_text: Trauma crews focus strictly on emergency stabilization long before transplant coordinators are ever contacted.

sec16-card-sec16-F009.question_text: When a sick or injured patient arrives at a hospital, what remains the health provider's first priority?
sec16-card-sec16-F009.teaching_text: Hospital care teams are legally and ethically dedicated to preserving every arriving patient's life.

sec16-card-sec16-F010.question_text: Which laboratory compatibility check is listed first among factors used to allocate a transplant?
sec16-card-sec16-F010.teaching_text: Compatible blood types prevent immediate immune rejection once a donated organ reaches a recipient.

sec16-card-sec16-F011.question_text: What physical dimension check helps match a donated organ to a transplant recipient?
sec16-card-sec16-F011.teaching_text: Hearts, lungs, and livers must physically fit the recipient's chest or abdominal cavity properly.

sec16-card-sec16-F012.question_text: How does the severity of a patient's condition factor into transplant allocation?
sec16-card-sec16-F012.teaching_text: Patients facing immediate organ failure move up allocation priority based on objective medical urgency.

sec16-card-sec16-F013.question_text: Alongside medical factors, how does waiting-list duration count in transplant allocation?
sec16-card-sec16-F013.teaching_text: Factoring in waiting-list duration keeps organ allocation fair and transparent between medically matched transplant candidates.

sec16-card-sec16-F014.question_text: Does organ or tissue donation prevent a family's funeral or burial arrangements from going forward?
sec16-card-sec16-F014.teaching_text: Surgical recovery treats donors with dignity so traditional family services continue uninterrupted.

sec16-card-sec16-F015.question_text: How can you record a donation choice directly through the Rhode Island DMV?
sec16-card-sec16-F015.teaching_text: Printing the designation right on your driver license keeps your wish visible in your wallet.

sec16-card-sec16-F016.question_text: Besides a driver-license mark, what written document can record your decision to donate organs or tissue?
sec16-card-sec16-F016.teaching_text: A signed donor card lets even non-drivers or permit holders document their wishes clearly.

sec16-card-sec16-F017.question_text: What should you do with a donor card after signing it?
sec16-card-sec16-F017.teaching_text: Leaving a signed donor card tucked inside a desk drawer at home hides it when needed.

sec16-card-sec16-F018.question_text: Which regional organization does the Rhode Island handbook name as a source for getting a donor card?
sec16-card-sec16-F018.teaching_text: Regional organ recovery organizations distribute official cards and educational answers across New England.

sec16-card-sec16-F019.question_text: Who should you talk to in addition to marking your driver license or signing a donor card?
sec16-card-sec16-F019.teaching_text: Sharing your decision ahead of time spares grieving relatives from surprise or doubt at the hospital.

sec17-card-sec17-F001.question_text: When does Rhode Island allow window films or tint treatments on a vehicle?
sec17-card-sec17-F001.teaching_text: Unapproved dark aftermarket tint blocks eye contact at intersections and draws inspection rejections.

sec17-card-sec17-F002.question_text: Which four window areas on a vehicle are covered by Rhode Island's window-treatment rule?
sec17-card-sec17-F002.teaching_text: Unlike states that exempt back glass, Rhode Island's rule spans front, second-row, and rear windows.

sec17-card-sec17-F003.question_text: What minimum percentage of total visible light must pass through regulated vehicle glazing in Rhode Island?
sec17-card-sec17-F003.teaching_text: Factory glass already absorbs some light, so dark stick-on film drops below seventy percent fast.

sec17-card-sec17-F004.question_text: What fine amount does the Rhode Island handbook list for a window-treatment violation?
sec17-card-sec17-F004.teaching_text: Paying two hundred fifty dollars plus peeling off dark film costs far more than keeping legal glass.

sec17-card-sec17-F005.question_text: For vehicles rated up to ten thousand pounds gross weight, what maximum height change from factory spec is allowed?
sec17-card-sec17-F005.teaching_text: Extreme lifts or drops misalign bumper crash zones and headlight aim on everyday pickups and cars.

sec17-card-sec17-F006.question_text: Which modification methods count toward Rhode Island's four-inch lift-or-lower limit?
sec17-card-sec17-F006.teaching_text: Swapping oversized mud tires plus a small lift kit adds together against the four-inch cap.

sec17-card-sec17-F007.question_text: At what distance from the lane center and under what driving condition are Rhode Island vehicle-noise limits measured?
sec17-card-sec17-F007.teaching_text: Standardizing microphone placement at fifty feet prevents guesswork when testing loud exhaust pipes.

sec17-card-sec17-F008.question_text: What acoustic scale and instrument does the Rhode Island handbook specify for vehicle-noise limits?
sec17-card-sec17-F008.teaching_text: A-weighting matches human ear sensitivity so loud aftermarket mufflers get measured objectively.

sec17-card-sec17-F009.question_text: What maximum vehicle-noise limit applies where the posted speed is thirty-five or lower?
sec17-card-sec17-F009.teaching_text: Residential neighborhoods and downtown blocks at thirty-five or lower cap exhaust noise tighter.

sec17-card-sec17-F010.question_text: In speed zones above thirty-five miles per hour, what maximum vehicle-noise limit applies?
sec17-card-sec17-F010.teaching_text: Faster highways generate extra tire roar, raising the legal ceiling slightly to ninety decibels.

sec17-card-sec17-F011.question_text: Alongside the driver at the wheel, who else is barred from allowing a car to exceed noise limits?
sec17-card-sec17-F011.teaching_text: Lending a straight-piped car to a friend can still bring legal trouble back to the registered owner.

sec17-card-sec17-F012.question_text: Beyond statewide decibel caps, who else may enforce additional vehicle-noise rules?
sec17-card-sec17-F012.teaching_text: Local beach towns and dense neighborhoods often enforce strict municipal quiet ordinances.

sec17-card-sec17-F013.question_text: What does the multiple-beam lighting rule require, and which two-wheeled vehicles are excluded from that quote?
sec17-card-sec17-F013.teaching_text: Cars switch between high and low beam elevations to balance rural reach against oncoming glare.

sec17-card-sec17-F014.question_text: What authority does the Rhode Island DMV Administrator hold over vehicle lighting devices?
sec17-card-sec17-F014.teaching_text: Unapproved off-road light bars or misaimed LEDs dazzle traffic and violate DMV equipment rules.

sec17-card-sec17-F015.question_text: With which professional engineering organization's standards are Rhode Island's lighting rules aligned?
sec17-card-sec17-F015.teaching_text: Matching SAE optical benchmarks ensures legal replacement bulbs project clean, predictable beam cutoffs.

sec17-card-sec17-F016.question_text: What three mindset habits do work zones demand since hazards vary from site to site?
sec17-card-sec17-F016.teaching_text: Yesterday's smooth shoulder work can shift overnight into a narrow concrete chute.

sec17-card-sec17-F017.question_text: At which three stages of a construction project may work-zone warning signs appear?
sec17-card-sec17-F017.teaching_text: End-Work signs confirm when normal lane rules resume after advance and in-zone alerts.

sec17-card-sec17-F018.question_text: Which three high-visibility colors and two shapes appear on work-zone signs in the Rhode Island handbook?
sec17-card-sec17-F018.teaching_text: Fluorescent pink incident signs and orange construction boards cut straight through rain and dusk.

sec17-card-sec17-F019.question_text: Which three common road changes can work-zone signs warn drivers about ahead?
sec17-card-sec17-F019.teaching_text: Spotting an Uneven Pavement diamond early stops grooved asphalt edges from jerking your steering.

sec17-card-sec17-F020.question_text: During how many hours of the day are speeding fines doubled in designated Rhode Island work zones?
sec17-card-sec17-F020.teaching_text: Narrowed barriers and milled drop-offs remain hazardous at midnight even if crews pause briefly.

sec17-card-sec17-F021.question_text: Which two driver errors are major contributors to work-zone crashes?
sec17-card-sec17-F021.teaching_text: Looking down for two seconds at highway pace slams you straight into stopped work-zone queues.

sec17-card-sec17-F022.question_text: Which three in-car distractions should you avoid while driving through a work zone?
sec17-card-sec17-F022.teaching_text: Tight concrete barriers leave inches of mirror clearance where one glance at a playlist scrapes walls.

sec17-card-sec17-F023.question_text: Whose live directions must you obey alongside merge signs in a work zone?
sec17-card-sec17-F023.teaching_text: Detail troopers and flaggers halt lanes on short notice whenever heavy loaders swing across traffic.

sec17-card-sec17-F024.question_text: Do work-zone flaggers hold legal authority to slow or stop you with hand signals or signs?
sec17-card-sec17-F024.teaching_text: Ignoring a flagger's STOP paddle carries the legal weight of running an official traffic control.

sec17-card-sec17-F025.question_text: What does the Rhode Island handbook instruct regarding changing lanes once inside a work zone?
sec17-card-sec17-F025.teaching_text: Weaving between narrowed cones surprises drivers watching workers and clips uneven lane seams.

sec17-card-sec17-F026.question_text: For whom and what must you stay alert inside work zones, including after dark?
sec17-card-sec17-F026.teaching_text: Rhode Island schedules major highway paving overnight, putting crews beside glare-lit travel lanes.

sec17-card-sec17-F027.question_text: Why must you anticipate sudden surprises every time you enter a construction area?
sec17-card-sec17-F027.teaching_text: Traffic patterns on your evening commute can shift to the opposite shoulder from morning setup.

sec17-card-sec17-F028.question_text: Why is extra following distance critical inside construction zones?
sec17-card-sec17-F028.teaching_text: One abrupt flagger stop ripples backward instantly, catching tailgaters with nowhere to steer.

sec17-card-sec17-F029.question_text: When should you merge into the open lane approaching a work-zone closure?
sec17-card-sec17-F029.teaching_text: Moving over smoothly at the first sign avoids pinch-point standoffs right at the barrels.

sec17-card-sec17-F030.question_text: List the roadside channeling devices, boards, and paint used to guide traffic through work zones?
sec17-card-sec17-F030.teaching_text: Following temporary orange barrels, tubes, panels, and arrow boards keeps you out of live trenches.

sec17-card-sec17-F031.question_text: Whom should a student contact to replace a lost CCRI driver-education completion certificate?
sec17-card-sec17-F031.teaching_text: CCRI maintains official completion records directly rather than the local DMV counter.

sec17-card-sec17-F032.question_text: Where do you request a replacement certificate if you finished driver ed at another authorized Rhode Island school?
sec17-card-sec17-F032.teaching_text: Each authorized driving school issues duplicate completion certificates for its own graduates.

sec18-card-sec18-F001.question_text: Which two core right-of-way signs lead the regulatory sign reference in the Rhode Island handbook?
sec18-card-sec18-F001.teaching_text: Both red-and-white regulatory shapes assign legal intersection priority rather than optional advice.

sec18-card-sec18-F002.question_text: Which two regulatory signs warn against entering or continuing down a road in the wrong direction?
sec18-card-sec18-F002.teaching_text: Spotting either red rectangle on a ramp demands an immediate safe stop before head-on traffic arrives.

sec18-card-sec18-F003.question_text: How does a No Left Turn regulatory sign differ from a curve warning?
sec18-card-sec18-F003.teaching_text: Confusing a slashed left arrow with a bend warning causes illegal turns into one-way streets.

sec18-card-sec18-F004.question_text: What maneuver is outlawed where a No U-Turn regulatory sign stands?
sec18-card-sec18-F004.teaching_text: Tight intersections and blind medians post U-turn bans where reversing direction stalls cross traffic.

sec18-card-sec18-F005.question_text: What legal restriction does a No Parking regulatory sign enforce?
sec18-card-sec18-F005.teaching_text: No Parking zones preserve fire lanes, snow-emergency routes, and clear corner sightlines.

sec18-card-sec18-F006.question_text: Which class of traffic is barred by a No Trucks regulatory sign?
sec18-card-sec18-F006.teaching_text: Weight-limited bridges and narrow historic streets exclude commercial trucks to prevent damage.

sec18-card-sec18-F007.question_text: Which regulatory sign in the reference restricts overtaking other vehicles?
sec18-card-sec18-F007.teaching_text: Blind hillcrests, curves, and busy intersections hide oncoming headlights until passing becomes completely impossible.

sec18-card-sec18-F008.question_text: What rule does a One Way regulatory sign set for every vehicle on that street?
sec18-card-sec18-F008.teaching_text: Checking horizontal One Way arrows before turning downtown keeps you from pointing against all lanes.

sec18-card-sec18-F009.question_text: Which regulatory sign sets the posted driving-speed restriction on a roadway?
sec18-card-sec18-F009.teaching_text: White Speed Limit rectangles post enforceable ceilings unlike yellow curve advisory plaques.

sec18-card-sec18-F010.question_text: Where does a Keep Right regulatory sign direct approaching traffic to steer?
sec18-card-sec18-F010.teaching_text: Steering right of median noses and islands keeps you clear of opposing lanes.

sec18-card-sec18-F011.question_text: When does a No Right Turn On Red sign forbid turning right?
sec18-card-sec18-F011.teaching_text: Heavy crosswalks and blind cross-street angles make red-light right turns unsafe at signed corners.

sec18-card-sec18-F012.question_text: What must every driver in a lane marked Right Turn Only do at the intersection?
sec18-card-sec18-F012.teaching_text: Driving straight out of a dedicated turn pocket sideswipes through traffic beside you.

sec18-card-sec18-F013.question_text: Which two movements are allowed by a Right or Straight lane sign, and which turn is barred?
sec18-card-sec18-F013.teaching_text: Multi-movement lane signs keep left-turn queues separate from faster curb-side straight and right-turning traffic.

sec18-card-sec18-F014.question_text: Which two movements are permitted by a Left or Straight lane sign, and which turn is barred?
sec18-card-sec18-F014.teaching_text: Turning right across an adjacent right-side lane from a left-straight lane causes instant T-bones.

sec18-card-sec18-F015.question_text: Under which sign category do Restricted Lane and Lane Restrictions appear in the Rhode Island reference?
sec18-card-sec18-F015.teaching_text: White diamond and lane-restriction panels carry enforceable legal penalties for unauthorized cars.

sec18-card-sec18-F016.question_text: Which three freeway navigation details do guide signs identify in the sign reference?
sec18-card-sec18-F016.teaching_text: Reading overhead exit boards early lets you position smoothly without last-second gore cuts.

sec18-card-sec18-F017.question_text: What purpose does a Mile Marker guide sign serve along a highway?
sec18-card-sec18-F017.teaching_text: Giving a 911 dispatcher the nearest green milepost brings roadside help straight to your car.

sec18-card-sec18-F018.question_text: How are Telephone and Hotels classified in the Rhode Island sign reference?
sec18-card-sec18-F018.teaching_text: Blue motorist-service panels point highway travelers cleanly toward nearby off-exit lodging and communication stops.

sec18-card-sec18-F019.question_text: Which two additional motorist-service destinations appear in the guide-sign reference?
sec18-card-sec18-F019.teaching_text: Blue Hospital H shields guide drivers directly toward emergency medical care in unfamiliar towns.

sec18-card-sec18-F020.question_text: How does the Rhode Island sign reference classify a Tourist Attraction sign?
sec18-card-sec18-F020.teaching_text: Advance cultural and coastal attraction signs help visitors exit cleanly without sudden braking.

sec18-card-sec18-F021.question_text: Which three highway numbering systems have route shields in the Rhode Island guide-sign reference?
sec18-card-sec18-F021.teaching_text: Distinguishing federal, state, and interstate shield outlines keeps navigation clear at interchanges.

sec18-card-sec18-F022.question_text: What do Yield Sign Ahead and Stop Sign Ahead warning signs alert you to?
sec18-card-sec18-F022.teaching_text: Curves and foliage often hide corner octagons or yield triangles until braking room gets tight.

sec18-card-sec18-F023.question_text: What lies ahead when you pass a Traffic Signal Ahead warning sign?
sec18-card-sec18-F023.teaching_text: High-speed rural corridors post signal warnings so drivers prepare to halt if red appears.

sec18-card-sec18-F024.question_text: What distinction does the sign reference make between the two railroad-crossing signs?
sec18-card-sec18-F024.teaching_text: Round yellow warns early down the road while the white crossbuck marks the rails themselves.

sec18-card-sec18-F025.question_text: What shared roadway activity do School Crossing and Pedestrian Crossing signs identify?
sec18-card-sec18-F025.teaching_text: Covering the brake and scanning both curbs protects walkers stepping into painted or school zones.

sec18-card-sec18-F026.question_text: Along with road-condition diamonds, which overtaking restriction appears on the warning-sign page?
sec18-card-sec18-F026.teaching_text: A yellow left-side pennant gives extra sightline visibility when trucks block right-shoulder signs.

sec18-card-sec18-F027.question_text: What do Road Alignment, Left Curve, and Right Curve warning signs tell you about the road?
sec18-card-sec18-F027.teaching_text: Chevron alignment boards and curve diamonds trace sharp bends through dark coastal fog.

sec18-card-sec18-F028.question_text: What road geometry does a Winding Road sign warn of ahead?
sec18-card-sec18-F028.teaching_text: Linked back-to-back curves require holding a steady reduced speed rather than accelerating between bends.

sec18-card-sec18-F029.question_text: How do Entering Divided Highway and Leaving Divided Highway signs differ?
sec18-card-sec18-F029.teaching_text: Leaving a divided highway puts opposing traffic right across a painted line again.

sec18-card-sec18-F030.question_text: What does a Detour indication alert drivers to follow?
sec18-card-sec18-F030.teaching_text: Following orange Detour arrows guides traffic cleanly around bridge work or utility closures.

sec18-card-sec18-F031.question_text: What does a Slow Moving Vehicle emblem warn approaching drivers to expect?
sec18-card-sec18-F031.teaching_text: Farm tractors and road sweepers move far below highway pace, closing your gap rapidly.

sec18-card-sec18-F032.question_text: What roadway conflict do Side Road and Intersection warnings announce ahead?
sec18-card-sec18-F032.teaching_text: Scanning side branches early spots merging or crossing traffic before blind trees clear.

sec18-card-sec18-F033.question_text: What hazards do Traffic Island and Object Marker indications highlight?
sec18-card-sec18-F033.teaching_text: Striped object panels mark bridge abutments and raised islands that blend into night shadows.

sec18-card-sec18-F034.question_text: Contrast Road Narrows from the right with Added Lane from the left?
sec18-card-sec18-F034.teaching_text: Road Narrows demands squeezing over smoothly while Added Lane brings new flow without merging.

sec18-card-sec18-F035.question_text: What nearby facility and hazard does a Fire Station warning sign identify?
sec18-card-sec18-F035.teaching_text: Fire engines can pull out across both lanes quickly whenever station bay doors open.

sec18-card-sec18-F036.question_text: What common message connects Tractor Crossing, Deer Crossing, and Bicycle Crossing signs?
sec18-card-sec18-F036.teaching_text: Matching your visual scan to farm equipment, wildlife, or trail riders prevents surprise strikes.

sec18-card-sec18-F037.question_text: In which sign group does Ramp Speed Advisory belong, and what does it communicate?
sec18-card-sec18-F037.teaching_text: Tight cloverleaf exit loops curl sharply right off seventy-mile-per-hour freeways, demanding early smooth deceleration.

sec18-card-sec18-F038.question_text: What roadside hazard does a Playground warning sign alert drivers to watch for?
sec18-card-sec18-F038.teaching_text: Chasing a stray ball can send a child running into neighborhood lanes without looking.

sec18-card-sec18-F039.question_text: What traffic pattern does a Two-Way Traffic warning sign alert you to?
sec18-card-sec18-F039.teaching_text: Transitioning off a one-way street or divided road puts oncoming cars right beside your left fender.

sec18-card-sec18-F040.question_text: What do Narrow Bridge and Hill warning signs have in common?
sec18-card-sec18-F040.teaching_text: Trimmed bridge shoulders and steep grades both demand controlled speed and steady lane centering.

sec18-card-sec18-F041.question_text: What roadway boundary does a Road End Marker identify in the sign reference?
sec18-card-sec18-F041.teaching_text: Reflective red-diamond end markers prevent nighttime drivers from overrunning unlit dead-end streets and cul-de-sacs.

sec18-card-sec18-F042.question_text: What traction warning does a Slippery When Wet sign deliver?
sec18-card-sec18-F042.teaching_text: Light rain lifts oil film onto smooth asphalt, lengthening stops and triggering skids.

sec18-card-sec18-F043.question_text: With what roadway situation are Construction Speed, Road Work, and Construction signs associated?
sec18-card-sec18-F043.teaching_text: Spotting orange roadwork labels early gives you room to drop speed and scan for cones.

sec18-card-sec18-F044.question_text: What lies farther down the road when you pass a Flag Person Ahead sign?
sec18-card-sec18-F044.teaching_text: Preparing to stop around blind work bends prevents rear-ending queues held by a flagger.

sec03-card-sec03-F001.question_text: How does the handbook distinguish driver distraction from driver inattention?
sec03-card-sec03-F001.teaching_text: Exam questions test the difference between an external event pulling your focus away and daydreaming with zero outside trigger.

sec03-card-sec03-F002.question_text: What serious roadway outcome can result from either distraction or inattention?
sec03-card-sec03-F002.teaching_text: Whether a notification buzzes or your thoughts drift silently, losing mental focus leaves your vehicle vulnerable to a crash.

sec03-card-sec03-F003.question_text: How does distraction affect a driver's ability to spot a developing traffic hazard?
sec03-card-sec03-F003.teaching_text: Missing early brake lights or spotting a pedestrian at the last split second erases the space needed to stop.

sec03-card-sec03-F004.question_text: Once a hazard appears, what two mental mistakes can distraction cause during decision-making?
sec03-card-sec03-F004.teaching_text: Divided attention makes drivers freeze too long or panic into swerving the wrong way instead of braking smoothly.

sec03-card-sec03-F005.question_text: Which three physical vehicle inputs can distraction disrupt even after you decide what to do?
sec03-card-sec03-F005.teaching_text: Even the right choice fails if a occupied hand or startled foot jerks the wheel or slams the wrong pedal.

sec03-card-sec03-F006.question_text: What defines a physical distraction behind the wheel?
sec03-card-sec03-F006.teaching_text: Reaching across the cabin for a fallen bottle or bag leaves one-handed or crooked steering right when lanes tighten.

sec03-card-sec03-F007.question_text: What happens during a mental distraction such as getting absorbed in a conversation?
sec03-card-sec03-F007.teaching_text: Your eyes can stare straight through the windshield while an intense chat hijacks the brainpower needed to read traffic.

sec03-card-sec03-F008.question_text: What defines a visual distraction such as glancing at a navigation screen?
sec03-card-sec03-F008.teaching_text: Looking down at a map display blinds you to lane shifts, sudden stops, and crosswalk activity ahead.

sec03-card-sec03-F009.question_text: What counts as an auditory distraction inside a moving vehicle?
sec03-card-sec03-F009.teaching_text: Blasting music or sharp notification chimes startle your focus and drown out sirens, horns, or tire screeches nearby.

sec03-card-sec03-F010.question_text: What happens to crash risk when physical, mental, visual, and auditory distractions overlap at once?
sec03-card-sec03-F010.teaching_text: Holding a phone, reading its screen, listening to alerts, and thinking up a reply leaves zero capacity to drive.

sec03-card-sec03-F011.question_text: What share of collisions does the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration estimate involve driver inattention?
sec03-card-sec03-F011.teaching_text: More than half of all wrecks trace back to lost focus, making steady attention your strongest everyday crash defense.

sec03-card-sec03-F012.question_text: Roughly how many crashes across North America involve driver inattention each year according to the handbook?
sec03-card-sec03-F012.teaching_text: Crossing the million-crash mark every single year proves wandering focus is a massive continental safety hazard, not a fluke.

sec03-card-sec03-F013.question_text: Looking away from your travel path for at least how many seconds doubles your likelihood of a collision?
sec03-card-sec03-F013.teaching_text: At highway speed, a two-second glance covers over half a football field without seeing a single brake light.

sec03-card-sec03-F014.question_text: Which group of drivers is especially vulnerable to distraction from passenger behavior?
sec03-card-sec03-F014.teaching_text: Newer drivers still need active focus for lane and speed judgment, so rowdy cabin energy overwhelms them fast.

sec03-card-sec03-F015.question_text: How does carrying one teenage passenger change a teenage driver's likelihood of a fatal crash?
sec03-card-sec03-F015.teaching_text: Even a single peer friend in the cabin doubles fatal-crash odds, explaining Rhode Island's strict provisional passenger rules.

sec03-card-sec03-F016.question_text: By what percentage does fatal-crash risk rise when a teenage driver carries two or more teenage passengers?
sec03-card-sec03-F016.teaching_text: Packing two or more teen friends into the car spikes fatal-crash danger by three hundred percent.

sec03-card-sec03-F017.question_text: What does scrolling audio tracks or switching radio stations pull away from the driving task?
sec03-card-sec03-F017.teaching_text: Hunting for a playlist mid-curve pulls fingers off the wheel and eyes onto the dash simultaneously.

sec03-card-sec03-F018.question_text: Why is reaching for a sliding object inside a moving car especially dangerous for teen drivers?
sec03-card-sec03-F018.teaching_text: Bending down toward the floorboard pulls your gaze below the dashboard and often tugs the steering wheel sideways.

sec03-card-sec03-F019.question_text: What physical and visual distractions happen when a driver places a handheld phone call?
sec03-card-sec03-F019.teaching_text: Tapping numbers on a screen combines single-hand steering with repeated downward glances away from moving traffic.

sec03-card-sec03-F020.question_text: Does a phone call still demand mental effort when the driver is quiet and only listening?
sec03-card-sec03-F020.teaching_text: Processing a caller's voice outside the car competes directly with the visual scanning parts of your brain.

sec03-card-sec03-F021.question_text: What two unintentional vehicle control slips often show up when a driver chats on the phone?
sec03-card-sec03-F021.teaching_text: When mental bandwidth shifts into a phone call, drivers drift toward lane lines and lose steady throttle control.

sec03-card-sec03-F022.question_text: Why can hands-free phone calls still cause a crash even though both hands stay on the wheel?
sec03-card-sec03-F022.teaching_text: Test questions target the myth that Bluetooth makes calling risk-free, when cognitive distraction stays wide awake.

sec03-card-sec03-F023.question_text: Why does the handbook single out texting as an especially dangerous distraction?
sec03-card-sec03-F023.teaching_text: Typing and reading messages locks your eyes onto glass and your fingers onto keys while traffic closes fast.

sec03-card-sec03-F024.question_text: How does studying a paper map or electronic navigation screen while rolling affect safety?
sec03-card-sec03-F024.teaching_text: Tracing street names or zooming a route map mid-drive pulls visual and mental attention off live traffic.

sec03-card-sec03-F025.question_text: Besides phones and stereos, what four everyday cabin activities does the handbook list as distractions?
sec03-card-sec03-F025.teaching_text: Unwrapping food, checking mirrors to groom, fiddling with vents, or calming a loose pet all break driving focus.

sec03-card-sec03-F026.question_text: Why is staring at a roadside crash scene dangerous as you drive past?
sec03-card-sec03-F026.teaching_text: Rubbernecking at flashing wreckers blinds you when the car directly ahead slams its brakes in slow traffic.

sec03-card-sec03-F027.question_text: What three outside roadside sights commonly compete for a driver's visual focus?
sec03-card-sec03-F027.teaching_text: Bright strobes, shifting digital ads, and big construction machines naturally grab human eyes unless you deliberately look ahead.

sec03-card-sec03-F028.question_text: In what two ways can animals near a roadway create danger for drivers?
sec03-card-sec03-F028.teaching_text: Wildlife can bolt straight into your lane or pull your gaze toward the shoulder even while staying off pavement.

sec03-card-sec03-F029.question_text: What should you do with vehicle controls, audio, and cabin temperature before shifting out of park?
sec03-card-sec03-F029.teaching_text: Dialing in volume and cabin temperature while parked eliminates dashboard hunting once you merge into moving traffic.

sec03-card-sec03-F030.question_text: Why should loose items inside the cabin be stowed securely before you start moving?
sec03-card-sec03-F030.teaching_text: A backpack or water bottle sliding across the floor tempts drivers to grab it or wedges near foot pedals.

sec03-card-sec03-F031.question_text: When should you study your travel route and maps?
sec03-card-sec03-F031.teaching_text: Knowing your exits and turns ahead of time keeps your eyes scanning intersections instead of squinting at directions.

sec03-card-sec03-F032.question_text: Which distracting digital activities must stay completely off-limits while driving?
sec03-card-sec03-F032.teaching_text: Browsing pages, watching clips, gaming, or texting hijacks visual and manual control simultaneously on live streets.

sec03-card-sec03-F033.question_text: Which four non-tech personal habits does the handbook tell drivers to avoid behind the wheel?
sec03-card-sec03-F033.teaching_text: Spilled hot drinks, dropped ashes, greasy wrappers, or propped paper pages trigger instant panic swerves.

sec03-card-sec03-F034.question_text: What must you do first if a child or passenger needs hands-on attention during a drive?
sec03-card-sec03-F034.teaching_text: Twisting around toward the back seat while rolling forward sends your car drifting across lanes in seconds.

sec03-card-sec03-F035.question_text: How can an available passenger help keep you focused when a minor cabin task comes up?
sec03-card-sec03-F035.teaching_text: Letting a rider adjust navigation, vents, or music keeps both of your hands and eyes locked on traffic.

sec03-card-sec03-F036.question_text: What should you do the moment you realize your thoughts have drifted off the road?
sec03-card-sec03-F036.teaching_text: Catching daydreaming early and actively scanning mirrors and spacing ahead breaks highway autopilot before hazards close in.

sec03-card-sec03-F037.question_text: How should you handle incoming calls and messages that arrive while you are driving?
sec03-card-sec03-F037.teaching_text: No ringtone is worth a wreck, so let messages record and call back only after parking safely.

sec03-card-sec03-F038.question_text: When should casual social phone conversations take place?
sec03-card-sec03-F038.teaching_text: Everyday catch-up chats drain mental alertness without urgency, so save them for times when you are off the road.

sec03-card-sec03-F039.question_text: What should you do before continuing a conversation that turns emotionally upsetting?
sec03-card-sec03-F039.teaching_text: Heated arguments flood you with adrenaline and tunnel vision, wrecking smooth speed and intersection awareness.

sec03-card-sec03-F040.question_text: Why must you refuse to juggle eating, phone talking, and audio tuning at the same time while driving?
sec03-card-sec03-F040.teaching_text: Layering food, conversation, and dashboard reaches leaves zero spare attention when traffic suddenly brakes.

sec03-card-sec03-F041.question_text: Who should place and speak on a necessary phone call whenever you are not driving solo?
sec03-card-sec03-F041.teaching_text: Having a rider dial and talk keeps the driver's brain, eyes, and hands dedicated entirely to the road.

sec03-card-sec03-F042.question_text: Why should your phone be secured in a mount or compartment rather than sitting loose on the console?
sec03-card-sec03-F042.teaching_text: During sudden braking or impact, an unrestrained phone launches across the cabin at vehicle speed and strikes occupants.

sec03-card-sec03-F043.question_text: How does drowsiness impair your eyes, reaction timing, and traffic judgment?
sec03-card-sec03-F043.teaching_text: Fatigue blurs sight, stretches out hazard recognition, and tricks you into misjudging how fast gaps are closing.
sec03-card-sec03-F043.must_match_memory_hook: Dims vision, slows choices, warps judgment

visual_sync.text_span: Dims vision, slows choices, warps judgment

sec03-card-sec03-F044.question_text: What are microsleeps, and why are they so dangerous behind the wheel?
sec03-card-sec03-F044.teaching_text: Nodding off for just three or four seconds sends an unsteered car drifting across centerlines or off shoulders at full speed.

sec03-card-sec03-F045.question_text: What two travel and rest factors sharply raise the odds of falling asleep at the wheel?
sec03-card-sec03-F045.teaching_text: Starting a marathon highway drive on skimpy sleep builds overwhelming fatigue long before you reach your destination.

sec03-card-sec03-F046.question_text: Does willpower or continuing to drive cure the impairment caused by drowsiness?
sec03-card-sec03-F046.teaching_text: Trying to tough out the last twenty miles only deepens sleep pressure until your brain shuts down involuntarily.

sec03-card-sec03-F047.question_text: How can untreated medical conditions like sleep apnea or narcolepsy affect driving?
sec03-card-sec03-F047.teaching_text: Untreated sleep disorders rob the brain of restorative rest and trigger sudden, irresistible sleep attacks in traffic.

sec03-card-sec03-F048.question_text: Which three recurring sleep symptoms should prompt a driver to consult a physician?
sec03-card-sec03-F048.teaching_text: Loud nightly snoring, chronic trouble sleeping, or constant daytime exhaustion often point to treatable medical sleep disorders.

sec03-card-sec03-F049.question_text: What does the handbook mean by the body's circadian rhythm?
sec03-card-sec03-F049.teaching_text: Your internal biological clock schedules natural alertness peaks and sleepiness dips across every twenty-four-hour day.

sec03-card-sec03-F050.question_text: Which two daily time windows does the handbook identify as natural low-alertness periods?
sec03-card-sec03-F050.teaching_text: Crash risk climbs overnight between midnight and six morning and dips again during the mid-afternoon slump from two to five.
sec03-card-sec03-F050.must_match_memory_hook: Midnight to six, two to five

visual_sync.text_span: Midnight to six, two to five

sec03-card-sec03-F051.question_text: What blood alcohol levels does the handbook compare to staying awake for twenty hours and twenty-four hours?
sec03-card-sec03-F051.teaching_text: Twenty hours awake mimics zero point zero five percent alcohol, while twenty-four hours matches legally drunk zero point one zero.
sec03-card-sec03-F051.must_match_memory_hook: Point zero five, point one zero

visual_sync.text_span: Point zero five, point one zero

sec03-card-sec03-F052.question_text: Which work shift patterns raise a driver's risk of drowsy driving?
sec03-card-sec03-F052.teaching_text: Graveyard hours, dawn starts, rotating schedules, and overtime shifts fight your natural circadian sleep window.

sec03-card-sec03-F053.question_text: Beyond missed sleep, what everyday physical or cabin conditions can bring on driver drowsiness?
sec03-card-sec03-F053.teaching_text: Toasty heater air, overeating, sun glare, illness, boredom, stress, alcohol, or drugs all accelerate behind-the-wheel fatigue.
sec03-card-sec03-F053.must_match_memory_hook: Warm cabin, heavy meals, glare, stress

visual_sync.text_span: Warm cabin, heavy meals, glare, stress

sec03-card-sec03-F054.question_text: Why can an easy, straight road and steady engine hum actually make driving riskier?
sec03-card-sec03-F054.teaching_text: Unchanging scenery and rhythmic tire hum lull your brain into passive drowsiness right when highway speeds stay high.

sec03-card-sec03-F055.question_text: Do drivers always notice clear warning signs before falling asleep behind the wheel?
sec03-card-sec03-F055.teaching_text: Exhausted drivers severely misjudge their own tiredness and can nod off abruptly without realizing how close sleep was.
sec03-card-sec03-F055.must_match_memory_hook: Sleep can strike without noticed warning

visual_sync.text_span: Sleep can strike without noticed warning

sec03-card-sec03-F056.question_text: What four eye and face signals warn that fatigue is setting in behind the wheel?
sec03-card-sec03-F056.teaching_text: Repeated yawns, frequent blinking, drooping eyelids, and trouble focusing are urgent red flags to exit traffic and rest.

sec03-card-sec03-F057.question_text: What memory and posture clues show a driver is becoming dangerously drowsy?
sec03-card-sec03-F057.teaching_text: Forgetting the last few miles, blowing past your exit, or fighting a bobbing head means microsleeps are starting.

sec03-card-sec03-F058.question_text: Which three vehicle-positioning mistakes warn that drowsiness is taking over?
