sec03-card-sec03-F058.teaching_text: Buzzing a shoulder rumble strip, wandering across lane paint, or creeping onto bumpers means pull off immediately.

sec03-card-sec03-F059.question_text: How many hours of nightly sleep does the handbook recommend for adults versus teenagers?
sec03-card-sec03-F059.teaching_text: Growing teen brains need eight to ten hours nightly, one more hour than the seven-to-nine adult range, for sharp reactions.

sec03-card-sec03-F060.question_text: What two planning steps help prevent drowsy driving before setting out on a long trip?
sec03-card-sec03-F060.teaching_text: Mapping rest areas ahead of time and sharing driving shifts stops solo exhaustion on multi-hour highway runs.

sec03-card-sec03-F061.question_text: How can an awake passenger help protect against drowsy driving on a road trip?
sec03-card-sec03-F061.teaching_text: An alert companion notices yawning or lane drift early and can take the wheel or call for a rest stop.

sec03-card-sec03-F062.question_text: What rule applies to prescription or over-the-counter medicines before you get behind the wheel?
sec03-card-sec03-F062.teaching_text: Cold, allergy, and pain pills carry real sedation warnings that slow steering and braking just like missed sleep.

sec03-card-sec03-F063.question_text: After how many miles or hours of driving does the handbook recommend taking regular breaks?
sec03-card-sec03-F063.teaching_text: Stopping on a set two-hour or hundred-mile rhythm refreshes your eyes and posture before deep fatigue builds.
sec03-card-sec03-F063.must_match_memory_hook: Every hundred miles or two hours

visual_sync.text_span: Every hundred miles or two hours

sec03-card-sec03-F064.question_text: On long-distance drives, at least how long should each two-hour or hundred-mile rest stop last?
sec03-card-sec03-F064.teaching_text: Giving yourself ten full minutes out of traffic resets concentration far better than a rushed thirty-second pause.

sec03-card-sec03-F065.question_text: How should you decide how far to travel in a single day?
sec03-card-sec03-F065.teaching_text: Capping your daily distance upfront removes the temptation to push dangerously past exhaustion just to reach a hotel.

sec03-card-sec03-F066.question_text: Why fail tricks like cold air, loud music, caffeine, gum, or speed changes when you are drowsy?
sec03-card-sec03-F066.teaching_text: Exam traps list rolled-down windows, coffee, or blasting stereos as cures, yet none keep sleepiness away for long.

sec03-card-sec03-F067.question_text: What is the only genuine recovery measure that restores safe alertness when drowsy?
sec03-card-sec03-F067.teaching_text: Only actual sleep pays back biological fatigue, so never trust temporary stimulants as substitutes for resting.

sec03-card-sec03-F068.question_text: If you have no choice except to rest along the road, what kind of spot should you pick?
sec03-card-sec03-F068.teaching_text: Parking right on a narrow interstate shoulder risks getting struck by drifting traffic, so seek security or maximum clearance.

sec03-card-sec03-F069.question_text: What kind of stopping place should you choose when pulling off to rest after dark?
sec03-card-sec03-F069.teaching_text: Bright lighting and active foot traffic keep you personally secure while you nap and recover.

sec03-card-sec03-F070.question_text: How should you set your doors, engine, and windows before napping at a rest stop?
sec03-card-sec03-F070.teaching_text: Shutting the engine prevents exhaust buildup while locked doors and a tiny window gap balance security with fresh air.
sec03-card-sec03-F070.must_match_memory_hook: Lock doors, engine off, crack window

visual_sync.text_span: Lock doors, engine off, crack window

sec03-card-sec03-F071.question_text: How should you set your lights and electrical accessories if resting beside the road?
sec03-card-sec03-F071.teaching_text: Parking lights keep your car visible to passing traffic while turning off extra electronics protects your battery.

sec03-card-sec03-F072.question_text: What should you do after waking from a rest stop before merging back into traffic?
sec03-card-sec03-F072.teaching_text: Taking a quick walk in a safe spot shakes off sleep inertia so you do not re-enter traffic half-awake.

sec03-card-sec03-F073.question_text: According to the handbook, naps longer than twenty minutes leave you groggy for at least how long after waking?
sec03-card-sec03-F073.teaching_text: Deep sleep kicks in past twenty minutes, so budget at least five awake minutes before touching the ignition.

sec03-card-sec03-F074.question_text: Which three driving abilities can strong emotions disrupt?
sec03-card-sec03-F074.teaching_text: Intense feelings cloud logical thinking, narrow your visual scan, and make you miss even familiar stop signs or signals.

sec03-card-sec03-F075.question_text: Are anger and frustration the only emotions that can impair safe driving?
sec03-card-sec03-F075.teaching_text: Test takers forget that celebration and intense excitement distract focus and encourage speeding just like anger does.

sec03-card-sec03-F076.question_text: What pushy behind-the-wheel behaviors define aggressive driving in the handbook?
sec03-card-sec03-F076.teaching_text: Pushing through traffic by tailgating, blowing signals, speeding, or weaving turns minor impatience into multi-car wrecks.

sec03-card-sec03-F077.question_text: How does road rage cross the line beyond ordinary aggressive driving?
sec03-card-sec03-F077.teaching_text: Aggressive driving breaks traffic rules, whereas road rage crosses into violent assault using a car or weapon to cause harm.

sec03-card-sec03-F078.question_text: Which three hostile actions does the handbook list as clear examples of road rage?
sec03-card-sec03-F078.teaching_text: Hurling items, making violent threats, or intentionally trying to ram another car are criminal assaults, never traffic habits.

sec03-card-sec03-F079.question_text: What two personal habits help keep frustration from boiling over behind the wheel?
sec03-card-sec03-F079.teaching_text: Leaving early removes clock pressure, and spotting your own emotional triggers keeps minor traffic delays from sparking anger.

sec03-card-sec03-F080.question_text: How should you interpret and respond when another driver makes a traffic mistake?
sec03-card-sec03-F080.teaching_text: Assuming a bad merge was an honest error rather than a personal insult defuses road conflict instantly.

sec03-card-sec03-F081.question_text: What should you do before starting the car if you are going through a temporary emotional upset?
sec03-card-sec03-F081.teaching_text: Taking ten quiet minutes before turning the key keeps fresh anger or tears from steering your car into danger.

sec03-card-sec03-F082.question_text: What is the safest move if strong emotional distress hits while you are already driving?
sec03-card-sec03-F082.teaching_text: Pulling into a safe lot lets your heart rate settle and clears your vision before rejoining moving lanes.

sec03-card-sec03-F083.question_text: What travel alternatives should you choose when deep grief, anxiety, or heavy emotion will not fade quickly?
sec03-card-sec03-F083.teaching_text: When lasting distress makes steady concentration impossible, handing off the keys or riding public transit protects everyone.

sec03-card-sec03-F084.question_text: Which three spacing and scheduling habits help prevent aggressive driving?
sec03-card-sec03-F084.teaching_text: Starting early, keeping generous following cushions, and skipping pointless lane weaving keeps traffic calm around you.

sec03-card-sec03-F085.question_text: How should you treat the far-left highway lane to prevent frustrating surrounding traffic?
sec03-card-sec03-F085.teaching_text: Camping slowly in the passing lane traps faster vehicles behind you and provokes risky right-side passes and tailgating.

sec03-card-sec03-F086.question_text: What two communication habits prevent sparking road hostility during lane changes?
sec03-card-sec03-F086.teaching_text: Clear turn signals show courtesy, whereas rude hand gestures can trigger sudden violent retaliation from a stranger.

sec03-card-sec03-F087.question_text: How should you sound your horn so other drivers do not read it as hostile?
sec03-card-sec03-F087.teaching_text: Laying on a long horn blast feels like an angry shout, while a light tap alerts politely.

sec03-card-sec03-F088.question_text: What two parking-lot mistakes should you avoid to prevent conflict with nearby drivers?
sec03-card-sec03-F088.teaching_text: Straddling two stalls or dinging a neighbor's paint with a swinging door sparks avoidable parking-lot confrontations.

sec03-card-sec03-F089.question_text: When must you switch off high-beam headlights around other traffic?
sec03-card-sec03-F089.teaching_text: Blasting bright beams into oncoming windshields or a lead driver's rearview mirror blinds them and looks aggressive.

sec03-card-sec03-F090.question_text: How can you help a vehicle entering the highway from an on-ramp when traffic permits?
sec03-card-sec03-F090.teaching_text: Sliding smoothly out of the right lane when clear opens an easy, stress-free gap for merging cars.

sec03-card-sec03-F091.question_text: How should you react if an aggressive driver tries to confront or provoke you?
sec03-card-sec03-F091.teaching_text: Locking eyes, shouting back, or brake-checking pours fuel on the fire, whereas calm detachment lets them move on.

sec03-card-sec03-F092.question_text: Why must you stay inside your vehicle during an aggressive roadside confrontation?
sec03-card-sec03-F092.teaching_text: Stepping out onto the pavement strips away locked steel doors and leaves you physically exposed to assault or traffic.

sec03-card-sec03-F093.question_text: Why should you leave maneuvering space around your car when stopping in traffic?
sec03-card-sec03-F093.teaching_text: Stopping right on a bumper traps you in place if a hostile person walks toward your window.

sec03-card-sec03-F094.question_text: What number should you call if you need help during an aggressive driving confrontation?
sec03-card-sec03-F094.teaching_text: Dialing emergency dispatch alerts police to your location instead of trying to handle a dangerous aggressor alone.

sec03-card-sec03-F095.question_text: Where should you drive and what should you do if an aggressive driver follows you?
sec03-card-sec03-F095.teaching_text: Never lead a hostile driver to your driveway; pull into a crowded, well-lit lot and honk to draw witnesses.

sec03-card-sec03-F096.question_text: What single factor on the road remains fully within your control even in frustrating traffic?
sec03-card-sec03-F096.teaching_text: Traffic jams and careless strangers happen daily, yet choosing a calm, defensive reaction always stays in your hands.

sec05-card-sec05-F001.question_text: How should you use the left lane versus the right lane on a multilane highway?
sec05-card-sec05-F001.teaching_text: Keeping through traffic in the right lane leaves the left lane open so faster vehicles pass predictably without weaving.

sec05-card-sec05-F002.question_text: What two courteous steps should you take when another driver is overtaking your vehicle?
sec05-card-sec05-F002.teaching_text: Speeding up traps the passing car in oncoming danger, whereas easing off the gas slightly lets them clear quickly.

sec05-card-sec05-F003.question_text: What does the handbook define as a vehicle's blind spots?
sec05-card-sec05-F003.teaching_text: Even well-aimed side and rearview mirrors leave flanking pockets large enough to hide a car or motorcycle.

sec05-card-sec05-F004.question_text: What two visual checks are required before changing lanes or pulling out to pass?
sec05-card-sec05-F004.teaching_text: Combining mirror scans with a quick head turn over the target shoulder catches vehicles sitting in your blind zone.

sec05-card-sec05-F005.question_text: Why must you avoid stacking tall packages on the back seat or rear parcel shelf?
sec05-card-sec05-F005.teaching_text: Piling boxes across the rear glass blocks your center mirror and widens the blind area behind your trunk.

sec05-card-sec05-F006.question_text: What checks and signal come before pulling left to overtake another vehicle?
sec05-card-sec05-F006.teaching_text: Verifying clear ahead distance, checking that nobody behind is already passing you, and signaling left prevents collisions.

sec05-card-sec05-F007.question_text: After overtaking, what exact sight in your inside mirror tells you it is safe to return to the right lane?
sec05-card-sec05-F007.teaching_text: Waiting until both front tires of the passed car appear in your rearview mirror prevents clipping their front bumper.

sec05-card-sec05-F008.question_text: How many vehicles may you overtake in a single passing maneuver according to the handbook?
sec05-card-sec05-F008.teaching_text: Trying to leapfrog a whole line of cars at once leaves you exposed in the passing lane if gaps close.

sec05-card-sec05-F009.question_text: May you exceed the posted speed limit briefly in order to finish passing a slower vehicle?
sec05-card-sec05-F009.teaching_text: Classic exam trap alert, because overtaking never grants a legal pass to drive faster than the posted limit.

sec05-card-sec05-F010.question_text: What maneuver by the vehicle ahead can make passing on the right lawful?
sec05-card-sec05-F010.teaching_text: When a driver ahead signals and positions for a left turn, lawful right-side passing keeps through traffic flowing.

sec05-card-sec05-F011.question_text: What roadway width and clearance condition allows passing on the right?
sec05-card-sec05-F011.teaching_text: You need genuine clear lane width free of parked cars or obstacles before passing on the right.

sec05-card-sec05-F012.question_text: When may you pass on the right along a one-way street?
sec05-card-sec05-F012.teaching_text: Wide one-way streets carrying two or more clear travel lanes allow smooth passing in either open lane.

sec05-card-sec05-F013.question_text: May you ever drive onto the shoulder or off the pavement to get around another vehicle?
sec05-card-sec05-F013.teaching_text: Dirt edges and breakdown shoulders hide gravel, guardrails, and stopped cars, making off-pavement passing strictly illegal.

sec05-card-sec05-F014.question_text: Which roadway features and traffic controls forbid overtaking?
sec05-card-sec05-F014.teaching_text: Blind hills, curves, railroad crossings, intersections, tunnels, bridges, solid lines, and no-passing signs all erase safe sightlines.

sec05-card-sec05-F015.question_text: When backing more than thirty feet, what warning lights does the handbook recommend turning on?
sec05-card-sec05-F015.teaching_text: Blinking four-way hazard lights give pedestrians and approaching cars extra notice during an unusually long reverse move.

sec05-card-sec05-F016.question_text: How should you position your head and body to see behind you when reversing?
sec05-card-sec05-F016.teaching_text: Pivoting to look directly through the back glass over your right shoulder reveals obstacles mirrors and cameras miss.

sec05-card-sec05-F017.question_text: How should you use your mirrors while backing in a straight line?
sec05-card-sec05-F017.teaching_text: Combining direct rear looks with frequent mirror glances spots people or cars stepping in from either side.

sec05-card-sec05-F018.question_text: What roadway design feature defines a limited-access highway?
sec05-card-sec05-F018.teaching_text: Replacing cross-street intersections with grade-separated ramps lets freeway traffic flow steadily without red lights.

sec05-card-sec05-F019.question_text: How must your scanning and reaction timing adjust for higher freeway speeds?
sec05-card-sec05-F019.teaching_text: Closing speeds on freeways eat up space fast, so scanning far downrange gives you time for smooth adjustments.

sec05-card-sec05-F020.question_text: What rear hazard must you check for before signaling into a freeway passing lane?
sec05-card-sec05-F020.teaching_text: A car already flying up the left lane closes the gap much faster than a casual mirror glance suggests.

sec05-card-sec05-F021.question_text: How should you pull off during a freeway emergency, and what shoulder hazard must you watch for?
sec05-card-sec05-F021.teaching_text: Signal early as you enter the breakdown lane, and check mirrors for impatient drivers illegally cruising that shoulder.

sec05-card-sec05-F022.question_text: Why must you double-check your speed reduction when leaving a freeway after cruising at highway pace?
sec05-card-sec05-F022.teaching_text: Because highway cruising makes fifty feel like twenty-five, trust your speedometer so you do not overshoot the ramp.

sec05-card-sec05-F023.question_text: Where should you stop to rest during a long freeway drive instead of parking in the breakdown lane?
sec05-card-sec05-F023.teaching_text: Breakdown shoulders are strictly for emergencies, whereas rest areas and service plazas shield parked cars from fast traffic.

sec05-card-sec05-F024.question_text: How often does the handbook advise stopping to rest on a long highway trip?
sec05-card-sec05-F024.teaching_text: Taking scheduled breaks every two hours or one hundred miles keeps highway monotony from turning into drowsiness.
sec05-card-sec05-F024.must_match_memory_hook: Every hundred miles or two hours

visual_sync.text_span: Every hundred miles or two hours

sec05-card-sec05-F025.question_text: Where should your tires sit and what lights belong on during an emergency roadside repair?
sec05-card-sec05-F025.teaching_text: Clearing every tire completely off active travel pavement and flashing four-ways warns approaching traffic early.

sec05-card-sec05-F026.question_text: What three portable warning devices may you place out if available during a roadside breakdown?
sec05-card-sec05-F026.teaching_text: Setting reflective triangles, flares, or reflectors behind a disabled vehicle alerts drivers rounding curves or hills.

sec05-card-sec05-F027.question_text: What is the job of a freeway acceleration lane?
sec05-card-sec05-F027.teaching_text: Using the full acceleration runway lets you match highway pace smoothly instead of creeping into fast lanes.

sec05-card-sec05-F028.question_text: What is the job of a freeway deceleration lane?
sec05-card-sec05-F028.teaching_text: Waiting until you enter the deceleration lane to brake prevents startling high-speed vehicles behind you on the main highway.

sec05-card-sec05-F029.question_text: Where is the freeway merging area located, and what happens there?
sec05-card-sec05-F029.teaching_text: Right after building speed on the acceleration strip, the merging zone is where you blend into an open highway gap.

sec05-card-sec05-F030.question_text: How are the leftmost, middle, and rightmost lanes assigned on a three-lane-plus freeway?
sec05-card-sec05-F030.teaching_text: Sorting fast passers left, steady cruisers middle, and slower or ramp traffic right keeps multi-lane freeways organized.
sec05-card-sec05-F030.must_match_memory_hook: Left pass, middle cruise, right slow

visual_sync.text_span: Left pass, middle cruise, right slow

sec05-card-sec05-F031.question_text: Which vehicle types can posted freeway signs bar from using the far-left lane?
sec05-card-sec05-F031.teaching_text: Keeping heavy trucks and buses out of the far-left lane preserves clear sightlines and passing flow.

sec05-card-sec05-F032.question_text: What residential speed limit and typical highway speed range does the Rhode Island handbook describe?
sec05-card-sec05-F032.teaching_text: Memorize twenty-five miles per hour for residential streets alongside the fifty-to-sixty-five range on state highways.

sec05-card-sec05-F033.question_text: How many seconds of following space should you keep in normal conditions, and when do you add more?
sec05-card-sec05-F033.teaching_text: A three-second dry cushion gives you perception and reaction room, while wet or icy asphalt demands extra seconds.

sec05-card-sec05-F034.question_text: How should you handle a driver tailgating closely behind your rear bumper?
sec05-card-sec05-F034.teaching_text: Slamming brakes causes a rear-end wreck and speeding up adds danger, so change lanes safely and let them go.

sec05-card-sec05-F035.question_text: What ongoing mirror habit protects you before pulling into the passing lane?
sec05-card-sec05-F035.teaching_text: Checking mirrors every few seconds keeps a live mental map so fast-approaching left-lane cars never surprise you.

sec05-card-sec05-F036.question_text: Within what distance before a lane change does the handbook instruct you to signal?
sec05-card-sec05-F036.teaching_text: Giving surrounding drivers a clear hundred-foot blinker warning prevents two vehicles from steering into the same lane together.

sec05-card-sec05-F037.question_text: What four actions signal for help safely if your car breaks down along a highway?
sec05-card-sec05-F037.teaching_text: Pulling clear, raising the hood, tying white cloth on the handle, and waiting inside locked doors signals distress safely.
sec05-card-sec05-F037.must_match_memory_hook: Clear lane, hood up, white cloth

visual_sync.text_span: Clear lane, hood up, white cloth

sec05-card-sec05-F038.question_text: Which lane position applies to ordinary highway driving when you are not overtaking or directed otherwise by signs?
sec05-card-sec05-F038.teaching_text: Defaulting to the right lane keeps faster passing lanes clear and lowers conflict across Rhode Island highways.

sec05-card-sec05-F039.question_text: What must you do immediately when drowsiness sets in during highway travel?
sec05-card-sec05-F039.teaching_text: High speeds leave zero margin for heavy eyelids, so pull into a safe rest stop instead of pushing farther.

sec05-card-sec05-F040.question_text: How must your driving change when rain, snow, or ice coats a highway?
sec05-card-sec05-F040.teaching_text: Slick winter or storm surfaces stretch braking distances dramatically even on wide multi-lane highways.

sec05-card-sec05-F041.question_text: What is the only safe move if you accidentally pass your highway exit?
sec05-card-sec05-F041.teaching_text: Stopping or backing up on a high-speed freeway or shoulder invites a catastrophic rear-end highway crash.

sec05-card-sec05-F042.question_text: How should your eyes move across the traffic scene while cruising on a highway?
sec05-card-sec05-F042.teaching_text: Staring at a single bumper creates highway tunnel vision that misses merging cars and brake lights ahead.

sec05-card-sec05-F043.question_text: What three immediate steps are required when an emergency vehicle approaches with lights or sirens?
sec05-card-sec05-F043.teaching_text: Clearing right and coming to a complete stop opens an unobstructed lane for ambulances, fire engines, and police.

sec05-card-sec05-F044.question_text: Before pulling back into traffic after an emergency vehicle passes, what hidden danger must you check for?
sec05-card-sec05-F044.teaching_text: Fire trucks and cruisers frequently travel in pairs, so pulling out blindly risks cutting off a second rig.

sec05-card-sec05-F045.question_text: At least how many feet back must you stay behind a responding emergency vehicle?
sec05-card-sec05-F045.teaching_text: Emergency units brake or turn sharply without warning, making five hundred feet the mandatory safety buffer.

sec05-card-sec05-F046.question_text: What pedestrian hazard should you watch closely around any stopped bus?
sec05-card-sec05-F046.teaching_text: Bus riders often hurry across lanes from in front of the bus where the tall body hides them.

sec05-card-sec05-F047.question_text: What should you do when another motorist ignores your legal right-of-way?
sec05-card-sec05-F047.teaching_text: Being legally right never softens twisted steel, so give up the space rather than forcing a collision.

sec05-card-sec05-F048.question_text: What two options apply on a multi-lane road when approaching a designated stopped roadside vehicle?
sec05-card-sec05-F048.teaching_text: Changing into an open lane away from roadside workers comes first, and slowing down protects them whenever lanes are full.

sec05-card-sec05-F049.question_text: What does Rhode Island's basic speed law require even when the posted speed sign allows faster travel?
sec05-card-sec05-F049.teaching_text: Heavy traffic, pedestrians, glare, or slick pavement can make driving the full posted number illegally fast.

sec05-card-sec05-F050.question_text: What conditions does a posted speed-limit sign actually represent?
sec05-card-sec05-F050.teaching_text: Think of the sign number as a ceiling for dry, clear, uncrowded pavement rather than a safe target in rain or work zones.

sec05-card-sec05-F051.question_text: What phone rule applies to Rhode Island drivers younger than eighteen?
sec05-card-sec05-F051.teaching_text: Drivers under eighteen cannot use handheld phones, Bluetooth hands-free systems, or speakerphones except in a real emergency.

sec05-card-sec05-F052.question_text: How should a driver under eighteen place an emergency phone call?
sec05-card-sec05-F052.teaching_text: Stopping in a safe spot first lets you focus on giving clear location details to emergency dispatchers.

sec05-card-sec05-F053.question_text: How does Rhode Island law treat texting while operating a motor vehicle?
sec05-card-sec05-F053.teaching_text: State law flatly bans texting behind the wheel to keep eyes and thumbs off screens in traffic.

sec05-card-sec05-F054.question_text: What two safe options exist when an adult driver faces a genuinely necessary phone call?
sec05-card-sec05-F054.teaching_text: Handing the phone to a rider or pulling completely off the road keeps driving attention undivided.

sec05-card-sec05-F055.question_text: Does using hands-free phone equipment completely remove distraction danger?
sec05-card-sec05-F055.teaching_text: Voice controls free your fingers, yet the conversation itself still taxes mental reaction speed.

sec05-card-sec05-F056.question_text: What fine amounts does the handbook list for a minor driver's first and second cell-phone offenses?
sec05-card-sec05-F056.teaching_text: Getting caught with a phone under eighteen starts at one hundred dollars and jumps to one hundred fifty next time.

sec05-card-sec05-F057.question_text: What two penalties hit a minor driver on a third or later cell-phone conviction?
sec05-card-sec05-F057.teaching_text: A third teen phone ticket costs two hundred fifty dollars and strips your license away until your eighteenth birthday.

sec05-card-sec05-F058.question_text: Which three wireless-handset actions are banned for Rhode Island drivers of every age?
sec05-card-sec05-F058.teaching_text: Whether you type a draft, glance at an incoming message, or hit send, all three violate the wireless-handset ban.

sec05-card-sec05-F059.question_text: What escalating fine amounts does the handbook list for first, second, and later texting offenses?
sec05-card-sec05-F059.teaching_text: Texting citations climb from one hundred dollars to one hundred fifty and then two hundred fifty on repeat offenses.

sec07-card-sec07-F001.question_text: Why might handbook emergency suggestions not fit every single roadside crisis?
sec07-card-sec07-F001.teaching_text: Every emergency varies by traffic, road surface, and vehicle design, requiring adaptable driver judgment.

sec07-card-sec07-F002.question_text: When should you adjust your speed for road and traffic conditions to avoid losing traction?
sec07-card-sec07-F002.teaching_text: Waiting until tires start sliding is too late because excess momentum already broke your grip.

sec07-card-sec07-F003.question_text: What steering and speed inputs must you avoid on wet or icy pavement?
sec07-card-sec07-F003.teaching_text: Jerky wheel tugs or abrupt pedal stabs snap fragile tire grip instantly on rain or ice.

sec07-card-sec07-F004.question_text: How should you apply conventional non-antilock brakes on a slippery road?
sec07-card-sec07-F004.teaching_text: Gentle pedal squeezes and releases prevent non-antilock wheels from locking into an unsteerable slide.

sec07-card-sec07-F005.question_text: How should you press the brake pedal during normal emergency braking with antilock brakes?
sec07-card-sec07-F005.teaching_text: Pumping an antilock pedal defeats rapid computer modulation and stretches your emergency stopping distance.

sec07-card-sec07-F006.question_text: What does rapid pulsing in the brake pedal indicate during hard antilock braking?
sec07-card-sec07-F006.teaching_text: Startled drivers who lift off a vibrating pedal give up maximum braking right when danger peaks.

sec07-card-sec07-F007.question_text: How does an antilock braking system help you during an emergency stop?
sec07-card-sec07-F007.teaching_text: Preventing wheel lockup lets you steer around an obstacle even while braking hard.

sec07-card-sec07-F008.question_text: Where should you check specific operating guidance for your vehicle's braking and emergency systems?
sec07-card-sec07-F008.teaching_text: Electronic stability and brake-assist features vary across models, so knowing your own controls prevents panic.

sec07-card-sec07-F009.question_text: What should you do with the accelerator at the very start of a skid?
sec07-card-sec07-F009.teaching_text: Easing off throttle lets weight settle evenly so sliding tires can reconnect with pavement.

sec07-card-sec07-F010.question_text: Where should your feet and steering go during handbook skid recovery?
sec07-card-sec07-F010.teaching_text: Staying off brake and clutch while looking and steering down your target lane aligns sliding tires.

sec07-card-sec07-F011.question_text: Why isn't one single turn of the wheel always enough to finish recovering from a skid?
sec07-card-sec07-F011.teaching_text: As grip snaps back, momentum can swing the tail the opposite way unless you countersteer smoothly.

sec07-card-sec07-F012.question_text: Across which three vehicle drivetrains can skid-control techniques differ?
sec07-card-sec07-F012.teaching_text: Power delivery pulls or pushes different axles, changing how each drivetrain responds when traction slips.

sec07-card-sec07-F013.question_text: If your brake pedal drops to the floor from brake failure, how does your response differ from normal ABS braking?
sec07-card-sec07-F013.teaching_text: Unlike firm antilock stops, a dead pedal on the floor needs rapid pumping to build hydraulic pressure.

sec07-card-sec07-F014.question_text: How many brake-pedal pumps tell you whether hydraulic pressure can return during total brake failure?
sec07-card-sec07-F014.teaching_text: If pressure stays dead after three or four pumps, switch immediately to downshifting and parking brake.

sec07-card-sec07-F015.question_text: How can your transmission help slow your vehicle when foot brakes fail?
sec07-card-sec07-F015.teaching_text: Stepping down into a lower gear uses internal engine resistance to bleed speed without wheel brakes.

sec07-card-sec07-F016.question_text: How should you manage the parking brake if your primary brakes fail?
sec07-card-sec07-F016.teaching_text: Yanking the parking brake too hard locks rear wheels into a spin unless you ease off immediately.

sec07-card-sec07-F017.question_text: Why must you keep scanning for an open escape area during brake failure?
sec07-card-sec07-F017.teaching_text: Lost foot brakes rarely disable steering, letting you guide a rolling car onto an open shoulder or uphill lane.

sec07-card-sec07-F018.question_text: What are your immediate steering and pedal actions right after a tire blowout?
sec07-card-sec07-F018.teaching_text: Slamming the brakes on a shredded tire pitches weight forward and yanks your car violently sideways.

sec07-card-sec07-F019.question_text: What lights and traffic checks come next while regaining control from a tire failure?
sec07-card-sec07-F019.teaching_text: Early hazard flashers warn fast-closing drivers behind you while you scan for a clear gap to exit.

sec07-card-sec07-F020.question_text: How should you brake and position your car as you exit the road after a tire failure?
sec07-card-sec07-F020.teaching_text: Light braking once speed drops guides a crippled rim smoothly onto firm ground away from lanes.

sec07-card-sec07-F021.question_text: What gear and pedal combination cuts engine power to the wheels when an accelerator sticks?
sec07-card-sec07-F021.teaching_text: Popping the transmission into neutral disconnects surging engine torque so your brakes can slow the car.

sec07-card-sec07-F022.question_text: What must you do immediately if your accelerator sticks midway through a sharp curve or turn?
sec07-card-sec07-F022.teaching_text: Cutting drive torque instantly keeps unwanted acceleration from pushing your tires wide off the curve.

sec07-card-sec07-F023.question_text: Where should you steer while continuing to brake during a stuck-accelerator emergency?
sec07-card-sec07-F023.teaching_text: Guiding into an open roadside space gets you clear of moving traffic before bringing the car to rest.

sec07-card-sec07-F024.question_text: When should you turn off the ignition during a stuck-accelerator emergency?
sec07-card-sec07-F024.teaching_text: Shutting the key off while still rolling in traffic can lock steering or kill power brake boost.

sec07-card-sec07-F025.question_text: What can you try at the first sputter or stall of engine failure while still rolling?
sec07-card-sec07-F025.teaching_text: Most automatics crank only in neutral or park, so shifting to neutral lets you attempt a rolling restart.

sec07-card-sec07-F026.question_text: Where should you steer and what lights should you activate as soon as an engine fails?
sec07-card-sec07-F026.teaching_text: Using remaining momentum immediately prevents getting stranded powerless in a middle travel lane.

sec07-card-sec07-F027.question_text: How can losing engine power change the feel of your steering wheel?
sec07-card-sec07-F027.teaching_text: Without engine-driven assist, turning the wheel takes extra muscle even though mechanical steering still functions.

sec07-card-sec07-F028.question_text: What step is required after a stalled engine restarts in neutral before you merge back into pace?
sec07-card-sec07-F028.teaching_text: Pressing the gas while still in neutral only revs the motor without moving your car forward.

sec07-card-sec07-F029.question_text: What four steps should you take once stopped at the roadside with an engine refusing to restart?
sec07-card-sec07-F029.teaching_text: Raising your hood and running four-way flashers makes a disabled car unmistakable to passing traffic and patrols.

sec07-card-sec07-F030.question_text: How should you steer and manage speed right after your wheels drop off the pavement?
sec07-card-sec07-F030.teaching_text: Jerking back onto asphalt at high speed catches the pavement lip and slingshots your car into oncoming lanes.

sec07-card-sec07-F031.question_text: What kind of shoulder spot should you pick before steering back onto the roadway?
sec07-card-sec07-F031.teaching_text: Climbing a steep pavement drop-off catches tire sidewalls, whereas a nearly flush edge lets wheels roll up smoothly.

sec07-card-sec07-F032.question_text: What three checks and signals come right before steering from the shoulder back onto pavement?
sec07-card-sec07-F032.teaching_text: Reentering lanes without signaling and checking over your shoulder puts you straight into fast passing cars.

sec07-card-sec07-F033.question_text: What steering move keeps you in the nearest lane as your front tires climb back onto pavement?
sec07-card-sec07-F033.teaching_text: Quick countersteering stops your car from shooting across multiple lanes once front tires bite hard asphalt.

sec07-card-sec07-F034.question_text: What three finishing steps complete a safe return from the shoulder into traffic?
sec07-card-sec07-F034.teaching_text: Centering up, clicking off your blinker, and matching traffic speed prevents rear-end conflicts behind you.

sec07-card-sec07-F035.question_text: How should you brake to lessen a threatened head-on collision?
sec07-card-sec07-F035.teaching_text: Scrubbing off maximum speed while keeping tires rolling slashes crash energy and preserves steering escape control.

sec07-card-sec07-F036.question_text: Which two vehicle alerts can snap a distracted oncoming driver out of a head-on drift?
sec07-card-sec07-F036.teaching_text: Combining loud sound and bright flashes gives a drifting driver maximum chance to look up and correct.

sec07-card-sec07-F037.question_text: Which direction should you steer if an oncoming vehicle keeps drifting into your lane, and why?
sec07-card-sec07-F037.teaching_text: Dodging left puts you straight into the opposing lane right when the startled other driver swerves back home.

sec07-card-sec07-F038.question_text: How should you respond when another vehicle threatens an immediate broadside impact?
sec07-card-sec07-F038.teaching_text: Depending on timing, either hard braking or brisk acceleration paired with horn and careful steering clears the collision point.

sec07-card-sec07-F039.question_text: What audible warning should you use during a threatened side-impact conflict?
sec07-card-sec07-F039.teaching_text: A sharp horn blast can prompt a distracted cross-street or merging driver to hit their brakes.

sec07-card-sec07-F040.question_text: What must you check around your car when swerving or changing lanes to dodge a side crash?
sec07-card-sec07-F040.teaching_text: Blindly swerving away from one fender-bender can pitch you into a faster crash in the next lane.

sec07-card-sec07-F041.question_text: How can your brake lights help prevent a rear-end crash from a following vehicle?
sec07-card-sec07-F041.teaching_text: Lighting your stop lamps early wakes up tailgaters well before you need full stopping force.

sec07-card-sec07-F042.question_text: What can you do if a car closes dangerously fast from behind and space ahead is clear?
sec07-card-sec07-F042.teaching_text: Creeping or accelerating into open pavement ahead gifts the sliding driver behind you extra feet to stop.

sec07-card-sec07-F043.question_text: Which controls should you try if your headlights suddenly fail while driving at night?
sec07-card-sec07-F043.teaching_text: Toggling the dimmer, main lamp switch, or hazard and fog lights often restores enough glow to pull off safely.

sec07-card-sec07-F044.question_text: What lights must remain on once you stop off the road after a headlight failure?
sec07-card-sec07-F044.teaching_text: Without working headlights, flashing four-way hazards keep nighttime traffic from drifting into your parked car.

sec07-card-sec07-F045.question_text: What is your top priority if a train approaches while your vehicle is stalled on railroad tracks?
sec07-card-sec07-F045.teaching_text: No car is worth a life, so getting every passenger out immediately comes before everything else.

sec07-card-sec07-F046.question_text: In which direction away from the tracks should you walk after evacuating ahead of an oncoming train?
sec07-card-sec07-F046.teaching_text: Impact flings wreckage forward down the tracks, so angling away toward the oncoming locomotive dodges flying debris.

sec07-card-sec07-F047.question_text: What two roadside features warn drivers well ahead of a railroad crossing?
sec07-card-sec07-F047.teaching_text: Spotting round yellow rail signs and painted pavement crosses early prepares you to quiet the cabin and scan.

sec07-card-sec07-F048.question_text: What must you do as soon as railroad crossing lights flash red or gates start lowering?
sec07-card-sec07-F048.teaching_text: Stopping promptly and checking both directions protects against fast trains or a second hidden locomotive.

sec07-card-sec07-F049.question_text: What two actions are strictly forbidden at lowered railroad gates or ahead of an approaching train?
sec07-card-sec07-F049.teaching_text: Trains look slower than their true speed, turning gate-weaving into catastrophic collisions.

sec07-card-sec07-F050.question_text: Why must you wait patiently behind buses and hazardous-material trucks approaching railroad tracks?
sec07-card-sec07-F050.teaching_text: Expecting mandatory stops prevents rear-ending or illegally passing large vehicles halting at unguarded rails.

sec07-card-sec07-F051.question_text: How must you treat railroad tracks appearing rusty or out of service?
sec07-card-sec07-F051.teaching_text: Irregular freight or maintenance runs can use quiet spurs at any hour without advance notice.

sec07-card-sec07-F052.question_text: How far may a train travel to come to a stop after applying emergency brakes?
sec07-card-sec07-F052.teaching_text: Even if an engineer spots your car early, massive freight weight needs up to a mile and a half.

sec07-card-sec07-F053.question_text: What three immediate steps are required if smoke starts pouring from under your hood?
sec07-card-sec07-F053.teaching_text: Cutting ignition stops fuel pumps and electrical arcs while stepping clear protects everyone from sudden flare-ups.

sec07-card-sec07-F054.question_text: Whom should you call when a vehicle catches fire?
sec07-card-sec07-F054.teaching_text: Trained firefighters and police manage toxic vehicle smoke, fuel hazards, and highway lane closures safely.

sec07-card-sec07-F055.question_text: Why must you keep the hood closed if flames are visible underneath it?
sec07-card-sec07-F055.teaching_text: Popping a burning hood feeds fresh oxygen straight onto engine flames, triggering an explosive fireball.

sec07-card-sec07-F056.question_text: How far back must people stand from an out-of-control vehicle fire instead of fighting it?
sec07-card-sec07-F056.teaching_text: Burning tires, airbags, and fuel tanks can rupture violently, sending toxic shrapnel across nearby pavement.

sec07-card-sec07-F057.question_text: What two immediate steps come first if your vehicle plunges into water?
sec07-card-sec07-F057.teaching_text: Power windows short out rapidly underwater, and outside water pressure quickly pins doors shut.

sec07-card-sec07-F058.question_text: How should children's restraints be released during a vehicle water emergency?
sec07-card-sec07-F058.teaching_text: Having older kids help unbuckle younger siblings speeds cabin evacuation while seconds remain.

sec07-card-sec07-F059.question_text: May you go back to a vehicle in water to grab a phone, bag, or valuables?
sec07-card-sec07-F059.teaching_text: A floating car can roll or sink suddenly, trapping anyone reaching back inside.

sec07-card-sec07-F060.question_text: How should you adjust speed and following gap on snow-covered or icy roads?
sec07-card-sec07-F060.teaching_text: Posted speed limits apply to dry pavement only, whereas ice multiplies stopping distance dramatically.

sec07-card-sec07-F061.question_text: Why is black ice so deceptive to drivers on cold roads?
sec07-card-sec07-F061.teaching_text: Transparent glaze blends right into dark asphalt, catching fast drivers completely by surprise.

sec07-card-sec07-F062.question_text: Which four roadway locations demand special caution for hidden black ice?
sec07-card-sec07-F062.teaching_text: Cold air chills elevated bridge decks and sunless shade first while exhaust moisture freezes at busy stops.

sec07-card-sec07-F063.question_text: How should you time and apply your brakes when stopping in winter conditions?
sec07-card-sec07-F063.teaching_text: Starting gentle deceleration early keeps tires rolling instead of skidding helplessly past stop lines.

sec07-card-sec07-F064.question_text: How does winter braking technique differ between antilock brakes and conventional brakes?
sec07-card-sec07-F064.teaching_text: Matching pedal technique to your car's brake hardware prevents wheel lockup on snow and ice.

sec07-card-sec07-F065.question_text: Why can't you smell carbon monoxide leaking from a faulty exhaust system into your cabin?
sec07-card-sec07-F065.teaching_text: Because carbon monoxide has zero scent or color, rust holes or leaky pipes poison occupants silently.

sec07-card-sec07-F066.question_text: Which three physical symptoms can warn of carbon monoxide exposure inside a car?
sec07-card-sec07-F066.teaching_text: Recognizing sudden unexplained drowsiness or nausea early lets you roll windows down and get fresh air.

sec07-card-sec07-F067.question_text: What can happen if carbon monoxide poisoning goes untreated?
sec07-card-sec07-F067.teaching_text: Carbon monoxide starves blood oxygen rapidly, turning mild sleepiness into unconsciousness and death.

sec07-card-sec07-F068.question_text: What routine maintenance step lowers the risk of exhaust fumes leaking into your vehicle?
sec07-card-sec07-F068.teaching_text: Regular underbody inspections catch corroded mufflers and loose clamps before winter windows stay rolled up.

sec07-card-sec07-F069.question_text: What idling habit does the Rhode Island handbook warn against?
sec07-card-sec07-F069.teaching_text: Sitting parked with the motor running and every window sealed traps creeping exhaust fumes inside.

sec07-card-sec07-F070.question_text: How should you set cruise control when driving in rain or snow?
sec07-card-sec07-F070.teaching_text: Automated throttle can spin hydroplaning or icy drive wheels right when gentle foot lift-off is needed.

sec08-card-sec08-F001.question_text: How can a motorcyclist slow down without activating a rear brake light?
sec08-card-sec08-F001.teaching_text: Waiting for a red brake lamp behind a bike causes rear-end collisions when engine compression slows it first.

sec08-card-sec08-F002.question_text: At least how many seconds of following distance must you maintain behind a motorcycle?
sec08-card-sec08-F002.teaching_text: Four full seconds gives you stopping margin if a rider swerves or brakes hard for road debris.

sec08-card-sec08-F003.question_text: What motorcycle deceleration habit should you anticipate as you approach an intersection?
sec08-card-sec08-F003.teaching_text: Riders routinely roll off the throttle approaching corners, closing your gap before any brake bulb glows.

sec08-card-sec08-F004.question_text: Why might a motorcyclist shift position from side to side within a single travel lane?
sec08-card-sec08-F004.teaching_text: Mistaking a rider's smart lane adjustment for an invitation to squeeze alongside creates deadly sideswipes.

sec08-card-sec08-F005.question_text: How does a motorcycle's narrow profile affect your judgment of distance before turning across its path?
sec08-card-sec08-F005.teaching_text: Misjudging a fast-closing bike's narrow silhouette triggers left-turn crashes across oncoming lanes.

sec08-card-sec08-F006.question_text: Which vehicle parts and surroundings can completely hide a motorcycle from a driver's view?
sec08-card-sec08-F006.teaching_text: Because a slim bike vanishes behind a windshield pillar or mirror housing, quick glances miss riders completely.

sec08-card-sec08-F007.question_text: When should you take an extra deliberate look specifically for motorcycles?
sec08-card-sec08-F007.teaching_text: Training your eyes to search specifically for narrow silhouettes prevents cutting off riders during turns and merges.

sec08-card-sec08-F008.question_text: How should you adjust following distance behind a motorcycle on slippery pavement, and why?
sec08-card-sec08-F008.teaching_text: Two-wheeled balance makes sudden hard stops treacherous on wet or slick asphalt, requiring a bigger buffer.

sec08-card-sec08-F009.question_text: How do motorcycle stopping distances generally compare with passenger car stopping distances in similar conditions?
sec08-card-sec08-F009.teaching_text: Assuming a lighter bike stops way shorter or way longer misleads drivers about safe spacing in traffic.

sec08-card-sec08-F010.question_text: How do small convex mirrors on a motorcycle distort a following car's position?
sec08-card-sec08-F010.teaching_text: A rider glancing at curved mirrors may think your bumper has plenty of room when you are close.
sec08-card-sec08-F010.must_match_memory_hook: Convex mirrors make cars seem farther

visual_sync.text_span: Convex mirrors make cars seem farther

sec08-card-sec08-F011.question_text: Why must you never count on a motorcyclist maneuvering out of a sudden traffic conflict?
sec08-card-sec08-F011.teaching_text: High speeds and rough pavement limit abrupt lean changes, so drivers must avoid creating conflicts first.

sec08-card-sec08-F012.question_text: How does carrying a passenger change a motorcycle's handling and braking?
sec08-card-sec08-F012.teaching_text: Extra weight on the rear seat slows steering response and stretches braking distance, demanding wider driver patience.
sec08-card-sec08-F012.must_match_memory_hook: Harder balance, longer stops, less agility

visual_sync.text_span: Harder balance, longer stops, less agility

sec08-card-sec08-F013.question_text: Why can a motorcycle's illumination be hard to pick out in nighttime traffic?
sec08-card-sec08-F013.teaching_text: One lone headlight or taillight easily disappears amid dual car beams and glowing storefronts after dark.

sec08-card-sec08-F014.question_text: What visual clues help you spot a dark-clothed motorcyclist at night?
sec08-card-sec08-F014.teaching_text: Dark jackets vanish into night shadows, leaving tiny reflective strips or helmet trim as your earliest warning.

sec08-card-sec08-F015.question_text: How should you expect a motorcyclist to react to a pothole or low manhole cover?
sec08-card-sec08-F015.teaching_text: Roadway dips a four-wheeled car barely feels can jolt handlebars violently, forcing riders to weave inside their lane.

sec08-card-sec08-F016.question_text: How can you warn following road users when preparing to stop at night?
sec08-card-sec08-F016.teaching_text: Light brake taps wake up trailing riders and drivers before steady deceleration shrinks the nighttime gap.

sec08-card-sec08-F017.question_text: Why is a physical shoulder check essential before passing or changing lanes near motorcycles?
sec08-card-sec08-F017.teaching_text: Side mirrors leave blind zones where a second or third staggered rider in a group may be cruising.

sec08-card-sec08-F018.question_text: Why must you take extra seconds before passing an older-model motorcycle with a blinking turn signal?
sec08-card-sec08-F018.teaching_text: Older motorcycle blinkers do not self-cancel, so an active lamp might be forgotten rather than signaling a turn.

sec08-card-sec08-F019.question_text: What should you give a motorcyclist time to do before you begin overtaking?
sec08-card-sec08-F019.teaching_text: Surprising a rider mid-pass risks a collision if the bike shifts laterally to dodge wind or pavement cracks.

sec08-card-sec08-F020.question_text: Alongside motorcycles, which three other compact road users require similar extra care?
sec08-card-sec08-F020.teaching_text: Smaller open-air vehicles share heightened vulnerability and lower visibility inside multi-lane traffic.

sec08-card-sec08-F021.question_text: What injury protection does a properly worn motorcycle helmet provide?
sec08-card-sec08-F021.teaching_text: An unbuckled or ill-fitting shell can fly off on impact, erasing crucial brain protection in a crash.

sec08-card-sec08-F022.question_text: What does Rhode Island law require for every motorcycle passenger regarding helmets?
sec08-card-sec08-F022.teaching_text: Rhode Island mandates helmets for all rear-seat motorcycle passengers regardless of how old they are.

sec08-card-sec08-F023.question_text: Under what age must a Rhode Island motorcycle operator wear a certified helmet?
sec08-card-sec08-F023.teaching_text: Operators younger than twenty-one have zero legal exemption from wearing a certified helmet on Rhode Island roads.

sec08-card-sec08-F024.question_text: How long must newly licensed motorcycle operators wear an approved helmet regardless of age?
sec08-card-sec08-F024.teaching_text: Even adult beginners over twenty-one must wear approved head protection throughout year one of motorcycle licensing.

sec08-card-sec08-F025.question_text: Who must wear appropriate eye protection while operating a motorcycle in Rhode Island?
sec08-card-sec08-F025.teaching_text: Windblast, grit, or a single insect strike at highway speed can blind an unprotected rider instantly.

sec08-card-sec08-F026.question_text: What type of footwear helps protect a motorcyclist's feet?
sec08-card-sec08-F026.teaching_text: Sneakers or sandals shred fast against hot exhaust pipes, flying gravel, or rough asphalt in a slide.

sec08-card-sec08-F027.question_text: What clothing items help shield a motorcyclist's body from injury?
sec08-card-sec08-F027.teaching_text: Tough full-length fabric guards bare skin from severe road rash, sun exposure, and flying stones.

sec08-card-sec08-F028.question_text: What style of gloves helps prevent hand injuries on a motorcycle?
sec08-card-sec08-F028.teaching_text: Instinctively bracing a fall with bare or fingerless hands leads to severe palm and knuckle abrasion.

sec12-card-sec12-F001.question_text: What is the minimum legal age to drink alcohol in Rhode Island?
sec12-card-sec12-F001.teaching_text: Possessing, buying, or consuming alcohol before your twenty-first birthday triggers strict underage licensing and court penalties.

sec12-card-sec12-F002.question_text: How fast does alcohol reach the brain, and which two abilities does it impair first?
sec12-card-sec12-F002.teaching_text: Because judgment erodes within seconds before physical stumbling starts, tipsy drivers misjudge their own fitness early.

sec12-card-sec12-F003.question_text: How does drinking distort your perception of surrounding traffic and control of your own car?
sec12-card-sec12-F003.teaching_text: Misreading how fast cross-traffic closes while steering sloppily turns routine intersections into T-bone collisions.

sec12-card-sec12-F004.question_text: How does alcohol change your physical reflexes, sight, alertness, and personal inhibitions?
sec12-card-sec12-F004.teaching_text: Slower reflexes paired with lowered inhibitions create the classic crash combo of late braking and reckless speed.

sec12-card-sec12-F005.question_text: Which serving sizes of beer, wine, and distilled spirits contain roughly the same amount of pure alcohol?
sec12-card-sec12-F005.teaching_text: Switching from shots to twelve-ounce beers or five-ounce wine glasses delivers the same alcohol dose per serving.

sec12-card-sec12-F006.question_text: Will the exact same number of drinks always affect the same person identically every night?
sec12-card-sec12-F006.teaching_text: Sleep debt, stress, hydration, and meal timing shift how hard two drinks hit you from one day to another.

sec12-card-sec12-F007.question_text: How does drinking on an empty stomach compare with drinking after eating a meal?
sec12-card-sec12-F007.teaching_text: Without food slowing stomach emptying, alcohol rushes straight into the small intestine and spikes bloodstream concentration rapidly.

sec12-card-sec12-F008.question_text: Which two everyday conditions amplify the impairing impact of alcohol?
sec12-card-sec12-F008.teaching_text: Having even one drink while exhausted or medicated compounds central-nervous-system slowdown dramatically.

sec12-card-sec12-F009.question_text: What is the only thing that actually lowers intoxication—and why fail coffee, food, exercise, or cold air?
sec12-card-sec12-F009.teaching_text: Strong coffee only creates a wide-awake drunk driver while your liver processes alcohol at its fixed hourly pace.

sec12-card-sec12-F010.question_text: Through which three bodily processes is alcohol eliminated from your system?
sec12-card-sec12-F010.teaching_text: Your liver oxidizes the vast majority slowly while tiny traces exit through breath and sweat—which breathalyzers detect.

sec12-card-sec12-F011.question_text: How can routine cold or nerve-calming medicines compromise safe driving?
sec12-card-sec12-F011.teaching_text: Common cold tablets and anti-anxiety remedies dull alertness enough to cause lane drifting just like alcohol.

sec12-card-sec12-F012.question_text: Whom should you ask about potential driving side effects whenever starting a prescribed medication?
sec12-card-sec12-F012.teaching_text: Checking side effects with the prescriber beforehand prevents discovering blurred vision or sedation on the freeway.

sec12-card-sec12-F013.question_text: What five rebound symptoms can follow a drug that briefly boosts alertness?
sec12-card-sec12-F013.teaching_text: Artificial pep pills wear off suddenly, leaving highway drivers shaky, dizzy, unfocused, and harder-hit by exhaustion.

sec12-card-sec12-F014.question_text: Why are sedatives and tranquilizers hazardous for drivers, especially alongside alcohol?
sec12-card-sec12-F014.teaching_text: Stacking calming sedatives with alcohol multiplies central-nervous-system depression into sudden sleep behind the wheel.

sec12-card-sec12-F015.question_text: Which four driving impairments does the Rhode Island manual link to marijuana use?
sec12-card-sec12-F015.teaching_text: Delayed reactions, drifting across lane lines, and slow recovery from oncoming headlights make cannabis-impaired driving hazardous.

sec12-card-sec12-F016.question_text: How do illegal drugs like cocaine, heroin, or LSD affect your fitness to drive?
sec12-card-sec12-F016.teaching_text: Hallucinations, euphoria, or narcotic stupor destroy reality perception and physical control needed in traffic.

sec12-card-sec12-F017.question_text: How does mixing alcohol with another drug compare to simply adding their separate effects together?
sec12-card-sec12-F017.teaching_text: Drug-alcohol synergy multiplies impairment unpredictably so two mild doses hit like a severe overdose.

sec12-card-sec12-F018.question_text: What exact measurement does Blood Alcohol Concentration describe?
sec12-card-sec12-F018.teaching_text: BAC captures the exact snapshot concentration of alcohol circulating in your bloodstream at the time of testing.

sec12-card-sec12-F019.question_text: At what blood alcohol percentage is a driver of any age over Rhode Island's per-se DUI threshold?
sec12-card-sec12-F019.teaching_text: Reaching 0.08 percent BAC establishes per-se DUI regardless of age or how steady the driver claims to feel.

sec12-card-sec12-F020.question_text: Which BAC range defines underage driving while impaired for a Rhode Island driver under twenty-one?
sec12-card-sec12-F020.teaching_text: Underage drivers face driving-while-impaired charges starting at just 0.02 percent BAC—a fraction of one drink.

sec12-card-sec12-F021.question_text: Which five factors govern how high your blood alcohol concentration climbs?
sec12-card-sec12-F021.teaching_text: Because body weight, meals, sipping duration, and individual liver speed vary, nobody can safely guess BAC from drink counts.

sec12-card-sec12-F022.question_text: What chemical-testing agreement comes automatically with operating a vehicle in Rhode Island?
sec12-card-sec12-F022.teaching_text: Turning the key on Rhode Island roads legally commits you to breath or bodily-fluid chemical testing upon lawful request.

sec12-card-sec12-F023.question_text: Does refusing a chemical test shield you from penalties since no BAC number was recorded?
sec12-card-sec12-F023.teaching_text: Refusal is prosecuted as its own serious violation carrying harsh license loss and assessments without any BAC reading.

sec12-card-sec12-F024.question_text: At least how many months of license suspension does the manual highlight for refusing a chemical test?
sec12-card-sec12-F024.teaching_text: Walking away from a breathalyzer costs at least half a year of driving privileges right off the bat.

sec12-card-sec12-F025.question_text: Beyond license suspension, which five court consequences can accompany a chemical-test refusal?
sec12-card-sec12-F025.teaching_text: Refusal stacks steep state assessments, mandatory community service hours, and alcohol education or treatment onto license loss.

sec12-card-sec12-F026.question_text: What suspension, fine, and two assessments hit a driver under eighteen on a first chemical-test refusal?
sec12-card-sec12-F026.teaching_text: A minor's first refusal brings six months suspended, a $200–$500 fine, plus $500 highway and $200 testing assessments.

sec12-card-sec12-F027.question_text: How many community-service hours and what educational mandate accompany a first under-eighteen test refusal?
sec12-card-sec12-F027.teaching_text: Alongside fines and six months off the road, minor first-refusers owe ten to sixty service hours plus coursework.

sec12-card-sec12-F028.question_text: Within five years, what custody, suspension duration, and fine apply to a second under-eighteen refusal?
sec12-card-sec12-F028.teaching_text: A second juvenile refusal within five years locks out licensing until age twenty-one with up to six months custody and $600–$1,000 fines.

sec12-card-sec12-F029.question_text: What assessments, service hours, and care requirement complete the second under-eighteen refusal schedule?
sec12-card-sec12-F029.teaching_text: Repeat minor refusers still owe the $500 and $200 assessments plus sixty to one hundred service hours and treatment.

sec12-card-sec12-F030.question_text: Within five years, what custody, suspension, and fine apply to a third or later under-eighteen refusal?
sec12-card-sec12-F030.teaching_text: A third minor refusal within five years risks up to a year locked up, two to five years suspended, and $800–$1,000 fines.

sec12-card-sec12-F031.question_text: What assessments, minimum community-service hours, and treatment apply to a third under-eighteen refusal?
sec12-card-sec12-F031.teaching_text: Community service climbs to at least one hundred hours alongside mandatory treatment and the $500 and $200 assessments.

sec12-card-sec12-F032.question_text: May a driver of legal drinking age consume alcohol or drugs while actively driving?
sec12-card-sec12-F032.teaching_text: Being twenty-one never permits sipping alcohol or taking impairing substances behind the wheel at any age.

sec12-card-sec12-F033.question_text: What suspension, assessment, and program apply to a first impaired-driving violation below age eighteen?
sec12-card-sec12-F033.teaching_text: Even below 0.08 DUI, a minor's first impaired-driving violation brings 6–12 months suspended, $150 or restitution, course, and treatment.

sec12-card-sec12-F034.question_text: How long is the license suspension on a second impaired-driving violation below age eighteen?
sec12-card-sec12-F034.teaching_text: A second underage impaired violation strips driving privileges all the way to age twenty-one alongside $150 or restitution and treatment.

sec12-card-sec12-F035.question_text: How much extra suspension time hits a third or later impaired-driving violation below age eighteen?
sec12-card-sec12-F035.teaching_text: A third juvenile impaired offense tacks two additional suspension years on top alongside the $150 assessment, course, and treatment.

sec12-card-sec12-F036.question_text: What suspension, highway assessment, and service hours apply to a first DUI below age eighteen?
sec12-card-sec12-F036.teaching_text: Crossing into full DUI under eighteen raises suspension to 6–18 months with a $500 highway assessment and 10–60 service hours.

sec12-card-sec12-F037.question_text: What suspension, custody or fine, and programs hit a second or later DUI below age eighteen?
sec12-card-sec12-F037.teaching_text: Repeat juvenile DUI locks out licensing until twenty-one and exposes the offender to up to a year incarcerated or $500 fine.

sec12-card-sec12-F038.question_text: What suspension, fine, and service hours apply on the first 18-to-21 impaired-driving schedule?
sec12-card-sec12-F038.teaching_text: Young adults 18 to 21 caught impaired below 0.08 face 1–3 months suspended, a $250 fine, 30 service hours, course, and treatment.

sec12-card-sec12-F039.question_text: How do suspension, assessments, and service hours jump on a second 18-to-21 impaired violation?
sec12-card-sec12-F039.teaching_text: A second 18-to-21 impaired offense doubles service to 60 hours, adds a $300 assessment to the $250 fine, and suspends 3–6 months.

sec12-card-sec12-F040.question_text: What suspension range, fine, assessments, and service hours apply to a first adult chemical-test refusal?
sec12-card-sec12-F040.teaching_text: Adults refusing their first test lose driving privileges 6–12 months and owe a $200–$500 fine, $500+$200 assessments, and 10–60 hours.

sec12-card-sec12-F041.question_text: Within five years, what crime class, prison cap, suspension, and fine hit a second adult refusal?
sec12-card-sec12-F041.teaching_text: A second refusal within five years becomes a criminal misdemeanor carrying up to 6 months prison, 1–2 years suspended, and $600–$1,000 fines.

sec12-card-sec12-F042.question_text: Which two assessments and community-service range accompany a second adult refusal?
sec12-card-sec12-F042.teaching_text: Alongside prison exposure and fines, second adult refusers pay $500 highway and $200 testing assessments plus 60–100 service hours.

sec12-card-sec12-F043.question_text: Within five years, what prison cap, suspension range, and fine hit a third or later adult refusal?
sec12-card-sec12-F043.teaching_text: A third refusal within five years brings misdemeanor prosecution up to one year in prison, 2–5 years suspended, and $800–$1,000 fines.

sec12-card-sec12-F044.question_text: What assessments and minimum community-service hours apply to a third adult refusal?
sec12-card-sec12-F044.teaching_text: Third-time adult refusers face at least 100 community-service hours on top of the $500 highway and $200 testing assessments.

sec12-card-sec12-F045.question_text: For a first 21-plus DUI in the 0.08-to-0.10 band, what crime class, prison, suspension, and fine apply?
sec12-card-sec12-F045.teaching_text: Even the lowest adult DUI band is a misdemeanor risking up to a year in prison, 30–180 days suspended, and $100–$300 fines.

sec12-card-sec12-F046.question_text: What assessment, fee, service hours, and program accompany that lowest-band first adult DUI?
sec12-card-sec12-F046.teaching_text: Mandatory add-ons tack a $500 assessment, $86 fee, 10–60 service hours, and course or treatment onto every lowest-band DUI.

sec12-card-sec12-F047.question_text: For a first adult DUI in the 0.10–0.15 band—or unknown BAC—what prison, suspension, and fine apply?
sec12-card-sec12-F047.teaching_text: Blowing 0.10–0.15 or having an unknown BAC pushes first-offense suspension to 3–12 months and fines to $100–$400 with up to a year prison.

sec12-card-sec12-F048.question_text: What assessment, fee, service hours, and course requirement complete the middle-band first adult DUI?
sec12-card-sec12-F048.teaching_text: Just like the lower tier, middle-band offenders owe the $500 assessment, $86 fee, 10–60 service hours, and education or treatment.

sec12-card-sec12-F049.question_text: At 0.15 percent BAC or higher on a first adult DUI, what prison, suspension, fine, and service apply?
sec12-card-sec12-F049.teaching_text: Extreme 0.15-plus BAC stretches first-DUI suspension up to 18 months, locks the fine at $500, and raises minimum service to 20 hours.

sec12-card-sec12-F050.question_text: Which assessment, fee, and program also attach to a 0.15-plus first adult DUI?
sec12-card-sec12-F050.teaching_text: High-BAC first offenders still pay the $500 assessment and $86 fee on top of their $500 fine and mandatory course or treatment.

sec12-card-sec12-F051.question_text: Within five years, what prison floor, suspension, and fine hit a second 0.08–0.15 or unknown-BAC DUI?
sec12-card-sec12-F051.teaching_text: A second DUI within five years carries mandatory jail starting at ten days up to a year, 1–2 years suspended, and a $400 fine.

sec12-card-sec12-F052.question_text: How long must an ignition interlock remain installed after a second lower-band adult DUI sentence?
sec12-card-sec12-F052.teaching_text: Finishing jail and suspension on a second DUI is followed by one to two years of breath-locked driving plus $500/$86 fees and treatment.

sec12-card-sec12-F053.question_text: Within five years at 0.15 percent or higher, what prison, suspension, and fine hit a second adult DUI?
sec12-card-sec12-F053.teaching_text: Blowing 0.15-plus on a second DUI jumps minimum prison from ten days to six full months with two years suspended and a $1,000 fine.

sec12-card-sec12-F054.question_text: Within five years, what crime class, prison, suspension, and fine hit a third 0.08–0.15 or unknown DUI?
sec12-card-sec12-F054.teaching_text: A third DUI within five years crosses into felony territory carrying 1–3 prison years, 2–3 suspension years, and a $400 fine.

sec12-card-sec12-F055.question_text: What happens to the offender's vehicle and post-sentence interlock on that third lower-band adult DUI?
sec12-card-sec12-F055.teaching_text: Felony third-time offenders face outright seizure of their vehicle plus two years of post-sentence ignition interlock and treatment.

sec12-card-sec12-F056.question_text: Within five years at 0.15 percent or above, what prison, suspension, and fine hit a third adult DUI?
sec12-card-sec12-F056.teaching_text: A third high-BAC DUI brings 3–5 years in state prison, 3 post-sentence suspension years, and $1,000–$5,000 fines.

sec12-card-sec12-F057.question_text: What property penalty, assessment, fee, and care apply to a third 0.15-plus adult DUI?
sec12-card-sec12-F057.teaching_text: Alongside multi-year felony prison time, the state seizes the vehicle and imposes the $500 highway assessment, $86 fee, and treatment.

sec12-card-sec12-F058.question_text: What crime class, prison range, revocation, and fine apply when a first DUI causes serious bodily injury?
sec12-card-sec12-F058.teaching_text: Hurting someone seriously in an impaired crash is an immediate felony carrying 1–10 prison years, up to 2 years revoked, and $1,000–$5,000 fines.

sec12-card-sec12-F059.question_text: Within five years, how do prison, revocation, and fines escalate on a second injury-causing DUI?
sec12-card-sec12-F059.teaching_text: A repeat injury DUI within five years raises felony prison to 2–15 years, revocation up to 4 years, and fines to $3,000–$10,000.

sec12-card-sec12-F060.question_text: What felony prison range, license revocation, and fine apply to a first DUI causing death?
sec12-card-sec12-F060.teaching_text: Taking a life while driving impaired brings 5–15 years in prison, 5 years of license revocation, $5,000–$10,000 fines, and treatment.

sec12-card-sec12-F061.question_text: Within five years, what prison sentence, fine range, and revocation apply to a second death-causing DUI?
sec12-card-sec12-F061.teaching_text: A second fatal DUI within five years doubles prison to 10–20 years and fines to $10,000–$20,000 plus five revocation years.

sec12-card-sec12-F062.question_text: What suspension can hit an unaccompanied driver under twenty-one who knowingly carries alcohol on a highway?
sec12-card-sec12-F062.teaching_text: Unless a parent or guardian is riding along, knowingly hauling alcohol under twenty-one risks up to thirty days off the road.

sec12-card-sec12-F063.question_text: Does Rhode Island's underage alcohol-transport ban apply only to open bottles, or sealed ones too?
sec12-card-sec12-F063.teaching_text: Stashing an unopened six-pack in the trunk still violates underage transport law anywhere inside the vehicle.

sec12-card-sec12-F064.question_text: When may a driver aged sixteen to twenty-one legally carry unopened alcohol inside a vehicle?
sec12-card-sec12-F064.teaching_text: Delivery or grocery employees aged 16–21 may transport factory-sealed alcohol strictly as part of paid job duties.

sec12-card-sec12-F065.question_text: How do minimum fines step up across first, second, and later underage alcohol-possession offenses?
sec12-card-sec12-F065.teaching_text: Every tier caps at $750, while minimum fines climb from $150 first to $300 second and $450 for third or later.

sec12-card-sec12-F066.question_text: At least how many days of license suspension—and what extra penalty—accompany underage alcohol possession?
sec12-card-sec12-F066.teaching_text: Getting caught holding alcohol under twenty-one costs at least sixty days of driving privileges and possible community service.

sec12-card-sec12-F067.question_text: What clinical order may follow a second underage alcohol-possession offense?
sec12-card-sec12-F067.teaching_text: Repeat underage possession lets the court mandate a formal evaluation by a licensed substance-abuse specialist.
